### DONE (negative result, no code change) — Investigated the GlucagonPathway milestone; rejected the planned postprandial mechanism with decisive primary-source evidence from the benchmark's own trial

Follow-on to the entry directly above: with the GLP-1 fixed-point bug
fixed, this was the correctly-sequenced next step for the `GlucagonPathway`
finding from the prior session's scoping pass (a new ODE-coupled pathway
representing GLP-1's glucagonostatic suppression of EGP, hypothesised to
explain part of the semaglutide/metformin/steroid benchmark undershoots).
Per that scoping's own Phase-0 literature gate, the two missing
coefficients had to be found (or the milestone explicitly deferred/
rejected) before any pathway code was written -- neither was assumed,
guessed, or back-solved from the 1.34 mmol.h/L benchmark reference.

**Coefficient A (semaglutide's postprandial glucagon suppression
magnitude) was found -- and it falsifies the mechanism the pathway was
designed to represent.** Re-fetched **PMID:28941314 (Hjerpsted et al.
2018, the exact trial the semaglutide benchmark itself uses)** with full
text via the now-fixed Europe PMC wiring and the now-fixed abstract-
truncation parser -- neither capability existed when this paper was
first read for the benchmark, so this was a genuinely new look, not a
re-read. Its own Table 1, for the SAME standardized carbohydrate-rich
breakfast / iAUC(0-5h) window the glucose benchmark measures:

```
                    Semaglutide 1.0mg   Placebo    ETR/ETD [95% CI]        P       Rel. diff
Fasting glucagon    89.39 pg/mL         104.22     ETR 0.86 [0.75,0.98]   .0224    -14%  (significant)
Postprandial        31.29 pg.h/mL       32.94      ETD -1.65 [-24.16,     .8811    -5.0% (NOT significant)
 glucagon iAUC(0-5h)                                      20.85]
```

The paper's own text (Results 3.2.3) states this explicitly, not just
the table: **"there was no significant difference in postprandial
increments (iAUC 0-5h) for glucagon between semaglutide and placebo."**
The 95% CI for the postprandial change (-24.16 to +20.85 pg.h/mL) spans
zero by a wide margin -- this is not a small-but-real effect, it is
statistical noise around no detectable postprandial change, in the
platform's own reference population and protocol.

This directly falsifies the motivating hypothesis for a *postprandial*
GLP-1-glucagon-EGP coupling: the mechanism the pathway would have
represented (GLP-1 suppressing glucagon acutely after a meal, lowering
EGP during the measured 0-5h window) does not operate detectably in the
exact trial this platform already validates against. The FASTING
glucagon effect is real and significant (ETR 0.86, matching the earlier
scoping pass's citation of this same number) but is a chronic/basal
phenomenon, not a postprandial one -- and per this project's own
double-counting discipline, a basal effect would need its own separate
justification (analogous to metformin's static `Gb` modifier), not the
dynamic postprandial pathway that was actually scoped.

**Coefficient B (a quantitative human glucagon-to-EGP dose-response
gain) was searched for and not found**, within the scoping's own capped
two-search-pass limit: `esearch` queries for glucagon+EGP+clamp+dose-
response and glucagon+hepatic-glucose-production+somatostatin+infusion
surfaced classic pancreatic-clamp-era candidates (PMID:3544860 "Pulsatile
hyperglucagonemia fails to increase hepatic glucose production in normal
man," 1987; PMID:9101062, exercise-specific; several insulin-dose-
response papers unrelated to glucagon) -- none gives a clean, directly
usable glucagon-concentration-to-EGP-rate gain figure. Also fetched
**PMID:33722838 (Bagger et al. 2021, *Diabetes*, "Glucagonostatic
Potency of GLP-1..."**, verified live) -- a real, controlled, dose-
response clamp study confirming GLP-1 potentiates glucose-induced
glucagon suppression in a dose-dependent manner in healthy subjects and
T2D, but reports the finding qualitatively (no extractable pM-to-EGP
gain in the abstract; would need full text not attempted this pass,
and would still only speak to glucose-induced suppression under a
stepped IV glucose clamp, not this platform's oral-meal protocol).

**Decision, per the scoping's own decision table**: with the primary
target mechanism (postprandial suppression, for the platform's actual
benchmark population) shown to be statistically absent, and the
secondary mechanism (fasting/basal suppression) lacking an EGP-gain
coefficient to translate it into a modeled effect, building the pathway
now would mean shipping a mechanism this project's own reference
literature does not support, or an isolated calibration constant with no
anchor at all for a mechanism that may not even be the right shape.
**Rejected, following the same discipline as the metformin-PK and
adipose/leptin negative results** -- a documented "don't build this, and
here is the primary-source evidence why" is treated as a complete,
valuable milestone outcome, not an incomplete one. No pathway file,
signal key, or coupling was written. No existing code was touched.

**Two new findings surfaced during this investigation, neither chased
this pass, both worth a future session's attention**:

1. **A real, more precisely-located version of the "94% of the model's
   semaglutide effect comes from amplifying insulin secretion" problem
   the original scoping pass flagged.** Hjerpsted's own Table 1 shows
   *fasting* insulin significantly ELEVATED under semaglutide (166 vs.
   115 pmol/L, ETR 1.45, P=.0005) but the *postprandial increment*
   (iAUC 0-5h) significantly REDUCED (-921 pmol.h/L, -43.4%, P=.0018) --
   a real subject can have higher fasting insulin and a smaller
   postprandial rise simultaneously. The platform's `incretin_effect`
   mechanism (`GlucoseInsulinPathway.dydt()`'s `delta_secretion` term)
   has no way to represent this split; it can only push the postprandial
   increment in one direction. This is a genuine architecture/
   calibration question -- whether `incretin_effect` should instead
   modulate a fasting set point separately from the postprandial gain,
   or whether the gastric-emptying-delay signal alone (already the
   smaller of the two current mechanisms per the mass-conservation-fix
   entry's decomposition) should be doing more of the postprandial work
   -- not attempted here; flagging it precisely, with the exact
   contradicting numbers, so a future session doesn't have to
   re-derive them.
2. **The fat-rich-breakfast condition (Table 1's second half, iAUC 0-8h,
   not the platform's benchmark window) shows a much larger, borderline-
   significant glucagon effect** (-27.3%, P=.0582) than the
   carbohydrate-rich/iAUC(0-5h) condition used by the benchmark (-5.0%,
   P=.88) -- a real, meal-composition-dependent difference in this
   trial's own data. Not investigated further (this platform's meal
   model has no fat/mixed-macronutrient representation to test it
   against), but worth knowing this isn't a single, generalizable
   number even within one trial.

Full suite unchanged: 1561 passed, 2 skipped (no source files modified
this entry).

### DONE — Fixed `ParameterStore.get_all_for_subject()`'s cross-scope data loss and two timestamp round-trip bugs (Track 3)

Executed the plan the `database-architect` scoping pass had already
precisely diagnosed: `get_all_for_subject()` indexed its result by kind
string with a plain assignment (`result[kind_str] = sorted(params, ...)`)
inside a loop over ALL 4-tuple `(subject, kind, object, reaction)` index
keys for a subject -- when one subject+kind spanned multiple object/
reaction scopes, only the LAST scope visited survived. Reproduced
directly (3 stored Kd parameters for one subject, 1 returned). Zero
production callers exist today (grepped the whole repo; only the
method's own pre-existing test called it), but this blocked Track 3's
own migration-equivalence gate: `infra/postgres/002_query_api.sql`'s
`parameter_all_for_subject()` never had this bug, so a shadow-read
comparator would have needed a permanent special case for it.

**Fixed**: `get_all_for_subject()` now accumulates across scopes
(`result.setdefault(kind_str, []).extend(...)`), sorted once per kind
with an explicit ascending insertion-sequence tiebreak -- a new
monotonic counter (`self._insertion_seq`/`self._next_seq`), assigned in
both `add()` and `load()`, deliberately mirroring Postgres's
`parameter.seq GENERATED ALWAYS AS IDENTITY` so the Python and SQL
tiebreakers are the same concept, not two things that happen to agree.

**A subtlety in the fix's own design was caught by the mandatory
code-reviewer pass, verified myself, and corrected before this was
considered done.** The first version's comment claimed the naive
alternative fix (`sorted(key=self._priority_score, reverse=True)`,
with no explicit seq) would fail because "`reverse=True` reverses the
tiebreak too" -- independently verified this is factually wrong
(`sorted([...], key=..., reverse=True)` is stable and preserves ties'
original relative order, confirmed by direct execution, not just
argued). The real reason an explicit tiebreak is needed is upstream of
the sort entirely: the accumulation loop groups by which SCOPE KEY was
first created in `_subject_kind_index`, not true global insertion
order -- interleaved insertion into different scopes (scope A, then
scope B, then scope A again) puts both A entries ahead of B's even
though B was added in between, confirmed by running the naive and real
implementations side by side against identical input
(`[a1, a2, b]` naive vs. `[a1, b, a2]` correct). The corresponding
regression test's own scenario was also wrong for the same reason (it
used three DIFFERENT scopes with no interleaving, which the naive fix
actually passes) -- rewritten to the genuinely discriminating
interleaved-scope case, and the misleading `reverse=True` explanation
corrected in `store.py`'s inline comment, `infra/MIGRATION_PLAN.md`'s
resolution of open question 5, and this entry.

**A second, independent bug found and fixed in the same pass**:
`_deserialize_parameter()` never passed `Parameter.created_at` or
`Provenance.extracted_at` through to their constructors on `load()`, so
both were silently regenerated via `default_factory=
datetime.now(timezone.utc)` on every save/load round trip -- reproduced
directly. This mattered specifically for Track 3: `parameter.created_at`
is `timestamptz NOT NULL` in the append-only, trigger-protected
`001_schema.sql` schema, so a migration backfill reading via
`ParameterStore.load()` would have permanently stamped every row with
the migration's wall-clock time instead of the parameter's real
creation time -- unfixable afterward without deliberately disabling the
append-only guard triggers. Fixed with a graceful `.get()`-based round
trip (`datetime.fromisoformat`, falling back to the default for pre-fix
snapshots that never wrote the field), matching `IDRegistry
.from_dict()`'s existing degradation convention.

**Two more follow-up fixes, both surfaced by the mandatory
security-reviewer pass and implemented in the same pass rather than
deferred**: (1) `seq` was being re-derived purely from the parameters
JSON array's order on `load()`, not persisted -- correct as long as the
array is never reordered, but silently wrong with no error the moment
it is (a hand-edited snapshot, a merge of two partial exports). Now
persisted explicitly in `_serialize_parameter()`, read back via the same
`.get()`-fallback pattern. (2) `ConflictRecord.detected_at` had the
identical default_factory-regenerated-on-load gap as `created_at`/
`extracted_at` -- `load()`'s conflict reconstruction only ever
overwrote `conflict_id`/`resolved`/`resolution_notes` from the JSON,
never `detected_at`. Fixed the same way.

Also updated `infra/postgres/002_query_api.sql`'s `parameter_all_for_
subject()` comment from "deliberate, documented divergence" to
RESOLVED (the shape contract a shadow-read adapter must honour: group
by kind, preserve row order, never re-sort client-side), and
`infra/MIGRATION_PLAN.md`'s Step 3 (removed the special-case bullet --
the comparator now has zero sanctioned divergences), Step 2 (fixed a
stale `ParameterStore.to_dict()` reference -- the store has `save()`/
`load()` only; `to_dict()`/`from_dict()` are `IDRegistry`'s API, added
a backfill insertion-order invariant note tying into `seq`), Step 5,
and replaced five stale hardcoded "1551 tests"/"5 clinical benchmarks"
references throughout the document with "the full test suite"/"all
clinical validation benchmarks" -- this is a multi-session repo and
those counts had already drifted (6 benchmarks registered today, not
5) by the time this fix landed.

+9 tests in `test_parameter_db.py`
(`TestObjectScopedParameters::test_get_all_for_subject_returns_every_
scope_not_just_the_last`, `..._ties_break_by_global_insertion_order`,
`..._orders_by_confidence_then_organism_then_system`, `..._include_
superseded_filters_across_scopes`, `..._groups_by_kind_across_scopes`;
`TestPersistence::test_created_at_survives_save_load_round_trip`,
`::test_extracted_at_survives_save_load_round_trip`,
`::test_insertion_seq_persists_and_survives_reload`,
`::test_conflict_detected_at_survives_save_load_round_trip`).
RED-proofed all 7 timestamp/scope tests directly against the pre-fix
code (confirmed each fails for the documented reason); the 2 follow-up
tests (seq persistence, conflict timestamp) were added alongside their
own fixes in the same review cycle. Full suite: 1561 -> 1568 passed
(this activity's own delta), 2 skipped.

**Review**: code-reviewer and security-reviewer passes both ran
successfully. Security-reviewer: APPROVE, traced the full save/load/
deserialize path for corruption risk (none found), confirmed zero
production callers, confirmed the insertion-sequence counter cannot
desync between `add()`/`load()` (both always write under `self._lock`),
and surfaced the two follow-up fixes above. Code-reviewer: APPROVE with
a note -- independently verified the sort-key math against the SQL's
`ORDER BY` clause (correct), independently verified no other caller
depends on old behavior, and caught the `reverse=True` comment/test
inaccuracy detailed above, which was corrected before considering this
done rather than left as a known cosmetic issue.

### DONE — Fixed `biosim_uncertainty`'s composite-pathway blindness: UQ/sensitivity analysis always saw a bare GlucoseInsulinPathway, never the point estimate's actual composed pathway

Executed the `architect` scoping pass's finding (re-verified directly
against current source before implementing, not trusted at face value):
`MonteCarloEngine.propagate()`, `OATSensitivityAnalyzer`, and
`SobolSensitivityAnalyzer` all hardcoded a bare `GlucoseInsulinPathway`
internally, with no way to supply the same `CompositePathway` (GLP1,
renal/SGLT2i, cortisol, hepatic, exercise, meal-absorption extensions)
`SimulationRunner._build_pathway()` composes for the point estimate.

**Verified this was a real, provable defect, not merely a theoretical
gap**: GLP-1 and SGLT2i drugs both have ZERO static `PathwayParameters`
effect (`_glp1_agonist_modifiers()`/`_sglt2_inhibitor_modifiers()` both
return `{}` -- the ODE pathway is their sole representation, by design).
For a semaglutide scenario with `run_uncertainty=True`, this meant the
sampled `PathwayParameters` ensemble -- and therefore the reported
confidence band -- was byte-for-byte identical to a drug-free ensemble's,
even though the point estimate itself correctly ran through the composed
GLP1 pathway. Confirmed via a new regression test constructing exactly
this scenario and RED-proofing it against the pre-fix `runner.py` (the
band contained only the bare-GI 6 species; `"GLP1" not in output.uq.bands`).

**One correction to the prior scoping pass, verified before trusting
it**: that pass's list of affected call sites included
`validator.py:334`/`:410` (`posterior_predictive_check_bergman_iv()`/
`validate_bergman_iv()`). Re-checked directly: both are the healthy-
subject Bergman 1981 IV glucose tolerance test -- no drug, no disease,
no stress, zero extension pathways activated -- so a bare-GI prior is
CORRECT there, not a defect. Treating them as bugs would have been a
false positive; excluded from the fix's scope.

**Fix**: added an optional `pathway_factory: Optional[Callable[
[PathwayParameters, list[MealInput]], BasePathway]] = None` parameter to
`propagate()`, `OATSensitivityAnalyzer.__init__()`,
`SobolSensitivityAnalyzer.__init__()`, and `BayesianCalibrator.calibrate()`
(forwarded unchanged to `engine.propagate()`). Defaults to `None`, which
reproduces the EXACT prior expression bit-for-bit -- every existing
caller (`calibrate_ogtt()`, both Bergman-IV methods, every pre-existing
test) is completely unaffected, verified via `np.array_equal` against a
fixed-seed baseline. `SimulationRunner.run()`'s UQ block now passes
`lambda p, m: self._build_pathway(scenario, GlucoseInsulinPathway(
params=p, meals=m))` -- reusing the exact same composition logic as the
point estimate two lines above it, so the UQ ensemble sees precisely
what was actually simulated, for every scenario, at zero behaviour
change for any scenario with no active extension (`_build_pathway()`
returns the bare pathway unchanged in that case).

`(params, meals)` is the minimum sufficient factory signature: every
extension pathway in `_build_pathway()` is constructed from the scenario
alone, never from `PathwayParameters`, so only the GI pathway needs the
sampled params; `meals` must be a factory ARGUMENT (not closed over),
because `MealAbsorptionPathway` derives its own `y0` from
`meals[i].D_eff_mM` and implements no `with_meals()` -- a factory closing
over stale meals could silently produce wrong absorption initial
conditions if meals ever differed from what's passed in (they don't
today, but the contract shouldn't rely on that).

**A defensive check added alongside the fix**: `propagate()` now
validates that each successful sample's `result.species` key set matches
the first successful sample's, raising a clear `ValueError` naming the
cause (not a bare `KeyError` deep in the trajectory-storing loop) if a
caller-supplied factory non-deterministically varies pathway structure
across samples. Verified this can't false-positive for any legitimate
usage: pathway structure depends only on `scenario` (fixed for the whole
`propagate()` call) and `_build_pathway()`/every `_detect_*()` helper is
a pure function of `(scenario, gi_pathway)` with no cached/shared
mutable state -- confirmed by reading every `_detect_glp1()`/
`_detect_renal()`/`_detect_cortisol()`/`_detect_hepatic()` implementation
directly (each constructs a fresh pathway instance per call; `scenario`
is only ever read, never mutated).

**A separate, independently real defect in `ConfidenceBand
.mean_relative_width()` fixed in the same pass**: `relative_width`'s own
`median != 0` guard only special-cases EXACT zero -- a median merely
passing NEAR zero (the `X` remote-insulin species, exactly 0 at t=0 and
decaying back toward ~0) produces an enormous relative width from an
ordinary-sized numerator over a tiny denominator, which dominated the
mean and made `most_uncertain_species()` answer "X" for ordinary
scenarios -- a bookkeeping artifact, not a genuine uncertainty signal.
Confirmed numerically before fixing: `X` measured ~0.25 mean relative
width vs. ~0.03-0.08 for physiologically real species on a real
scenario. Fixed with a per-band, peak-relative significance floor
(default 5% of the band's own peak `|median|`, an engineering choice in
the same category as `MIN_GB_THRESHOLD_MARGIN_MM` -- not a literature-
derived statistic) excluding near-zero-median time points before
averaging. `most_uncertain_species()` also gained an optional
`candidates` filter parameter (defaults to every band, unchanged prior
behaviour) so a caller can scope the comparison to a known species set.

**Review, disclosed honestly**: both the mandatory code-reviewer and
security-reviewer passes hit a session-quota outage mid-verification
("resets 12:40pm Europe/London") -- the code-reviewer had confirmed
points (1) through (5) of its own checklist and was mid-way through
verifying `calibrate_ogtt()`'s deliberate non-use of `pathway_factory`
when it was cut off; the security-reviewer had confirmed the fix's
blast radius and was about to re-run `validate_all()` for an exact
before/after comparison. Per this project's standing rule, did not
retry identically -- completed both agents' exact unfinished checks
myself: (1) confirmed `calibrate_ogtt()`'s call to `calibrator.calibrate()`
does not pass `pathway_factory` (matches its own docstring: works "at
the bare ODE-engine level," a healthy OGTT with zero active extensions),
(2) re-ran `ModelValidator().validate_all()` and confirmed every one of
the 6 registered benchmarks' exact reported values (deviations, verdicts)
are byte-for-byte identical to their pre-fix values already on record in
this file, (3) independently traced the closure/shared-mutable-state
question the security-reviewer was heading toward (detailed above,
confirmed safe).

+9 tests: `TestMonteCarloPathwayFactory` (5, `test_uncertainty.py`),
2 `ConfidenceBand` floor tests, 1 each for `OATSensitivityAnalyzer`/

### DONE (partial, docs/hygiene only) — Resolved Track 3 open question 7, added the backfill seq invariant, and fixed four operational hygiene gaps in `infra/`

**Open question 7 (who runs the backfill, and when, under this
project's own documented concurrent-session git activity) -- RESOLVED**:
adopted an explicit operational rule rather than an implicit assumption
-- the backfill only ever reads a file PATH to a JSON snapshot (never a
live in-process store object, matching `migration_audit.source_snapshot`'s
own already-documented contract), copies it to a read-only temp location
before reading (so a concurrent session's `save()` mid-backfill can't
produce a torn read), never writes back to the file-based store (already
true), and the operator picks a quiet moment procedurally (checking
`git status` on the snapshot file first) rather than this project
building automated file-locking for a single-operator repo.

**A second, related invariant surfaced while resolving Q7, not
previously named**: the backfill must insert parameter rows in EXACT
snapshot array order, single-threaded. `parameter.seq` is `bigint
GENERATED ALWAYS AS IDENTITY` (Postgres assigns it at INSERT time,
cannot be supplied directly without `OVERRIDING SYSTEM VALUE`), and
`parameter_best()`'s SQL and `ParameterStore.get_all_for_subject()`'s
Python (the fix two entries above) both now tiebreak on
`seq ASC`/`self._insertion_seq` specifically because they're meant to
represent the identical concept -- an out-of-order backfill would
silently diverge the two stores' tie order for any subject+kind with
genuinely tied parameters, and `ON CONFLICT (parameter_id) DO NOTHING`
provides zero protection against it (idempotency guards re-insertion of
the same row, not insertion order across separate runs). Documented as
an explicit backfill contract requirement plus a post-backfill
verification query (snapshot array index order must equal `seq` order
for every row) to run before considering any backfill complete.

### DONE (scoping, no code change) — First real Track 4 scoping pass (genome-scale metabolism / hybrid ODE-FBA): the naive design is wrong, the track's own framing needs correcting, and there's a small, real, zero-dependency first step if it's ever picked up

With Track 1 and Track 2 exhausted and Track 3's named milestones done
or explicitly resolved, ran the roadmap's own prescribed "dedicated
architecture-planning initiative" for Track 4 -- dispatched `architect`
(software/coupling architecture) and `computational-biologist`
(scientific value and literature precedent) in parallel, per the
roadmap's own suggestion. Both independently converged on the same
verdict from different directions, which is itself a strong signal.

**The naive reading of the roadmap line -- FBA as a normal extension
pathway through `CouplingSpec` -- is not merely inefficient, it is
architecturally wrong**, for five independent, code-grounded reasons:

1. `CompositePathway.dydt()` computes every pathway's `output_signals()`
   from its own state slice BEFORE any signal injection (verified
   directly in `coupling.py`) -- an FBA pathway needing current glucose/
   insulin (which it does) would be forced to solve the LP inside
   `dydt()` itself, following `RenalPathway`'s pattern, which is exactly
   what the next point rules out.
2. An LP solution is piecewise-linear with discontinuous basis changes --
   `ODESystem.simulate()`'s Radau solver (implicit, finite-difference
   Jacobians, Newton iterations) requires a smooth vector field. A
   non-smooth `dydt()` doesn't raise an exception; it silently produces
   wrong answers with `sol.success == True`, undermining exactly the
   fixed-point discipline (KNOWN BUGS FIXED #10-#14, `validate_y0
   (tolerance=1e-8)`, 600-minute drift tests) this codebase is built on.
3. FBA optima are frequently non-unique (alternate optimal flux vectors
   for the same objective value) -- in direct tension with this
   project's `validate_y0`/basal-invariance/`ReproducibilityBundle`
   determinism guarantees.
4. **Performance, quantified**: this platform's own measured timings
   (16 scenarios/0.259s, 100-individual cohort/2.222s -- both already on
   record) put a single simulation at ~20ms; an LP inside `dydt()` at
   an estimated 500-3,000 solver evaluations would be a 100x-7,500x
   slowdown, made catastrophically worse by `MonteCarloEngine`/
   `SobolSensitivityAnalyzer`'s N(k+2)-evaluation multiplier and
   `PopulationRunner` cohorts. This is a hard design constraint, not a
   tuning problem.
5. `BatchRunner`/`PopulationRunner`'s `ProcessPoolExecutor` workers
   pickle `ScenarioDefinition`/`SimulationOutput` across a Windows spawn
   boundary -- a live solver handle is not reliably picklable, and
   `SimulationCache._key()` would need every FBA configuration knob
   folded into `to_dict()` or silently collide (the exact bug class
   already fixed once for personalisation/meal-GI/drug-timing).

**Independent, empirical confirmation of point 2 from the actual
published literature, not just architectural reasoning**: the one real
open-access hybrid ODE/FBA glucose-insulin model found and read in full
(Ben Guebila & Thiele, bioRxiv 10.1101/859876, the preprint of PMID:38217214,
*Nat Comput Sci* 2021 -- paywalled, preprint read directly) states in
its own methods that its bidirectional ("direct") coupling mode produced
"nonsmooth profiles with nonbiological concentrations," required
pFBA+MOMA regularization plus halving the integration time step to
recover physiological curves, and still permanently failed on 2 of 31
simulated cases. Its working ("indirect") coupling mode instead computes
glucose *entirely* from the ODE layer and only interprets the result
through FBA afterward -- direct textual confirmation that **FBA cannot
improve any of Biosim's own 7 registered concentration/timing benchmark
points**, because in the one place this has actually been tried, it
didn't improve the analogous glucose curve either.

**Measured cost comparison, not estimated**: `PlatformSession().simulate
("ogtt_75g")` timed at 0.035s on this platform; the same published
hybrid reports "a model could typically run for 2-3 days for simulations
representing a 10-hour time window" using CPLEX (commercial, explicitly
excluded by roadmap decision 2's free/local-only constraint). A ~10^7x
gap, against a platform whose entire statistical layer (Monte Carlo,
Sobol, population cohorts) assumes simulations are effectively free.

**Two premises in the roadmap's own framing need correcting, not just
executing**:
- FBA would NOT deepen this platform's mTOR/AMPK representation. Verified
  directly: `mTOR`/`AMPK` in `pathway.py` are pure Hill functions of
  insulin alone, feeding nothing back (already-honestly-documented, per
  `report.py`/`risk_score.py`'s existing "may reflect blunted insulin
  secretion, not genuine balance" caveats) -- and a genome-scale metabolic
  reconstruction contains NO signal-transduction reactions at all (no
  mTORC1, no AMPK, no insulin receptor). FBA yields fluxes, not
  concentrations, so it cannot supply the AMP:ATP ratio AMPK actually
  senses either -- confirmed the published hybrid needed to invent
  organ-specific demand reactions just to approximate an ATP time course,
  and even then explicitly could not report metabolite concentrations
  ("Naturally, we cannot predict the concentrations of the metabolites
  that were in steady-state").
- A biomass objective function (named explicitly in the original
  scoping prompt) is biologically inappropriate for this platform's
  postprandial-hours timescale -- biomass/growth is the standard FBA
  objective because most GEM work targets proliferating microbes/cancer
  lines; hepatocytes/myocytes/adipocytes in a 2-5h window are
  post-mitotic. Flux Variability Analysis (feasible-range bounds,
  objective-free or near so) is architecturally and scientifically the
  right first framing, not a point-estimate objective choice -- and its
  interval output maps naturally onto this platform's own existing
  confidence-band/tolerance-tier machinery rather than requiring a new,
  unanchored calibration assumption.

**A real, verified precedent base exists (15 papers fetched live via
PubMedFetcher/NCBI this session, not asserted from memory)** -- Ben
Guebila & Thiele 2021 (PMID:38217214, T1D whole-body dFBA), Krauss et al.
2012 (PMID:23133351, hepatocyte GEM in a PBPK model), Wadehn et al. 2016
(PMID:28268592, multi-tissue GEM + gene-knockout simulation), Zhu et al.
2021 (PMID:34351898, ALDH2 x disulfiram PBPK-WBM), Maldonado et al. 2018
(PMID:30131870, glucose-vs-fructose kinetics, validated in vitro), Nogiec
et al. 2015 (PMID:25737951, muscle FBA identifying a dual-knockdown
mechanism for insulin-resistant inflexibility, experimentally validated),
Thiele et al. 2020 (PMID:32463598, sex-specific whole-body models, IEM
biomarker prediction) -- all real, all framed around FLUX distributions,
biomarkers, and target discovery, never around predicting a postprandial
glucose CURVE the way Biosim's own benchmarks require. Negative
zero-hit PubMed searches for "genome-scale metabolic + oral glucose,"
"whole-body metabolic model + T2D/metformin," "FBA + glucose tolerance/
OGTT" were run and are reported honestly as UNDER-RECALL, not proof of
absence (the search missed Ben Guebila's own paper, which doesn't use
those exact terms despite simulating an OGTT) -- a real methodological
caveat, not a confident negative claim.

**A structural finding tying back to today's earlier Glucagon
investigation, independently surfaced**: every real published hybrid
builds its FBA layer on a bihormonal glucose-insulin-GLUCAGON ODE core
(Schaller et al. 2013, PMID:23945606, verified) -- Biosim has no glucagon
state at all (see the negative-result entry earlier in this file).
Pursuing Track 4 now would bolt a genome-scale network onto an ODE core
strictly less complete, in the ODE paradigm's own terms, than every real
precedent's own core -- an independent argument (from the biological
side) for the same track-ordering conclusion the roadmap's Track 1-4
sequencing already encodes.

**Recommended reframing, a documentation change for a future session to
adopt, not a decision made unilaterally here**: rename the track from
its solver ("hybrid ODE/FBA") to its biology ("substrate/tissue-resolved
metabolism"), with genome-scale FBA as one *candidate implementation*
among several, not the track's definition; add explicit entry criteria
(a named biological question the ODE paradigm structurally cannot
answer, whose answer is concentration-INDEPENDENT since FBA cannot
produce concentrations; a flux/partition-type validation target, not a
concentration curve; a compute budget compatible with the existing test
suite and roadmap decision 2). **The named, load-bearing blocker for
ever validating any FBA work on this platform**: all 7 of Biosim's own
registered benchmark points are concentration/timing measures -- there
is currently no flux-type benchmark (a tracer study, indirect
calorimetry RQ, or ¹³C-MRS glycogen measurement) to validate an FBA
layer against at all, and this project does not ship unvalidated
mechanisms.

**A small, real, genuinely first-step-sized milestone was identified,
IF this track is ever picked up (not started this pass)**: a hand-
curated core stoichiometric model (~20-60 reactions, hepatic central
carbon metabolism -- glycolysis/gluconeogenesis/glycogen/TCA/oxphos,
every reaction individually citable, no genome-scale download, no
licence question) solved with `scipy.optimize.linprog`'s HiGHS backend
(already installed, zero new dependency, zero new licence, zero Python-
3.14/Windows wheel risk -- unlike COBRApy/libsbml/GLPK, all of which
would be genuinely new, heavier dependencies), used entirely OFFLINE
(no runtime coupling, no new `CouplingSpec`, no change to `dydt()`) via
Flux Variability Analysis to put a defensible stoichiometric bound on
`hepatic.py`'s currently-uncited `EGP_MAX_MM_MIN = 0.080` constant --
which four separate hepatic preset derivations (`_solve_egp_suppression_ic50()`)
already depend on. Explicit decision gates that would produce a
documented negative result rather than a workaround (matching this
project's own strong precedent: metformin-PK, adipose/leptin, and
today's Glucagon rejection): if the derived bound is vacuously wide, if
the mmol.gDW^-1.h^-1-to-mM/min unit conversion needs more than two
documented approximations to be believable, or if HiGHS can't solve the
model reliably.

**Two small, unrelated housekeeping gaps surfaced while scoping, flagged

### DONE — First-phase insulin secretion is now literature-gated on fasting glucose level, not scaled identically to second-phase by T2D's flat `secretion_scale` (Track 1)

After the 6-activity plan above completed, ran the standing multi-agent
selection process again (computational-biologist, database-architect,
architect, general-purpose in parallel) to find the next milestone.
Track 1 had been treated as exhausted for several sessions -- this
pass's `computational-biologist` check found it genuinely was NOT: a
real, well-evidenced, previously-unconsidered gap (not a re-hash of
glucagon/metformin-PK/adipose-leptin, all already rejected). Per the
standing track-order rule, this took priority over three other real
findings the same fan-out surfaced in Track 3 (documented below, not
yet acted on).

**The gap, verified directly before implementing**: `PathwayParameters
.first_phase_gain` (`pathway.py:128`, default 121.3) is the model's only
representation of first-phase/acute insulin secretion (`first_phase_
secretion = first_phase_gain * max(dG, 0.0) * secretion_scale_eff`,
Mari et al. 2002, PMID:12388151). It was a bare constant with NO
consumer that could ever change it -- confirmed via repo-wide grep,
absent from `_PARAM_BOUNDS`, absent from every disease/drug/genetic
modifier. T2D's disease preset (`secretion_scale=0.60`) scaled first-
and second-phase secretion identically via the same shared factor,
despite real primary literature (**Brunzell JD, Robertson RP, Lerner
RL, Hazzard WR, Ensinck JW, Bierman EL, Porte D. "Relationships between
fasting plasma glucose levels and insulin secretion during intravenous
glucose tolerance tests." J Clin Endocrinol Metab. 1976;42(2):222-9.
PMID:1262429** -- independently re-fetched and verified live this
session, not trusted from the scoping agent's report) stating directly:
"The acute insulin response was present in subjects with fasting
glucose levels below 115 mg/dl but was absent above this level." 115
mg/dL converts to ~6.39 mM using the same divisor (18.0) this codebase's
own ADA fasting-glucose thresholds already use (`report.py`'s
`_FASTING_NORMAL_MM=5.6`, `_FASTING_DIABETIC_MM=7.0`, both `X/18.0`).
The T2D preset's own `Gb` (5.0 x 1.30 = 6.5 mM) sits ABOVE that
threshold, yet retained 55-60% of first-phase gain before this fix.
Corroborating citations, also independently re-fetched live: **Porte D,
Pupo AA. "Insulin responses to glucose: evidence for a two pool system
in man." J Clin Invest. 1969;48(12):2309-19. PMID:5355342** (normal
subjects, rapid IV glucose: acute insulin response peaks 3-5 min then
returns to baseline -- confirms first-phase is a genuinely fast,
transient phenomenon, not just "more secretion").

**Verified the term was mathematically dead in the platform's own IVGTT
benchmark protocol, independently, before committing to any fix** (this
was a `computational-biologist` finding, re-derived myself rather than
trusted): `validate_bergman_iv()` applies the IV bolus as an elevated
initial condition with `meals=[]`, so glucose only ever *falls*
post-bolus -- `max(dG,0)=0` throughout, for any `first_phase_gain`
value. Confirms the term's real, intended effect is confined to the
oral-meal, T2D-preset case this fix actually targets.

**Fix**: in `PhysiologicalPersonalizer.personalize()`, after the
existing joint Gb/G_threshold safety clamp, added a gate on the FINAL
effective `Gb` (post-composition, post-clamp) -- not on disease-state
identity -- setting `first_phase_gain = 0.0` whenever `Gb >= 115.0/18.0`
(~6.39 mM). Gating on glucose LEVEL rather than "is T2D present"
directly implements Brunzell's own finding and generalises correctly:
`INSULIN_RESISTANT`'s own `Gb` factor (x1.03 -> 5.15 mM) stays well below
the threshold and is correctly untouched, matching Brunzell's own
"present below 115 mg/dl" -- confirmed this is not a hardcoded disease-
state special case by checking every other Gb-touching modifier
(BMI tiers, hypothyroidism [doesn't touch Gb], the one drug modifier
that raises Gb [glucocorticoid, already excluded from this path for
drug-event scenarios by an earlier fix], exercise [only lowers Gb]) --
no plausible stacking of non-T2D modifiers crosses the threshold.
Set to exactly `0.0`, not an invented intermediate fraction -- Brunzell's
own finding is binary ("absent"), and picking a percentage with no
anchor would repeat the unsupported-placeholder pattern this project
rejects elsewhere (`KG_secretion~200`, joint-fit `p1~0.008`).

**Fixed-point safety, verified both algebraically and by direct
`validate_y0()` execution**: `first_phase_secretion` is exactly zero at
ANY basal steady state (`dG=0` there, by construction) for any
`first_phase_gain` value -- this cannot perturb the analytic fixed point
regardless of which profile triggers the gate. No new fixed-point
calibration risk of the KNOWN BUGS #10-#14 class.

**Measured impact via the real production path (`SimulationRunner`,
not bare ODE), before and after, via a scoped `git stash`** -- a T2D-
personalized 75g meal scenario: insulin peak dropped from **262.9 pM @
12.0 min to 111.2 pM @ 42.1 min** (matches Porte 1969's own finding that
removing an artificial early spike delays the observed peak, not just
shrinks it); glucose peak barely moved (12.13 -> 12.30 mM, +1.4%) --
confirming the computational-biologist's own prediction that this fix
is primarily a *timing* correction, not a glucose-magnitude one.

**Benchmark impact, checked honestly across all 6 registered datasets,
not just asserted**: `OGTT_75g_healthy`, `Bergman_IV_glucose`,
`Semaglutide_1mg_postprandial`, and `Canagliflozin_300mg_postprandial`
are byte-identical (none activate a Gb->threshold-crossing personali-
sation path). `Prednisone_40mg_T2D_postprandial` barely moved (model
8.36% -> 8.27% vs. ref 19.0%, deviation -56.0% -> -56.5%, negligible).
`Metformin_T2D_postprandial` **improved substantially**: model 4.45 ->
**24.3** mmol.min/L vs. ref 186.0, deviation -97.6% -> **-86.9%** -- a
genuine, unforced improvement (this fix touches no metformin-specific
code at all), not something tuned to happen. All WIDE-tier, none affect
verdicts (unchanged: all 6 still PASS).

**Honest open question, not resolved this pass, flagged explicitly by
the scoping agent and independently confirmed as genuinely
unanswerable with current infrastructure**: whether the resulting T2D
postprandial insulin AMPLITUDE (111.2 pM peak, down from 262.9) is
*more* or *less* realistic than before -- real early-T2D patients are
often postprandially hyperinsulinaemic (compensatory second-phase
hypersecretion), which this fix does not represent, and there is
currently NO benchmark scoring T2D insulin amplitude at all (only
healthy-OGTT `peak_insulin`/`time_to_peak_insulin_min` and
canagliflozin's `insulin_auc_2h_percent_reduction` are scored anywhere
in the suite). This fix is anchored and defensible on TIMING grounds
(Brunzell's AIR-presence/absence threshold) independent of that open
amplitude question, and is disclosed as such rather than silently
assumed to be a net improvement in every respect.

+4 tests in `test_physiology.py`
(`test_first_phase_gain_abolished_above_brunzell_threshold`,
`test_first_phase_gain_preserved_below_brunzell_threshold`,

- **`ParameterStore.query()`/`.best()` have the SAME tie-order bug this

### DONE — SGLT2i renal pathway now uses each drug's own cited T2D-cohort TmG, not always the healthy value (Track 1, MASTER_PLAN 1.8)

Picked via the standing autonomous-loop process (`AUTONOMOUS_LOOP_PROMPT.md`):
`docker info` still fails ("Docker Desktop is unable to start"), so Track
3's Docker-gated chunks stayed blocked; Track 1's `MASTER_PLAN.md` row 1.8
was the smallest, already-well-scoped open Track 1 candidate (citations
already recorded in this file's own history, no fresh literature search
needed) -- `for_dapagliflozin()`/`for_empagliflozin()` had always used
their cited papers' HEALTHY-subject baseline TmG (maximal renal glucose
reabsorption capacity) regardless of the simulated patient's actual
disease state, even though both papers directly measure and report a
separately elevated T2D-cohort TmG that was never adopted.

**Both citations re-fetched and re-verified live this session** (full
text for DeFronzo via the Europe PMC wiring; abstract-only for Al-Jobori,
no open-access full text exists for it) rather than trusted from an
earlier session's note:
- **DeFronzo RA et al. 2013, *Diabetes Care* 36(10):3169-76,
  PMID:23735727** -- full text confirms verbatim: "the calculated
  baseline TmG in diabetic subjects was 32% higher... than in healthy
  subjects (420 vs. 317 mg/min, excluding outlier; P < 0.001)." Also
  confirmed GFR "similar" (127+/-34 T2D vs. 128+/-36 healthy mL/min,
  matching the pathway's existing shared `GFR_REFERENCE_ML_PER_MIN`) and
  that the ~55% TmG reduction after 7 days of dapagliflozin is
  proportionally identical in both groups (420->176 T2D, 317->150
  healthy) -- confirming beta (which represents that reduction) does not
  need a population split, only TmG does.
- **Al-Jobori H et al. 2017, *Diabetes*, PMID:28428225** -- abstract
  confirms verbatim: "459 +/- 53 vs. 337 +/- 25 mg/min" (T2D vs. healthy
  baseline TmG); "reduced the TmG in both individuals with and without
  diabetes by 44 +/- 7 and 53 +/- 6%, respectively" (48h); "further
  reduced... on day 14 (by 65 +/- 5 and 75 +/- 3%, respectively)."

**Fix**: added `t2d: bool = False` to both `RenalClearanceParameters
.for_dapagliflozin()` and `.for_empagliflozin(days_of_treatment)`
(`renal_pathway.py`). `t2d=True` selects `DAPAGLIFLOZIN_TMG_T2D_MG_PER_MIN
= 420.0` / `EMPAGLIFLOZIN_TMG_T2D_MG_PER_MIN = 459.0` instead of the
healthy constants (317.0/337.0, now named
`*_TMG_HEALTHY_MG_PER_MIN`), and for empagliflozin ALSO selects that
paper's own T2D-cohort day2/day14 reduction fractions (0.44/0.65) instead
of the healthy fractions (0.53/0.75) for the beta duration-scaling --
not just a different TmG with a healthy-cohort beta fraction
incorrectly carried over. GFR and `SPLAY_INDEX_P` are deliberately NOT
split by t2d: GFR because DeFronzo's own paper already reports it as
"similar" between groups (the existing shared reference value already
reflects this); splay because both papers report only an aggregate splay
AUC figure with no principled way to convert it into this model's
dimensionless `splay_p` exponent (same, already-documented limitation
`SPLAY_INDEX_P`'s own docstring states for the healthy value) --
disclosed explicitly in the new docstrings, not silently dropped.

`t2d` defaults to `False`, reproducing the exact prior behaviour
byte-for-byte when omitted -- verified directly (both classmethods'
`t2d=False` output compared to the pre-diff hardcoded constants) and via
`ModelValidator().validate_all()`: all 6 registered clinical benchmarks
(OGTT, Bergman IV, semaglutide, prednisone/T2D, metformin/T2D,
canagliflozin) report byte-identical verdicts/deviations before and
after, since `Canagliflozin_300mg_postprandial` (the one existing SGLT2i
benchmark, Polidori et al. 2013) is a healthy-subject scenario with no
`physiological_profile` set, so it genuinely takes the unaffected
`t2d=False` path.

**Wired auto-detection into `SimulationRunner._detect_renal()`**
(`runner.py`), which previously took only `drug_events: list`; changed to
take the full `scenario: ScenarioDefinition` (mirroring `_detect_hepatic()`'s
established `profile = scenario.personalization.physiological_profile;
disease_states = profile.disease_states if profile is not None else []`
pattern line-for-line) so a `DiseaseState.TYPE_2_DIABETES` profile
automatically selects each active SGLT2i drug's T2D-cohort preset,
without the caller needing to pass `t2d` explicitly.

Numerically verified the fix changes real behaviour, not just a stored-
but-unused field: at a given filtered glucose load, the T2D preset's
higher Tm genuinely reabsorbs more before saturating than the healthy
preset does (e.g. at G=10mM: no-drug excretion 2.09 mg/min healthy vs.
0.23 mg/min T2D) -- a real, if modest, distinguishing physiological
effect, not a no-op.

### DONE — Sulfonylureas (glibenclamide): a genuinely new additive, glucose-independent insulin-secretion mechanism (Track 1, MASTER_PLAN 1.3)

Picked via the standing autonomous-loop process. MASTER_PLAN.md row 1.3
described this as "architecturally cheap — reuses the existing
`secretion_scale_modifier` rule-11 slot," estimated at 1 chunk. Dispatched
a `computational-biologist` scoping pass to verify this before
implementing, per the loop's own discipline of not trusting a backlog
row's own framing at face value -- it found the assumption was **wrong**,
not just under-scoped.

**The mechanistic problem, verified numerically before accepting it**:
sulfonylureas close the pancreatic beta-cell KATP channel via SUR1
binding, triggering insulin secretion INDEPENDENT of ambient glucose --
the textbook mechanism behind their real, defining hypoglycaemia risk.
But `secretion_scale` multiplies `delta_secretion` (`pathway.py`'s
Michaelis-Menten, glucose-gated term), which is exactly zero at basal
glucose and goes MORE NEGATIVE below it (floors at exactly `-ke*Ib`).
Probed directly: at G=3.5mM, `delta_secretion=-6.138` (already floored);
a 1.5x `secretion_scale` makes it `-9.207` -- i.e. a `secretion_scale`-only
implementation would model a sulfonylurea as SUPPRESSING insulin harder
during hypoglycaemia, the exact opposite of its defining clinical risk.
Also confirmed `G_threshold`/`KG_secretion` can't fix this either:
`F_secretion_basal` is analytically pinned so total secretion always
floors at exactly zero regardless of either, and lowering `G_threshold`
to raise low-glucose secretion collapses `F_secretion_basal` and
suppresses the POSTPRANDIAL response instead (34.19->8.58 pM/min at
G=11mM for a `G_threshold` of 3.2 vs. 4.5) -- neither parameter is usable
alone.

**Literature, found by a `literature-curator` agent and independently
re-verified live via NCBI efetch** (not trusted from either agent's
report): **Riefflin A, Ayyagari U, Manley SE, Holman RR, Levy JC. "The
effect of glibenclamide on insulin secretion at normal glucose
concentrations." Diabetologia. 2015;58(1):43-9. PMID:25297572** -- RCT,
double-blind, placebo-controlled crossover, n=19 T2D, glibenclamide
2.5mg twice daily x14 days vs. placebo x14 days, 3-step hyperinsulinaemic
glucose clamp (4.0/8.0/12.0 mmol/L). C-peptide secretion rate rose by an
ABSOLUTE increment "independent of clamp glucose concentration (p=0.54)"
-- 140/126/158 pmol/min at 4.0/8.0/12.0 mmol/L respectively (proportional
increase 2.8-/1.8-/1.7-fold vs. placebo, all p<0.001) -- i.e. genuinely
glucose-INDEPENDENT, exactly the mechanism needed and directly
falsifying the `secretion_scale`-only design. Corroborating source, also
verified live: **Go EH, Kyriakidou-Himonas M, Berelowitz M. "Effects of
glipizide GITS and glibenclamide on metabolic control, hepatic glucose
production, and insulin secretion in patients with type 2 diabetes."
Diabetes Metab Res Rev. 2004;20(3):225-31. PMID:15133754** -- a real,
disclosed tension: "fasting insulin was not significantly increased by
any treatment" in an ambulatory (non-clamped) T2D population, a weaker
but genuine counterpoint to Riefflin's clamp-study finding.

**Design**: added `glucose_independent_secretion: float = 0.0`
(pM/min, additive to `dI`, neutral default) to `PathwayParameters`
(`pathway.py`) -- the first PathwayParameters field ever added to `dI`
unconditionally, not gated by any rule-11 signal (it doesn't need
`CompositePathway` coupling: it's not a function of another pathway's
state, matching metformin/glucocorticoid's static-field precedent, not
GLP1/hepatic/renal's coupled-pathway one).

**A real, non-obvious fixed-point subtlety, worked through carefully
before implementing (this project's own established discipline for any
new state-affecting mechanism)**: setting `glucose_independent_secretion`
nonzero shifts the analytic insulin fixed point away from `Ib` (now
`I_ss = Ib + glucose_independent_secretion/ke`) -- which means `X`
(remote insulin, `dX = -p2*X + p3*max(I-Ib,0)`), `IGF1` (production
scales with `I/Ib`), and `mTOR`/`AMPK` (relax toward Hill functions of
`I`) ALL have correspondingly shifted fixed points too, not just
insulin. `basal_state()` was rewritten to derive every one of these from
`I_ss` rather than the old hardcoded `Ib`-based formulas -- getting only
`I` right and leaving `X` hardcoded at `0.0` would have reproduced the
EXACT bug class in KNOWN BUGS FIXED #10-14 (`X` would immediately start
drifting away from 0 at t=0 with zero meal input, since `dX` at
`(X=0, I=I_ss>Ib)` is nonzero). Every formula reduces to EXACTLY the
prior hardcoded value when `glucose_independent_secretion=0.0` --
verified both symbolically and via `pathway.validate_y0(tolerance=1e-8)`
returning `[]` for a nonzero value, plus a 600-step standalone
integration confirming no drift.

**Hard safety bound**: `__post_init__` rejects
`glucose_independent_secretion >= ke*Ib` -- at that boundary, `I_ss`
would reach 2x the patient's own basal `Ib` from the glucose-independent
floor alone, with zero glucose-driven secretion. An engineering safety
bound (same "isolated, disclosed assumption" category as
`MIN_GB_THRESHOLD_MARGIN_MM`), not a literature-derived ceiling.

**Calibration, honestly disclosed as an approximation, not a directly-
cited number**: `SULFONYLUREA_SECRETION_FRACTION_OF_KE_IB = 0.5`
(`drug_interactions.py`) -- Riefflin's absolute pmol/min figures are
whole-body C-peptide secretion RATES (via two-compartment
deconvolution), a different physical quantity from this model's plasma
INSULIN CONCENTRATION rate constant, and converting between them needs
an insulin distribution-volume/clearance relationship this paper doesn't
report and this codebase doesn't otherwise anchor. Rather than invent an
unverified conversion factor, the paper's ROBUST, GLUCOSE-INDEPENDENT
FINDING (not its absolute units) justifies a bounded fraction of this
model's own `ke*Ib` reference: 0.5 gives `I_ss = 1.5*Ib`, clearly large
enough to represent Riefflin's real, significant effect (1.7-2.8-fold,
all p<0.001) while staying well below the hard safety bound and not
grossly contradicting Go et al. 2004's weaker "not significantly
increased" finding.

**Wiring**: `Drug.GLIBENCLAMIDE` added to the `Drug` enum;
`_sulfonylurea_modifiers()` returns `{}` (matching the
GLP1/SGLT2i precedent) since `compose_all_modifiers()`'s multiplicative
pipeline (`new_val = base_val * factor`) can never move a 0.0 base value
regardless of factor -- the real effect is applied directly in
`PhysiologicalPersonalizer.personalize()` via a new special-cased
override block (same pattern as the existing Gb/G_threshold margin
clamp and Brunzell first_phase_gain zeroing), gated on `dose_mg > 0`.
`_describe_modifiers()` gained a matching special case so the audit
trail (`AppliedModifier`) actually records this drug's real effect --
otherwise `modifiers_for_dose()` returning `{}` would make the generic
per-drug loop silently skip it entirely, the same "audit trail misses
this source's effect" bug class already fixed for BMI/T2D/metformin
elsewhere in this file.

**Two real findings from the mandatory review passes, both fixed before
finalizing**:
- **Code-reviewer** (APPROVE, 0 CRITICAL/HIGH): one MEDIUM, a test-
  organization slip -- the new `TestGlucoseIndependentSecretionFixedPoint`
  class was inserted without a proper boundary, silently reparenting
  three pre-existing, unrelated `TestPathwayParameters` tests
  (`test_kg_secretion_matches_literature_gsis_ec50`,
  `test_p3_matches_bergman_1981_own_reported_si`,
  `test_first_phase_gain_positive`) into it. Zero functional impact
  (pytest still collected and ran all three correctly), fixed by moving
  them back.
- **Security-reviewer** (APPROVE, 0 CRITICAL/HIGH): one real MEDIUM --
  the special-cased override block checked only drug identity, not
  `dose_mg`, so a `dose_mg=0.0` glibenclamide event still triggered the
  FULL effect (confirmed directly: 0.001mg, 2.5mg, and 100mg all
  produced the identical `glucose_independent_secretion`, and so did
  `dose_mg=0.0`). Fixed with the same `dose.dose_mg <= 0: return {}`
  guard every other dose-scaled modifier function in this file already
  has. The reviewer's second observation (the effect is also
  timing-independent -- `hours_since_ingestion=0` vs. `500` produce the
  identical value) was confirmed to be an intentional design choice, not
  a second bug: Riefflin's own study measured a CHRONIC, steady-state
  effect, matching `metformin_modifiers()`'s own established "always
  chronic, timing irrelevant" precedent -- documented explicitly in the
  code (not left as an unexamined assumption) and locked in with a
  dedicated regression test
  (`test_glibenclamide_effect_is_deliberately_timing_independent`) so a
  future session doesn't mistake this for an unfixed bug either.
  Reviewer also flagged (LOW) that it lacked live PubMed access to
  independently spot-check the two citations -- both were already
  independently re-verified live by this session directly (the exact
  quotes are captured above), so not a live gap.

+18 tests total: 9 in `test_ode_engine.py` (field validation, safety
bound enforcement at/just-below the boundary, fixed-point derivation,
`validate_y0()` at tolerance 1e-8, 600-step trajectory stability,
glucose-independence proof at severe hypoglycaemia), 7 in
`test_physiology.py` (no multiplicative modifier, personalizer wiring,

analogous to the existing `glucose_peak_uM`) plus a `glucose_nadir_mM`
property, computed in `_compute_expert_metrics()` via `np.min(G)` over
the full simulated trajectory. New "Hypoglycaemia risk" indicators added
to both `report.py` (GREEN >=3.9mM / AMBER 3.0-3.8mM "Level 1" / RED
<3.0mM "Level 2") and `risk_score.py` (LOW/ELEVATED/HIGH, same two
thresholds) -- `risk_score.py` imports the threshold constants directly
from `report.py` (`_HYPO_LEVEL1_MM`/`_HYPO_LEVEL2_MM`) rather than
duplicating them, closing off the exact "two files compute the same
thing independently, drift apart" bug class already caught once for
`food_items.py`'s `gi_category` vs. `gi_meals.py`'s `GI_VALUES`.

**A genuine, honestly-disclosed finding, not a limitation of the test
suite**: verified numerically, before writing any test, that this
platform's CURRENT drug-effect calibrations cannot push a real
`SimulationRunner` scenario's glucose below the 3.9mM alert value at
all -- not even at each mechanism's own most extreme valid parameter.
`RenalClearanceParameters(beta=0.95)` (near its architectural ceiling)
reaches only ~4.34mM nadir in a fasted scenario; combining it with
`glucose_independent_secretion` near its own safety bound (99% of
`ke*Ib`) made negligible further difference (4.319mM). Both mandatory
review agents independently reproduced this same finding by trying
further combinations (T2D profile, exercise-in-progress, alcohol,
metformin, both SGLT2i drugs stacked) -- none crossed 3.9mM. This means
the AMBER/RED code paths, while correctly implemented and unit-tested,
cannot currently be exercised by any real, currently-shippable scenario
-- disclosed explicitly (see below), not silently left as an unverified
assumption.

**Two real findings from the mandatory review passes**:
- **Security-reviewer** (APPROVE, 0 CRITICAL/HIGH): one real MEDIUM --

- **Code-reviewer** (APPROVE, 0 CRITICAL/HIGH): independently re-fetched

### DONE — Acarbose (alpha-glucosidase inhibitor): a new absorption-rate drug mechanism (Track 1, MASTER_PLAN 1.4)

Picked via the standing autonomous-loop process. Dispatched a
`computational-biologist` + `literature-curator` scoping fan-out first
(this drug acts on a part of the model -- meal absorption -- no prior
drug addition this session had touched).

**Mechanism, verified before implementing**: acarbose competitively
inhibits intestinal alpha-glucosidase enzymes, slowing carbohydrate
breakdown into absorbable glucose -- mechanistically distinct from
every other drug this platform models (it acts purely on absorption
RATE, not insulin secretion/action/clearance at all). The scoping
agent confirmed, by direct execution, that reducing `MealInput.kabs`
(the absorption rate constant) directly is mass-conserving by
construction (`integral(D*k*exp(-k*t) dt) = D for any k>0`), unlike
scaling `Ra(t)`'s output (the GLP-1 gastric-emptying bug already fixed
earlier in this file's history, which deletes mass rather than
delaying it) -- confirmed independently by me and by both mandatory
review agents.

**Literature, verified live via NCBI efetch (full text)**: Chen Z, Fu
X, Kuang J, Chen J, Chen H, Pei J, Yang H. "Single-dose acarbose
decreased glucose-dependent insulinotropic peptide and glucagon levels
in Chinese patients with newly diagnosed type 2 diabetes mellitus
after a mixed meal." BMC Endocr Disord. 2016. PMID:27686734. n=12
newly diagnosed T2D, single 100mg dose with a mixed meal (370kcal,
74% carbohydrate), same meal given a week apart without/with the drug
(a real, if unblinded/non-randomized-order, same-meal comparison --
disclosed limitation, not a randomized double-blind crossover like
this platform's other drug benchmarks). Table 2's own numbers,
confirmed directly against the real full text: peak glucose 13.22
mmol/L @ 60min (no drug) -> 9.45 mmol/L @ 90min (with drug) -- a
**-28.5% peak-height reduction combined with a 60->90min (1.5x)
peak-TIME DELAY**, not just a lower peak. This dual signature (lower
AND later peak) is exactly what a genuine rate-constant slowdown
produces (a pure amplitude scale would only lower the peak without
moving it) -- direct confirmation that a kabs reduction is the
mechanistically correct design, not merely convenient. Insulin moved
the same direction (-40.6% peak, no time shift, also confirmed against
the primary numbers) -- consistent with insulin secretion simply
tracking a smaller/later glucose stimulus, not a separate anti-
secretory mechanism, corroborated by Zhou et al. 2013 (PMID:23631607),
a head-to-head study where a true secretagogue's insulin ROSE while
acarbose's fell.

**Calibration, a genuine two-number consistency check, not a single-
target curve fit**: numerically searched for the single kabs-scale
factor that reproduces BOTH Chen et al.'s independent observations
simultaneously in this platform's own real ODE model for a 75g meal --
found `ACARBOSE_100MG_KABS_SCALE = 0.35` gives -27.0% peak height
(target -28.5%) AND 1.51x peak-time delay (target 1.5x) at once. No
literature exists mapping acarbose dose directly to a kabs percentage
(Fischer et al. 1998, PMID:9625287, a real 495-patient placebo-
controlled dose-ranging RCT, gives a saturating dose-response curve
but in chronic 24-week postprandial-AUC-percentage terms, a different
metric) -- the log-dose-response SHAPE used to extrapolate to other
doses is a disclosed modeling assumption (same "log-dose, calibrated
at one measured point" limitation already disclosed for
`caffeine_modifiers()`), capped at the 100mg reference dose rather
than extrapolated to higher doses this platform has no acute-kabs data
for.

**Design**: `Drug.ACARBOSE` added; `_alpha_glucosidase_inhibitor_
modifiers()` returns `{}` (matching the GLP-1/SGLT2i/sulfonylurea
precedent -- the real effect lives outside the multiplicative
PathwayParameters pipeline entirely, this time on meal inputs rather
than PathwayParameters or an ODE-coupled pathway). `acarbose_kabs_
scale(dose_mg)` computes the scale factor; `SimulationRunner.run()`
detects an active acarbose event (via the same `Drug(...) in
ALPHA_GLUCOSIDASE_INHIBITOR_DRUGS` pattern `_detect_glp1()`/
`_detect_renal()` already use) and applies `dataclasses.replace(meal,
kabs=meal.kabs*scale)` to each meal.

**A real, disclosed scope limitation, not silently applied only where
convenient**: any meal using `MealEvent.glycaemic_index` (which routes
to `GutAbsorptionModel`, and never reads `kabs` at all -- includes
`ogtt_75g()`, this platform's own flagship benchmark scenario) is left
completely unaffected by acarbose, with an explicit warning appended
(matching the existing GI-route-validity warning's own pattern)
instead of silently doing nothing. Verified directly: a GI-adjusted
meal's glucose trajectory is byte-identical with and without acarbose.
Not fixed this pass -- would need reducing `GutAbsorptionModel.
k_absorption` instead, subject to its own `k_absorption > k_emptying`
validity constraint (flagged as MASTER_PLAN.md row 1.4b). A second,
related, disclosed limitation: `MealEvent` has no substrate-composition
field, so acarbose's kabs reduction applies uniformly regardless of
whether a meal is free glucose (which alpha-glucosidase doesn't act on
at all) or starch/disaccharide-containing (which it does) -- this
happens to coincide with the GI-route limitation for the one pure-
glucose flagship scenario (`ogtt_75g()`'s `glycaemic_index=100.0`
already triggers the "not applied" warning above for an unrelated
reason), but remains a real, undisclosed-until-now gap for any
non-GI-adjusted meal that's mostly free sugar.

**A genuine, unrelated bug found and fixed while implementing this**:
`runner.py` had a redundant LOCAL `import dataclasses` inside one `if`
branch of `run()` (the glucocorticoid-event block). Adding a new
module-level `import dataclasses` for this milestone's own code
triggered a real `UnboundLocalError` -- Python's function-scoping rules
mean any assignment/import anywhere in a function body makes that name
local to the ENTIRE function, so the dormant local import silently
shadowed the new module-level one for the WHOLE `run()` method,
including this milestone's own new code, whenever the glucocorticoid
branch wasn't reached first. Fixed by removing the redundant local
import and relying on the module-level one; both the mandatory
code-reviewer and security-reviewer passes independently reproduced
the failure mode against the pre-fix code and confirmed the fix.

**Two real findings from the mandatory review passes, both fixed**:
- **Code-reviewer** (APPROVE, 0 CRITICAL/HIGH/MEDIUM): one LOW -- the
  new `ALPHA_GLUCOSIDASE_INHIBITOR_DRUGS` set was defined but never
  actually consulted by `runner.py` (which used a bare `e.drug ==
  "acarbose"` string check instead), a forward-compatibility trap for
  whenever miglitol is added later (MASTER_PLAN row 1.4b). Fixed to
  match the established `GLP1_DRUGS`/`SGLT2_DRUGS` convention exactly
  (`Drug(event.drug) in ALPHA_GLUCOSIDASE_INHIBITOR_DRUGS`, wrapped in
  the same `try/except ValueError` pattern those detectors use).
- **Security-reviewer** (APPROVE, 0 CRITICAL/HIGH): one real LOW --
  `acarbose_kabs_scale()` takes a raw float directly (unlike every
  other modifier function in this file, which takes an already-
  validated `DrugDose`/`DrugEvent`), and a NaN dose silently returned
  `0.35` (via `min(1.0, nan)`, which Python resolves to the first
  argument on a NaN comparison) instead of raising -- not reachable via
  the real `DrugEvent`/`SimulationRunner` path today (already validated
  finite upstream), but the function is public and independently
  callable. Fixed with an explicit `math.isfinite()` guard, matching
  `DrugEvent.__post_init__`'s own established pattern for exactly this
  bug class -- this also makes `+inf` raise instead of silently
  clamping to 0.35, a deliberate strengthening for consistency with how
  every other dose-accepting entry point in this codebase treats
  infinite input as invalid, not just NaN specifically.

+14 tests: 7 in `test_physiology.py` (no-PathwayParameters-modifier
guard, zero/negative-dose neutrality, 100mg calibration match, dose-
response monotonicity, capping beyond 100mg, positivity floor, the
NaN/inf guard), 1 in `test_ode_engine.py` (mass conservation at the
actual calibrated scale and two others), 6 end-to-end in
`test_simulation_api.py` (dual peak-height/peak-time signature,
dose-response monotonicity, GI-route byte-identical-with-warning,
zero-dose neutrality, drug-only quick path, no-acarbose-means-no-
warning). 13 of 14 RED-proofed via a scoped `git stash` on the 2
source files (confirmed the exact expected `AttributeError`/
`ImportError`/`ValueError` failures pre-fix); 1 is a legitimate
non-discriminating "no acarbose event means no warning" guard. Full
suite: 1631 -> 1645 passed, 2 skipped. All 6 clinical benchmarks
unaffected (none currently use acarbose).

**Not built this pass, explicit follow-ons** (MASTER_PLAN.md row
1.4b): miglitol (a real second alpha-glucosidase inhibitor, but wasn't
this session's literature-search focus); extending the kabs-reduction
mechanism to GI-adjusted meals via `GutAbsorptionModel.k_absorption`
(needs its own investigation of that model's `k_absorption >
k_emptying` validity constraint); a substrate-composition field on
`MealEvent` to correctly exempt free-glucose meals from acarbose's
effect (currently only coincidentally handled for the one flagship
pure-glucose scenario via the GI-route limitation above).

`MASTER_PLAN.md` row 1.4 updated to done, linking here; row 1.4b added
for the three explicit follow-ons.

### DONE — Exogenous insulin (regular human insulin) (Track 1, MASTER_PLAN 1.2a)

Picked via the standing autonomous-loop process. This platform had no
way to model INJECTED insulin at all before this -- every existing
insulin-raising mechanism (delta_secretion/first_phase_secretion,
sulfonylurea's glucose_independent_secretion) is endogenous, and this
is the prerequisite (MASTER_PLAN row 1.10) for a future T1D disease
state, where injected insulin is the only insulin the patient has.

**Mechanism, verified numerically before picking a structure**: a
SINGLE subcutaneous depot compartment feeding into this model's own
plasma-insulin elimination rate (`ke=0.093/min`, Sherwin 1974) cannot
reproduce a realistic time-to-peak (Tmax) at all -- solving for the
single-depot absorption rate constant that would give Howey et al.
1994's observed Tmax=101min (10U regular insulin, healthy subjects,
PMID:8314011, verified live via NCBI efetch this session) requires a
depot half-life of ~20 hours, making the modeled duration of action
unbounded (>900min, never returning to baseline) -- physiologically
absurd for regular insulin's real ~5-8h duration. This is the classic
"flip-flop kinetics" problem in the real PK literature (independently
confirmed: Potocka et al. 2011, PMID:20940337, uses a genuine
2-sequential-compartment absorption model for exactly this reason).

**Solved with TWO sequential depot compartments (S1 -> S2 -> plasma)
using the SAME rate constant `ka` for both transitions** -- a special,
exactly-solvable repeated-eigenvalue case with a closed-form analytic
solution, needing NO new ODE integration state at all:
`S1(t) = S1_0*exp(-ka*t)`, `S2(t) = S1_0*ka*t*exp(-ka*t)` (verified by
direct differentiation), giving `exogenous_insulin_delta(t) =
ka^2*S1_0*t*exp(-ka*t)` -- a Bateman-function shape, confirmed
numerically to match a genuine two-state ODE integration to ~1e-8
relative error before being adopted as the sole implementation.
`ExogenousInsulinPathway` (new file, `exogenous_insulin_pathway.py`) is
stateless (zero species, mirroring `ExercisePathway`'s precedent),
exposing this signal as a new additive rule-11 key,
`exogenous_insulin_delta` (added to `dI`'s computation in `pathway.py`
and to `descriptor.input_signals` -- also fixing a pre-existing,
unrelated documentation-drift bug where `renal_glucose_clearance_delta`
was already used in `dydt()`'s own docstring but missing from that same
metadata list). Exactly zero before/without a dose and never perturbs
the analytic basal steady state for any dose (`validate_y0(tolerance=
1e-8)` confirmed for both zero-dose and an active dose scheduled at
t=0) -- a strictly easier fixed-point situation than sulfonylurea's own
`glucose_independent_secretion` (which needed a full `basal_state()`
re-derivation), since this signal is genuinely transient rather than a
constant floor.

**Calibration, disclosed as a genuine engineering back-solve, not a
directly-cited pair of numbers** (same "isolated calibration
assumption" category as `HPA_FEEDBACK_GAIN`/the SGLT2i beta constants):
`INSULIN_REGULAR_KA_PER_MIN=0.0113` and `INSULIN_REGULAR_PM_PER_UNIT=
695.1`, chosen so a 10U dose reproduces Howey et al. 1994's observed
Tmax=101min/Cmax=308pM excess exactly through the FULL composed ODE
(`ExogenousInsulinPathway` + `GlucoseInsulinPathway` + `ODESystem`), not
just the isolated signal. Kobayashi et al. 1983's one-compartment fit
(PMID:6339306, ka=0.026/min, ke=0.013/min) was explicitly NOT reused --
that paper's `ke` is the APPARENT elimination rate of its own
one-compartment fit (dominated by the slow absorption phase itself),
not this model's independently-anchored true plasma clearance rate;
reusing it directly against this model's much faster `ke` gives
Tmax~19min, verified far too early.

**Wiring**: `Drug.INSULIN_REGULAR` added to the `Drug` enum;
`_exogenous_insulin_modifiers()` returns `{}` unconditionally (matching
the GLP-1/SGLT2i/sulfonylurea precedent -- the ODE pathway is the sole
representation). New `SimulationRunner._detect_exogenous_insulin()`
finds an active `insulin_regular` `DrugEvent` and composes the pathway,
computing `dose_time_min = (event.time_s/60.0) - (event.
hours_before_simulation*60.0)` -- combining BOTH fields into one net
time offset relative to t=0, rather than reusing `DrugEvent.
to_drug_dose()`'s `hours_since_ingestion` snapshot (which discards
`time_s` entirely for the standard `simulation_start_s=0.0` call every
real caller uses) -- this signal is genuinely time-varying throughout a
simulation, unlike every other drug's static personalization snapshot,
so the snapshot-style formula would be architecturally wrong here, not
just imprecise. Only one `insulin_regular` event is composed per
scenario today (a documented limitation, verified with a regression
test -- a second event is silently ignored, matching `CompositePathway`'s
own inability to disambiguate two pathway instances sharing one name).

**A real, honestly-verified model behaviour, not a bug**: a FASTED
(no-meal) scenario shows insulin genuinely rising with dose but glucose
staying EXACTLY flat at Gb regardless of dose size -- confirmed this
matches the earlier glibenclamide-alone finding exactly: insulin's
glucose-clearance action (via the X/remote-insulin compartment) is
proportional to `(G - Gb_eff)`, which is exactly zero at the analytic
basal state regardless of how large X becomes. A real, dose-dependent
glucose-lowering effect DOES appear in a MEAL scenario (peak/AUC/later-
timepoint reductions all confirmed, dose-response monotonic). Both
behaviours are locked in with dedicated tests, including one that
explicitly documents the fasted-scenario non-effect as intentional
(matching this project's convention of testing and disclosing real,
possibly-counterintuitive model behaviour rather than leaving it
silently unverified).

**Mandatory code-reviewer and security-reviewer passes, both ran
successfully (no quota outage), both surfaced real findings, all fixed
before finalizing**:

- **Code-reviewer** (APPROVE with findings): MEDIUM -- `dose_mg` is
  silently reinterpreted as INSULIN UNITS for this one drug (no
  per-drug unit system exists on `DrugEvent`), but this was disclosed
  only in backend implementation comments, never at the `DrugEvent.
  dose_mg`/`DrugEventIn.dose_mg` field definitions themselves -- the two
  places a REST consumer or future contributor would actually look.
  Fixed: added explicit docstring notes at both field definitions. LOW
  -- `exogenous_insulin_delta` was missing from `coupling.py`'s
  `ADDITIVE_SIGNAL_KEYS` frozenset (every other additive rule-11 signal
  is registered there per the project's own established convention,
  used to combine multiple simultaneous contributions to the same
  signal) -- confirmed currently harmless (only one
  `ExogenousInsulinPathway` can ever be composed per scenario today,
  per the "first wins" limitation above), but fixed for forward
  consistency. LOW -- no test for the "multiple insulin events -> first
  wins" documented limitation; added one.
- **Security-reviewer** (APPROVE with findings): **HIGH** -- no
  plausibility bound existed on `dose_units` at all, combined with the
  `dose_mg`-as-Units reinterpretation -- a realistic copy-paste error
  (reusing a metformin-style `dose_mg~2000` for an insulin_regular
  event) would silently produce a ~200x-too-large insulin spike with
  zero warning, the same severity class as the previously-fixed
  Gb/G_threshold margin collapse. Fixed: added
  `MAX_PLAUSIBLE_REGULAR_INSULIN_DOSE_UNITS=100.0` (an engineering
  plausibility ceiling, not a literature-derived clinical maximum,
  documented as such), enforced in `ExogenousInsulinParameters
  .__init__`. **MEDIUM** -- `S1_0 = dose_units*pm_per_unit` was never
  checked for overflow after construction; an extreme-but-individually-
  finite `dose_units`/`pm_per_unit` pair could silently produce
  `inf`/`NaN` fed unguarded into `dI`, unlike the precedent already
  established for `RenalPathway.target_delta_mM_per_min()`'s
  `GLUCOSE_UPPER_BOUND_MM` clamp. Fixed: added an explicit
  `math.isfinite(dose_units*pm_per_unit)` check at construction.
  **MEDIUM** -- an extreme (but schema-valid; Pydantic only enforces
  `ge=0`, no upper bound) `hours_before_simulation` overflows
  `dose_time_min` to `-inf`, which `ExogenousInsulinParameters
  .__init__`'s existing finiteness check correctly catches as a
  `ValueError` -- but that exception propagated uncaught through
  `SimulationRunner.run()` and past the REST API's only
  `except ValueError -> 400` handler (which only wrapped
  `scenario_in_to_definition()`), producing an unhandled 500 instead of
  a graceful 400. Fixed: wrapped the `SimulationRunner().run(scenario)`
  call in `/simulate` with its own `except ValueError -> 400` handler.
  Confirmed clean: no double-counting (`_exogenous_insulin_modifiers()`
  is the sole, empty static representation), no OWASP/secrets/injection
  concerns (pure numerical code).

All three security findings and all three code-review findings
RED-proofed directly (temporarily reverting just the relevant lines,
confirming the exact documented failure mode, then restoring) rather
than via `git stash` for the two new, not-yet-committed source/test
files -- confirmed the extreme-`hours_before_simulation` REST test
produces the documented raw `ValueError`/500 traceback pre-fix, and
both the plausibility-ceiling and `S1_0`-overflow tests fail with
`DID NOT RAISE` pre-fix.

+8 tests: 18 new unit/integration tests in
`test_exogenous_insulin_pathway.py` (parameter validation including the
new ceiling/overflow guards, pathway mechanics, basal-invariance,
composed-simulation Howey 1994 reproduction, long-trajectory stability)
plus 9 end-to-end `SimulationRunner` tests in `test_simulation_api.py`
(insulin raises plasma insulin, Howey 1994 Tmax/Cmax match through the
real production path, meal-scenario dose-dependent glucose-AUC
lowering, the fasted-scenario non-effect documented as intentional,
dose timing via `hours_before_simulation`, zero-dose neutrality, no

wins), 1 new REST-level test (extreme timing -> 400 not 500). Full
suite: 1645 -> 1676 passed, 2 skipped. All 6 registered clinical
benchmarks (`ModelValidator().validate_all()`) confirmed byte-identical
before/after (none use insulin_regular).

**Not built this pass, explicit follow-ons** (MASTER_PLAN.md rows
1.2b/1.2c): a dedicated `InsulinDoseEvent` scenario type with genuine
