### DONE (negative result, no code change) — Fresh literature search for the glucagon fasting/basal-EGP gain coefficient found a real anchor point, but it cannot be honestly extrapolated to the magnitude this platform needs (MASTER_PLAN 1.1)

Picked via the standing autonomous-loop process -- lowest-numbered open
Track 1 chunk, Docker still down (Track 3 stays blocked). Row 1.1
explicitly named "a fresh search angle" as the way to un-stall this
chunk after two prior capped search passes failed to find a usable
glucagon-to-EGP-rate gain coefficient. Dispatched `literature-curator`
with instructions to try genuinely new search terms (not repeat the
two already-tried angles) and either find a real coefficient or confirm
a documented negative result.

**A real, previously-unfound primary source WAS found this time**,
independently re-verified live via `PubMedFetcher.fetch_by_pubmed_id()`
before trusting it (the agent's own abstract paraphrase matched the
live-fetched text exactly, word for word): **Liljenquist JE, Mueller
GL, Cherrington AD, Keller U, Chiasson J-L, Perry JM, Lacy WW,
Rabinowitz D. "Evidence for an important role of glucagon in the
regulation of hepatic glucose production in normal man." J Clin
Invest. 1977;59(2):369-374. PMID:833282** -- n=4 healthy men,
hepatic-vein/brachial-artery catheterization, euglycaemic pancreatic
(somatostatin) clamp with basal insulin held constant (10-14 uU/ml,
explicitly controlling for insulin confounding, exactly what's needed
to isolate the glucagon effect specifically), FASTING/basal conditions
throughout. Confirmed verbatim: "Arterial plasma glucagon levels fell
by greater than 50%... In response... net splanchnic glucose production
(NSGP) fell by 75% and remained suppressed for the duration of the
study." This is a genuine, human, primary-source, quantitative
fasting-condition relationship between a defined glucagon reduction and
a defined hepatic glucose production reduction, with insulin explicitly
controlled -- precisely the class of anchor this chunk needed and the
two prior passes hadn't found (a different search angle -- author-name-
based physiology-literature search rather than "clamp+dose-response" or
GLP-1-specific terms -- surfaced it).

**Why this was NOT implemented anyway, despite being real evidence,
after weighing it against this project's own precedent for accepting
single-anchor-point calibrations (`HPA_FEEDBACK_GAIN`, the exogenous-
insulin `ka`/`pm_per_unit` back-solve, acarbose's `kabs`-scale
calibration)**: in every one of those accepted precedents, the single
real anchor point is matched EXACTLY against the SAME scenario the
model actually needs to reproduce (exogenous insulin's `ka`/`pm_per_unit`
are calibrated at Howey et al. 1994's own 10U dose, the exact dose this
platform models; acarbose's `kabs` scale is calibrated at the SAME
100mg reference dose the model's production presets use, with
extrapolation to OTHER doses done via a documented, disclosed log-dose
SHAPE assumption, not by extrapolating the CALIBRATED anchor point
itself). **Liljenquist 1977's anchor point is a >50% glucagon
reduction** (near-total suppression via somatostatin) -- this
platform's actual target scenario (semaglutide's real, measured fasting
glucagon effect, Hjerpsted et al. 2018, PMID:28941314: ETR 0.86, a
**-14%** reduction) is a 3.5x-SMALLER perturbation than the only
quantitative data point available. Translating the 50%->75% ratio into
a linear per-percent gain (implying a ~21% EGP reduction for a 14%
glucagon change) would require assuming the glucagon-EGP dose-response
relationship is LINEAR across a >3x range it was never actually
measured at -- a real, unverified assumption, not something Liljenquist
1977 itself establishes (the paper's own second arm, somatostatin alone
with insulin also allowed to fall, shows the relationship is NOT even
sustained the same way across different experimental conditions --
NSGP rebounded to basal by 105min in that arm despite continued
hormonal suppression, precisely because insulin wasn't held constant --
demonstrating this system's real sensitivity to exactly the kind of
condition-dependence that makes a naive linear extrapolation risky).
Real endocrine dose-response relationships are commonly sigmoidal/
saturating rather than linear, and a targeted search specifically for
a genuine multi-point dose-response curve ("graded glucagon infusion
hepatic glucose production man") returned zero results -- confirming no
data exists to check the linearity assumption against, one way or the
other.

**Decision, per this chunk's own MASTER_PLAN-stated fallback**: fitting
a specific numeric gain by extrapolating a single large-perturbation
anchor point down to a 3.5x-smaller regime it was never measured at
would manufacture a specific, precise-looking coefficient this
project's own evidence base cannot actually support -- the same
"fabricating false precision is worse than an honest unknown" principle
already applied to reject the GI-timing-slope's own single-study
extrapolation (`for_gi()`'s documented permanent limitation) and the
`KG_secretion~200`/joint-fit `p1~0.008` curve-fit leads earlier this
project's history, even though the specific evidentiary shape here
(one real study at the wrong perturbation magnitude, rather than two
directly-contradicting studies) is different. **Recorded as
permanently blocked, matching row 1.1's own explicitly-named
alternative outcome**, not implemented. No pathway, signal key, or
coupling was written; no existing code was touched.

**What would actually resolve this, for a future session**: a genuine
dose-response study spanning multiple glucagon-reduction magnitudes,
including physiologically small (10-20%) changes comparable to real
GLP-1-agonist effect sizes -- not another search for the same
50%-plus-suppression-paradigm literature this and the two prior passes
have already exhausted. A secondary candidate checked and rejected
during this search, for the record: Kelly RP et al. 2015 (PMID:25656305,
the glucagon-receptor-antagonist LY2409021 trial) reports a real fasting
glucose reduction but with glucagon CONCENTRATION RISING (compensatory
feedback from receptor blockade) rather than independently varied, and
no EGP tracer data at all -- confounded in the opposite direction from
what's needed and not usable for this purpose either.

No code changed this entry. Full suite unchanged: 1676 passed,
2 skipped.

`MASTER_PLAN.md` row 1.1 updated: still permanently blocked, but now
with the real literature (Liljenquist 1977, PMID:833282) documented so
a future session doesn't have to re-search the same ground -- only a
genuinely different (multi-point, small-perturbation) dose-response
study would unblock this.

### DONE (negative result, no code change) — Investigated extending acarbose's effect to GI-adjusted meals; the bi-exponential model cannot reproduce the real effect size even at its mathematical extreme (MASTER_PLAN 1.4b)

Picked via the standing autonomous-loop process. Row 1.4b's own note
flagged this as needing "its own investigation of that model's
`k_absorption > k_emptying` validity constraint" before attempting a
fix -- did that investigation properly rather than assuming a naive
scale-and-clamp would work.

**Confirmed the naive approach is genuinely unsafe, not just
theoretically risky**: `GutAbsorptionModel.__post_init__` enforces
`k_absorption > k_emptying` as a HARD mathematical requirement of the
bi-exponential Ra(t) formula itself (`Ra(t) = coeff*(exp(-ke*t) -
exp(-ka*t))` -- if `ka <= ke`, this expression goes negative for large
t, which is non-physical), not an arbitrary implementation choice.
Verified directly: naively multiplying `k_absorption` by acarbose's
existing monoexponential-calibrated scale factor (0.35 at 100mg dose)
against `ogtt_calibrated_glucose()`'s own real k_emptying/k_absorption
values (0.0249/0.0416) gives `ka_new=0.01456 < ke=0.0249` -- an
immediate constraint violation at a realistic, currently-prescribable
dose.

**Designed a mathematically-safe alternative before testing it**:
instead of scaling `k_absorption` directly, scale the MARGIN by which
it exceeds `k_emptying` (`ka_new = ke + (ka_old - ke) * scale`) --
guaranteed to satisfy `ka_new > ke` for any `scale` in `(0, 1]`,
by construction, for any starting `ka_old > ke`. This also has a
genuine physiological interpretation: as intestinal absorption slows
enough to approach gastric emptying's own rate, the process becomes
increasingly emptying-rate-limited rather than absorption-rate-limited
-- a real pharmacokinetic phenomenon, not an arbitrary mathematical
trick.

**Calibrated this new functional form against the SAME real target as
the original acarbose milestone (Chen et al. 2016, PMID:27686734:
-28.5% peak-height reduction combined with a 1.5x peak-time delay),
rather than blindly reusing the monoexponential model's own 0.35 scale
factor** -- a different absorption-model SHAPE genuinely needs its own
calibration to hit the same real physiological target, verified through
the full composed ODE (`GlucoseInsulinPathway` + a real 75g meal routed
through `GutAbsorptionModel.for_gi(100.0)`, matching the original
milestone's own verification methodology exactly).

**Result: even at the mathematical extreme of this approach
(`k_absorption` pushed all the way down toward `k_emptying`, scale
-> 0), the achievable effect plateaus at only ~92% peak-height ratio
and ~1.19x peak-time delay** -- confirmed by direct numerical search
(bisection failed to reach the target ratio at any point in its search
range) and independently reconfirmed by evaluating the scale parameter
at increasingly extreme values (0.1, 0.05, 0.01, 0.001, 0.0001) and
observing the result asymptotically converge to this same ceiling,
not continue improving. This falls FAR short of Chen et al.'s real,
measured -28.5%/1.5x effect -- a genuine, confirmed STRUCTURAL
limitation of this specific functional form (the bi-exponential
Ra(t) curve's own achievable dynamic range as `ka` approaches `ke`
from above is bounded), not a calibration failure that a different
number could fix.

**Decision, per this project's own established discipline (same as the
glucagon-EGP-coefficient and metformin-PK negative results)**: NOT
implemented. Shipping a forced, mathematically-safe-but-severely-
underpowered representation of acarbose's real effect specifically for
GI-adjusted meals would be worse than the status quo (no effect at all,
with an existing, honest runtime warning already in place per the
original milestone) -- it would silently understate a real drug effect
by roughly 3-4x for exactly the meal type where a user might reasonably
expect the same, already-verified monoexponential calibration to carry
over. The existing behavior (acarbose has zero effect on GI-adjusted
meals, with `SimulationRunner`'s pre-existing warning) is left
unchanged, not replaced with a weaker mechanism.

### DONE (scoping only, no code change) — Tirzepatide (dual GIP/GLP-1 agonist): mechanism decided, calibration still blocked on paywalled full text (Track 1, MASTER_PLAN 1.5)

Picked via the standing autonomous-loop process, deliberately choosing
a candidate LESS likely to repeat the prior three cycles' negative-
result pattern (glucagon, sulfonylurea, acarbose-GI) -- tirzepatide is
a well-studied, FDA-approved, extensively-trialled drug, unlike the
narrower literature bases those three searches ran into. Row 1.5's own
structure explicitly calls for a scoping pass FIRST ("does GIP need a
genuinely distinct signal from `GLP1Pathway`... Then implementation"),
so this entry deliberately stops at that first step, matching the
row's own two-step design rather than forcing a premature
implementation.

**Real, controlled, directly on-point evidence found and verified live
via NCBI efetch** (both mandatory review agents remain in the confirmed
weekly quota outage from earlier this session -- literature scoping
done directly, bypassing agent dispatch entirely, same as the last two
cycles):
- **Heise T, Mari A, DeVries JH, et al. "Effects of subcutaneous
  tirzepatide versus placebo or semaglutide on pancreatic islet
  function and insulin sensitivity in adults with type 2 diabetes: a
  multicentre, randomised, double-blind, parallel-arm, phase 1 clinical
  trial." Lancet Diabetes Endocrinol. 2022. PMID:35468322** -- n=117
  (39 tirzepatide 15mg / 39 semaglutide 1mg / 24 placebo evaluable),
  28 weeks, on stable metformin background, a real 3-arm RCT including
  a genuine placebo comparator (not just tirzepatide-vs-semaglutide).
  Confirmed verbatim: "On meal tolerance testing, tirzepatide
  significantly reduced glucose excursions (lower insulin and glucagon
  concentrations) compared with placebo, with effects... greater than
  with semaglutide" -- and a real, quantified mechanistic decomposition:
  clamp disposition index improved by ETD 1.92 pmol.m⁻².L.min⁻².kg⁻¹
  vs. placebo (95% CI 1.59-2.24, P<.0001), driven by both improved
  total insulin secretion rate AND improved insulin sensitivity vs.
  semaglutide specifically.
- **Mather KJ, Mari A, Heise T, et al. "Effects of Tirzepatide vs
  Semaglutide on β-Cell Function, Insulin Sensitivity, and Glucose
  Control During a Meal Test." J Clin Endocrinol Metab. 2024.
  PMID:38795393** -- a model-based re-analysis of the SAME trial's
  MMTT data. The single most important sentence for this platform's
  own architecture, confirmed verbatim: **"Incremental glucose AUC did
  not differ significantly between treatments; therefore, greater
  total glucose AUC reduction with tirzepatide was mainly attributable
  to greater suppression of FASTING glucose"** [emphasis mine] --
  i.e., tirzepatide's real clinical advantage over a GLP-1-alone
  agonist (already modeled, `GLP1Pathway`) is substantially a
  BASAL/fasting-state effect, not an amplified postprandial incretin
  effect. Also confirmed: ISR7.2 (insulin secretion rate at a
  glucose-clamped 7.2 mmol/L reference point) significantly higher with
  tirzepatide vs. semaglutide (P<.05, a genuine beta-cell-glucose-
  sensitivity enhancement), and both fasting and total glucagon AUC
  more strongly suppressed with tirzepatide (P<.01 vs. semaglutide).

**The scoping question row 1.5 explicitly asked, answered with real
evidence rather than assumed**: representing tirzepatide as simply
"`GLP1Pathway` with a stronger `agonist_scale`" (the simplest possible
design, and the one a hasty implementation would likely reach for)
would be WRONG, not just imprecise -- `GLP1Pathway`'s existing two
signals (`incretin_effect`, `gastric_emptying_modifier`) are BOTH
postprandial-acting mechanisms, and the paper's own explicit statement
above says tirzepatide's real advantage over semaglutide is NOT in the
postprandial/incremental component at all (which "did not differ
significantly" between the two drugs) -- it's the FASTING component
that's genuinely different. A stronger-agonist_scale-only
implementation would amplify exactly the mechanism (postprandial) the
primary literature says is NOT where the real difference lies, while
leaving out the one (fasting) that is.

**This connects directly to, and is now doubly motivated by, this
session's own earlier glucagon-EGP investigation (MASTER_PLAN 1.1)**:
that investigation found a real, qualitative fasting-glucagon-
suppression-lowers-EGP mechanism (Liljenquist et al. 1977, PMID:833282)
but explicitly could not find a small-perturbation (10-20%) dose-
response coefficient to quantify it -- recorded as permanently blocked
for that reason. Tirzepatide's own real fasting-glucose/glucagon
advantage over semaglutide runs through the SAME underlying mechanism
class (fasting glucagon suppression -> reduced hepatic glucose
production), so the identical blocker applies here: even having decided
the RIGHT architectural shape (a distinct, fasting/basal Gb-lowering
component, analogous to metformin's own static `Gb` modifier -- NOT a
postprandial `GLP1Pathway`-style coupling), a specific numeric
calibration for how much tirzepatide's basal glucagon suppression
translates into a fasting glucose reduction is not yet available from
what's been found.

**Confirmed via direct Europe PMC full-text lookup that both key
papers are paywalled** (`fetch_full_text=True` returned 0-length full
text for both PMID:35468322 and PMID:38795393 -- Lancet Diabetes
Endocrinol and JCEM, both subscription-gated), so the exact tabulated
fasting-glucose-vs-placebo reduction magnitude (which likely exists in
a results table, given the abstract's own qualitative claim) could not
be extracted this pass. Two further targeted searches ("tirzepatide
fasting glucose placebo phase 1 dose response healthy", "tirzepatide
glucagon suppression fasting placebo controlled") did not surface a
different, openly-accessible primary source with the specific number
either.

**Decision, per this project's own established discipline**: NOT
implemented this pass -- inventing a fasting-Gb-reduction magnitude
without a real number would repeat the exact unsupported-precision
anti-pattern already rejected three times this session (glucagon,
sulfonylurea, acarbose-GI). This is recorded as a genuine scoping
outcome, not a negative result: the mechanism DECISION is real,
evidence-based, and settled (distinct fasting/basal component, not a
stronger `GLP1Pathway` agonist_scale) -- what remains is purely
acquiring the calibration number, either via full-text access to one
of these two papers (through a library/institutional route not
available to this session) or a different, open-access primary source
reporting the same fasting-glucose-vs-placebo comparison.

**A second, real, decided sub-question**: the ISR7.2/beta-cell-glucose-
sensitivity enhancement (a genuine, well-evidenced, POSTPRANDIAL-
compatible finding, P<.05 vs. semaglutide) DOES fit naturally as a
stronger `incretin_effect` via the EXISTING `GLP1Pathway` machinery
(reusing, not replacing, the architecture already built for GLP-1
agonists) -- this piece of tirzepatide's real mechanism has no
architectural blocker at all, only needs its own quantitative
calibration (also not yet extracted from the paywalled full text).

### DONE — Acarbose's effect now scales with meal substrate composition, not applied unconditionally to every meal (Track 1, MASTER_PLAN 1.4b(iii))

Picked via the standing autonomous-loop process -- a genuine
engineering task with no literature-search risk, deliberately chosen
to break the recent run of research-heavy cycles (glucagon, sulfonylurea,
acarbose-GI, tirzepatide) that each ended blocked or scoping-only.

**The gap**: the original acarbose milestone applied its full,
literature-calibrated `kabs` reduction to EVERY non-GI-routed meal
unconditionally, regardless of what the meal was actually made of.
Alpha-glucosidase inhibitors mechanistically act on the ENZYMATIC
DIGESTION step (breaking starch/disaccharides into absorbable
monosaccharides) -- a meal that's mostly free glucose/fructose (fruit
juice, soda, candy) needs no such digestion step at all, so acarbose
should have little-to-no effect on it, but the platform applied the
drug's FULL modelled effect regardless. This was already flagged as a
real, disclosed gap in the original milestone (only coincidentally not
yet live-triggered, since the one flagship pure-sugar scenario happens
to be GI-routed for an unrelated reason, which independently exempts it
from the kabs mechanism entirely).

**Design**: added `MealEvent.complex_carb_fraction: float = 1.0` (the
fraction of a meal's carbohydrate requiring enzymatic digestion --
starches/disaccharides -- vs. free monosaccharides that absorb
directly). Default 1.0 preserves the original milestone's own
unconditional-full-effect behaviour EXACTLY for every existing
scenario (verified with a dedicated regression test comparing the
default against an explicit `complex_carb_fraction=1.0`, byte-for-
byte). `runner.py`'s acarbose block now computes a PER-MEAL effective
scale: `effective_scale = 1.0 - (1.0 - dose_kabs_scale) *
complex_carb_fraction` -- at fraction=1.0 this reduces to exactly the
original dose-dependent scale (`acarbose_kabs_scale(dose_mg)`,
unchanged); at fraction=0.0 it's exactly 1.0 (no effect at all,
confirmed byte-identical to a no-drug baseline, not just a smaller
effect); intermediate fractions interpolate linearly and were verified
to produce a genuinely monotonic, intermediate effect (a half-free-
sugar/half-starch meal shows less effect than fully-starch, more than
fully-free-sugar).

**Wired through every layer this session has already established the
convention for** (matching `glycaemic_index`/`kabs`'s own prior
extension exactly, confirmed via a full repo-wide grep that these are
the only 4 sites needing the same treatment): `MealEventIn`'s REST wire
schema (`Field(default=1.0, ge=0.0, le=1.0)`), `scenario_in_to_definition()`'s
translation layer, `ScenarioDefinition.to_dict()` (needed for
`SimulationCache`'s own key correctness -- otherwise two scenarios
differing only in this field would silently collide in the cache,
the exact bug class already fixed once this session for other
`MealEvent`/`DrugEvent` fields), and `MealEvent.__post_init__`'s bounds
validation (`0.0 <= complex_carb_fraction <= 1.0`, verified this chained
comparison correctly rejects NaN and +/-inf, not just out-of-range
values -- confirmed directly rather than assumed, given this project's
own history of NaN-comparison bugs with bare `<`/`>` checks).

**Review-process note, said honestly**: both mandatory review agents
remain in the confirmed weekly quota outage from earlier this session
(resets Aug 8) -- did not re-attempt dispatching either agent (retrying
into a confirmed weekly, not session-level, limit within the same
session would almost certainly fail identically). Performed the
equivalent verification directly: confirmed via `grep` that the same 4
call sites already established for `glycaemic_index`/`kabs` are the
complete set needing this same treatment (no `from_dict()` exists to
also update -- `to_dict()` is one-directional, used for cache-key/
archiving purposes only); confirmed the effective-scale formula's two
boundary cases algebraically and numerically; confirmed no double-
counting or interaction risk (this only rescales an existing scalar
per-meal, no new pathway/signal); confirmed the REST `Field` bounds
match the internal dataclass validation exactly.

+6 tests: 4 in `test_simulation_api.py` (free-sugar meal genuinely
unaffected -- byte-identical to no-drug, not just smaller; a partial
fraction produces a genuinely intermediate, monotonic effect; the
default reproduces the exact pre-existing full effect; out-of-bounds/
NaN values raise), 1 in `test_rest_api.py` (the new field reaches the
acarbose scaling through the real REST route, not just the internal
path), 1 in `test_infrastructure.py` (`SimulationCache` no longer
collides two scenarios differing only in this field). RED-proofed via
a scoped `git stash` on the 4 modified source files (kept the 3

(the new field's default preserves every existing scenario's exact

### DONE — Type 1 diabetes disease-state preset (Track 1, MASTER_PLAN 1.10)

Both prerequisites (1.2a exogenous insulin, 1.2c near-total-beta-cell-
failure fixed-point verification) were already done; this chunk
supplied the piece 1.2c's own investigation deliberately left open: a
real, literature-anchored `DiseaseState.TYPE_1_DIABETES` preset in
`physiology/modifiers.py`, rather than the illustrative-only values
that verification used.

**Literature, verified live via `PubMedFetcher`** (a fresh search angle
after 1.2c's own attempt didn't converge): **Simonson DC, Delprato S,
Castellino P, Groop L, DeFronzo RA. "Effect of glyburide on glycemic
control, insulin requirement, and glucose metabolism in insulin-treated
diabetic patients." Diabetes. 1987;36(2):136-46. PMID:3100365.** n=5
confirmed IDDM (T1D) patients on chronic exogenous insulin
(54+/-8 U/day): "C-peptide levels were undetectable (less than
0.01 pmol/ml) in the basal state and after glucagon [stimulation]...
remained undetectable after glyburide therapy" -- genuinely
unresponsive to a secretagogue, confirming near-total (not merely
reduced) beta-cell failure. Corroborated by the broader residual-
beta-cell-function literature also found this pass (Kalinowska et al.
2017, PMID:29253033; PMID:35181926; both independently verified live):
most confirmed long-duration T1D patients sit at or below C-peptide
assay detection limits, though a minority retain measurable residual
secretion -- this preset represents the modal, near-total (not
absolute-zero) case.

**Design**: `Ib`/`secretion_scale` factors (0.05, 0.02) are chosen so
that after `PhysiologicalPersonalizer`'s existing `_PARAM_BOUNDS` clamp
they land exactly at the model's own engineering floors (10.0 pM /
0.05) -- treating that floor as the operational proxy for "at or below
assay detection," not a precise measured plasma insulin concentration
(C-peptide and insulin are co-secreted equimolarly but cleared at
different rates, so no direct unit substitution was attempted). `Gb`
(2.2, giving 11.0 mM) is explicitly disclosed as an ENGINEERING CHOICE,
not literature-anchored to a specific citation -- a dedicated search
for a clean untreated-T1D fasting-glucose consensus number did not
converge (matching 1.2c's own earlier experience). Chosen to clearly
exceed `BRUNZELL_AIR_ABSENT_THRESHOLD_MM` (~6.39 mM) so the EXISTING
first_phase_gain-zeroing gate (added for T2D) fires automatically, with
no new special-casing -- and to be well above T2D's own 6.5 mM
(reflecting more severe, total insulin deficiency) while staying safely
within the `Gb` ceiling. Weak corroborating context: Simonson's own
cohort ran ~9.83 mM even ON substantial exogenous insulin.

Added a `PhysiologicalProfile.__post_init__` mutual-exclusivity check
(TYPE_1_DIABETES cannot combine with TYPE_2_DIABETES/INSULIN_RESISTANT
-- opposite beta-cell mechanisms), mirroring the existing HYPO/
HYPERTHYROIDISM convention.

**Verified**: `validate_y0(tolerance=1e-8)` returns `[]` for the real
preset (not just the illustrative values), confirming `basal_state()`'s
existing generalization holds; an end-to-end `SimulationRunner` test
confirms near-zero endogenous insulin response without a dose and a
genuine, substantial restoration with a 6U `insulin_regular` event
(mirroring 1.2c's manual finding, now automated against the real named
preset). All 6 registered clinical benchmarks confirmed byte-identical
(none use T1D).

**Mandatory code-reviewer and security-reviewer passes both ran
successfully** (first time since the confirmed weekly quota outage
reset -- both worked cleanly). Code-reviewer: 0 CRITICAL/HIGH, one real
MEDIUM (a correct PMID with a mismatched author name, "Bogun" instead
of the paper's actual "Kalinowska") and one LOW (a page-range typo,
136-43 vs. the real 136-46) -- both were citation-comment errors,
fixed. Security-reviewer found one real MEDIUM: `glucose_independent_
secretion_pM_per_min()` (the sulfonylurea/glibenclamide mechanism)
depends only on `ke`/`Ib`, never `secretion_scale` -- deliberately,
since KATP-channel closure is glucose-independent, not beta-cell-mass-
independent -- so composing a sulfonylurea with a T1D profile silently
produced a real, nonzero (~50%-of-floor) insulin rise from a drug that
clinically requires substantial functional beta-cell mass and is not
prescribed in confirmed T1D. Verified directly (reproduced the exact
0.465 pM/min value) before fixing: rather than retune the formula to
scale by `secretion_scale` (which would also change T2D's own,
already-calibrated-against-Riefflin-et-al.-2015 effect size), the
override -- and its audit-trail entry -- is now skipped specifically
when `TYPE_1_DIABETES` is present, the narrower fix the review itself
offered as sufficient. Added a paired regression test confirming T2D's
own effect is completely unaffected (guards against the T1D exclusion
becoming a blanket "any diabetes" one). RED-proofed via a scoped
`git stash` on `personalizer.py` alone -- reproduced the exact 0.465
value pre-fix, confirmed 0.0 post-fix.

### DONE — Miglitol, the second alpha-glucosidase inhibitor (Track 1, MASTER_PLAN 1.4b(ii))

Fresh literature search after the original acarbose milestone deferred
this drug ("wasn't this session's literature focus"). Same mass-
conserving `MealInput.kabs`-reduction mechanism as acarbose (already
verified mechanistically correct -- reducing the absorption RATE
CONSTANT preserves total carbohydrate mass exactly), calibrated
against its own, separate real citation.

**Literature, verified live via NCBI efetch**: **Samad AH, Ty Willing
TS, Alberti KG, Taylor R. "Effects of BAYm 1099, new alpha-glucosidase
inhibitor, on acute metabolic responses and metabolic control in NIDDM
over 1 mo." Diabetes Care. 1988;11(2):100-9. PMID:3042310.** BAYm 1099
confirmed to be miglitol's own original development code (cross-
checked against PMID:9540024: "the alpha-glucosidase inhibitor
miglitol (BAY m 1099)"). n=12 diet-treated NIDDM (T2D) patients
completing a double-blind, placebo-controlled crossover: 4 weeks
miglitol 50mg TID vs. 4 weeks placebo, test meals during the last week
of each phase. For a 25g pure-sucrose test meal (the purest, most
demanding substrate -- no starch-digestion component at all): peak
glucose **11.3 +/- 1.0 mM (drug) vs. 14.3 +/- 1.4 mM (placebo),
P<0.001 -- a -21.0% peak-height reduction**. "Peak blood glucose
levels were significantly delayed" is stated qualitatively, with no
reported ratio -- unlike acarbose's own Chen et al. 2016 calibration
(a genuine two-number cross-check), this is a single-quantity anchor.
`MIGLITOL_50MG_KABS_SCALE = 0.1446` reproduces the peak-height number
exactly through this platform's own ODE model for a matching 25g
sucrose meal; the resulting ~2.05x peak-time delay is a mechanical
CONSEQUENCE of the mass-conserving mechanism, disclosed explicitly as
NOT independently verified against a real timing figure (unlike
acarbose's confirmed 1.51x-vs-1.5x match).

No miglitol dose-ranging study reporting an acute, single-dose,
peak-height-comparable magnitude was found (PMID:9540024's 50-200mg
TID dose-ranging reports only 1-year HbA1c/fasting-glucose endpoints,
a chronic, different metric) -- `miglitol_kabs_scale()` is therefore a
step function capped at the single verified 50mg reference dose (with
linear interpolation below it), deliberately narrower in scope than
`acarbose_kabs_scale()`'s own continuous log-dose curve, rather than
reusing acarbose's unrelated dose-response shape with no miglitol-
specific data to justify it.

**Found and fixed a real, previously-latent dispatch bug while wiring
this in**: `SimulationRunner.run()`'s alpha-glucosidase-inhibitor block
unconditionally called `acarbose_kabs_scale()` for ANY drug in
`ALPHA_GLUCOSIDASE_INHIBITOR_DRUGS` -- harmless before this milestone
(that set had exactly one member), but would have silently applied
acarbose's calibration to a miglitol dose. Fixed with a per-drug
dispatch dict (`_AGI_KABS_SCALE_FUNCTIONS`), verified end-to-end that
acarbose and miglitol produce genuinely different simulated peaks for
the same dose.

**Mandatory code-reviewer and security-reviewer passes both ran
successfully**, both APPROVE with real, actionable coverage gaps (no
functional defects) -- all fixed before considering this done:
- A real, if currently latent, drift risk: `_AGI_KABS_SCALE_FUNCTIONS`
  (runner.py) and `ALPHA_GLUCOSIDASE_INHIBITOR_DRUGS`
  (drug_interactions.py) are two independently-written sets that could
  desync if a third AGI drug is ever added to one without the other,
  producing an uncaught `KeyError`. Rather than restructure this
  file's established local-import layering (biosim_physiology imports
  are deliberately kept inside methods throughout, not at module
  level) just to expose the dict for direct introspection, added a
  behavioral regression test that runs every drug in
  `ALPHA_GLUCOSIDASE_INHIBITOR_DRUGS` through a real `SimulationRunner`
  scenario -- a desync would surface as an immediate test failure
  (the KeyError itself), not silently.
- No test exercised a scenario with BOTH acarbose and miglitol present
  together, nor confirmed `complex_carb_fraction` scaling (MASTER_PLAN

  acarbose (the underlying mechanism is drug-agnostic by construction,
  confirmed by reading `runner.py`'s `effective_scale` formula, but
  untested for this drug). Added both.
- Added a "first AGI wins" disclosure comment to the dispatch block,
  matching the established convention already documented for
  `_detect_glp1()`/`_detect_renal()`/`_detect_exogenous_insulin()`

- Cleaned up two validation assertions that had been left in the wrong

### DONE (partial) — Gestational diabetes disease-state preset (Track 1, MASTER_PLAN 1.11)

Row 1.11 named two new disease states (gestational diabetes, MODY);
this entry covers gestational diabetes only -- MODY needs a new
enzyme-activity parameter this model doesn't currently expose and is
left open. Scoped gestational diabetes first since it fits the
existing static-modifier architecture (Gb/p1/p3/secretion_scale, same
as T2D/insulin-resistant/hypothyroidism), unlike MODY.

**A genuine design question, worked through carefully before picking
any numbers**: unlike every other disease state in this file, this
platform has no "pregnant, not diabetic" baseline to layer a GDM-
specific delta on top of. Confirmed this matters, not just in theory:
normal (non-diabetic) pregnancy itself causes major insulin resistance
relative to a non-pregnant reference -- so a preset built only from a
"GDM vs. matched pregnant controls" study would be missing pregnancy's
own large contribution, understating the true difference from this
model's own non-pregnant default. Resolved by finding a single study
that measures GDM against a TRUE non-pregnant reference directly, and
folding BOTH pregnancy's own shift and GDM's additional decompensation
into ONE preset (matching every other disease state's own "one preset,
no intermediate baseline" convention) -- documented explicitly in both
`modifiers.py`'s citation comment and, per the mandatory code-reviewer
pass's own finding, a pointer comment on the `DiseaseState.
GESTATIONAL_DIABETES` enum value itself, so a future maintainer working
from `profile.py` alone doesn't miss this and risk double-counting
pregnancy's own effect if a separate "pregnant, NGT" state is ever
added later.

**Literature, verified live via PubMedFetcher and Europe PMC full
text**: **Kautzky-Willer A, Prager R, Waldhausl W, Pacini G, Thomaseth
K, Wagner OF, Ulm M, Streli C, Ludvik B. "Pronounced insulin resistance
and inadequate beta-cell secretion characterize lean gestational
diabetes during and after pregnancy." Diabetes Care. 1997;20(11):
1717-23. PMID:9353615.** Mathematical minimal-model kinetic analysis
(the same modelling tradition Pacini's own co-authorship already
anchors this platform's p2/KG_secretion-adjacent parameters to)
comparing lean GDM, lean pregnant women with normal glucose tolerance
(NGT), and healthy nonpregnant lean women: "S1 [insulin sensitivity]
was blunted in pregnant women with GDM by 84%... and in those with NGT
by 66% compared with lean nonpregnant women" (confirming the pregnancy-
itself contribution is real and large, with GDM adding a further,
quantified decompensation on top); "glucose effectiveness was decreased
by 33% in both pregnant groups... vs. healthy nonpregnant lean control
subjects" (a pregnancy effect, not GDM-specific, folded in for the same
reason); "insulin secretion was 30% higher... in subjects with GDM than
in pregnant women with NGT or in nonpregnant lean women" (real,
measured compensatory hypersecretion, same shape as INSULIN_RESISTANT's
own secretion_scale=1.05, just independently anchored here). `Gb` is
anchored to a SEPARATE citation, since this paper reports sensitivity/
secretion percentages, not a fasting glucose value: **Metzger BE et al.
(IADPSG Consensus Panel). "International Association of Diabetes and
Pregnancy Study Groups recommendations on the diagnosis and
classification of hyperglycemia in pregnancy." Diabetes Care.
2010;33(3):676-82. PMID:20190296** -- full text (fetched live, since
the abstract itself is empty for this consensus-panel report) confirms
verbatim: "fasting plasma glucose >=5.1 mmol/l (92 mg/dl)... diagnose
as GDM." Preset: `{"p1": 0.67, "p3": 0.16, "secretion_scale": 1.30,
"Gb": 1.02}` (Gb factor gives exactly 5.0*1.02=5.1 mM).

**Mutual exclusivity, deliberately asymmetric vs. the T1D precedent**:
`GESTATIONAL_DIABETES` cannot combine with `TYPE_1_DIABETES`/
`TYPE_2_DIABETES` (pre-existing diabetes in pregnancy is "pregestational
diabetes," a distinct clinical entity this platform doesn't model) but
CAN combine with `INSULIN_RESISTANT` (a real, common GDM risk factor,
not a contradictory diagnosis, unlike T1D's own opposite-mechanism
exclusion of it) -- confirmed by the mandatory code-reviewer pass as a
deliberate, well-justified distinction, not an inconsistency.

### DONE — GCK-MODY (glucokinase-gene MODY) disease-state preset (Track 1, MASTER_PLAN 1.11, completes the row)

Completes row 1.11 -- gestational diabetes was done in the prior
commit; this covers MODY, specifically the GCK subtype (MODY2), not
generic MODY. **First correction made before any literature search**:
the row's own prior text ("would need a new PathwayParameters field")
was checked against the current code rather than trusted -- `KG_secretion`
is already a real `PathwayParameters` field (`pathway.py`, used in
`F_secretion_basal`), and `G_threshold` is already personalizable via
`_PARAM_BOUNDS`. No new field was actually needed; the original scoping
note was an unverified assumption from an earlier session, now corrected.

**Mechanism, verified before picking a design**: glucokinase (GCK) is
the beta cell's own glucose SENSOR -- a heterozygous inactivating
mutation resets the glucose set-point upward WITHOUT reducing maximal
secretory capacity or peripheral insulin sensitivity. Mechanistically
the OPPOSITE shape from every other diabetes-related state in this
file (T1D = secretion loss; T2D/GDM/INSULIN_RESISTANT = resistance with
partial/compensatory secretion) -- a pure threshold reset with
everything else intact, matching this condition's real clinical
reputation as mild, stable, and rarely treated.

**Literature, verified live via PubMedFetcher**: **Guenat E, Seematter
G, Philippe J, Temler E, Jequier E, Tappy L. "Counterregulatory
responses to hypoglycemia in patients with glucokinase gene mutations."
Diabetes Metab. 2000;26(5):377-84. PMID:11119017.** n=7 confirmed
GCK-MODY, n=5 T2D, n=13 healthy, hyperinsulinaemic clamp with
progressive hypoglycaemia (small but real, controlled, directly-
measured -- the standard evidence base for this rare population, same
category as the small "lean GDM" cohort already cited this session).
Confirmed verbatim: "Basal glucose concentrations were significantly
higher in MODY2 patients (7.6 +/- 0.4 mmol/l)... than in healthy
subjects (5.3 +/- 0.1 mmol/l, P<0.01)" -- `Gb` factor is this
within-study ratio (7.6/5.3=1.434), applied to this platform's own
default (5.0*1.434=7.17 mM), same convention as every other preset.
Critically, the SAME paper directly confirms (not merely omits) that
p1/p3 must stay unchanged: "Insulin-mediated glucose disposal and
suppression of endogenous glucose production at euglycemia were
unchanged in MODY2 patients, but were blunted in type 2 diabetes" --
a real, measured null result, directly contrasted against T2D in the
SAME cohort. `secretion_scale` is also left untouched (no citation
found or expected for a genuine capacity change); PMID:36342518 (a
dorzagliatin/GCK-MODY clamp study, verified live) independently
corroborates the "rightward-shifted response curve, not reduced
capacity" shape. Preset: `{"Gb": 7.6/5.3}` -- p1/p3/secretion_scale
deliberately ABSENT from the dict (not set to 1.0); verified this is
provably equivalent to an explicit 1.0 in every composition case by
reading `compose_all_modifiers()`'s actual fold logic directly
(`combined.get(param, 1.0) * factor` -- a key absent from one dict
simply never participates in that dict's multiplication pass,
regardless of what other active modifiers do to that same key) and by
constructing GCK_MODY+GESTATIONAL_DIABETES together and confirming p1/
p3/secretion_scale end up exactly at GDM's own values with zero
influence from GCK_MODY.

**Honestly disclosed, unresolved uncertainty, left as-is rather than
silently accepted or silently overridden**: this Gb value (7.17 mM)
exceeds `BRUNZELL_AIR_ABSENT_THRESHOLD_MM` (~6.39 mM), so the existing,
generic, glucose-level-keyed gate (added for T2D, Brunzell et al. 1976)
fires and zeroes `first_phase_gain` for this preset too. No citation
was found confirming this generalizes correctly to GCK-MODY's own
threshold-reset mechanism (as opposed to T1D's genuine secretion loss,
the population Brunzell's finding is best-supported for) -- the source
above addresses hypoglycaemic counter-regulation, not hyperglycaemic
first-phase secretion, in this population. Left the existing rule
firing uniformly (documented and tested as CURRENT behaviour, not
asserted as correct) rather than inventing an unsupported carve-out for
one disease state.

**Mutual exclusivity**: `GCK_MODY` cannot combine with `TYPE_1_DIABETES`/
`TYPE_2_DIABETES` (distinct clinical diagnoses) but CAN combine with
`INSULIN_RESISTANT` and `GESTATIONAL_DIABETES` (independent mechanisms,
not contradictory -- a GCK-MODY carrier can develop unrelated insulin
resistance or become pregnant).

### DONE — Fixed `ParameterStore.query()`/`.best()`'s tie-order bug (Track 3, MASTER_PLAN 3.1)

Track 1 is now exhausted (see the entry directly above); moved to
Track 3's lowest-numbered open, unblocked chunk -- this one explicitly
flagged in an earlier session's own scoping as "No Docker needed."

**Background**: an earlier session fixed `get_all_for_subject()` to
break ties via an explicit `self._insertion_seq` monotonic counter
(mirroring Postgres's `seq bigint GENERATED ALWAYS AS IDENTITY`) rather
than relying on `_subject_kind_index`'s own list order. At the time, a
comment claimed `query()`/`best()` did NOT need the same fix ("within
one index key the id list is already a subsequence of insertion
order"). Checked that claim directly rather than trusting it -- it's
true for the in-memory `add()`-only path, but FALSE the moment a store
is round-tripped through `save()`/`load()` with a "parameters" JSON
array that isn't in true seq order (a hand-edited snapshot, a merge of
two partial exports, a future non-Python writer -- `load()`'s own
docstring already anticipates exactly this): `load()` appends to
`_subject_kind_index` in ARRAY order, not seq order, silently desyncing
`query()`/`best()` from the already-fixed `get_all_for_subject()`.

**Reproduced directly before writing any fix**: built two tied-priority
parameters (same confidence/organism/system) added A-then-B, saved,
reversed the JSON array while leaving each parameter's own persisted
`seq` untouched, reloaded -- `query()[0]`/`best()` returned B (array
order, wrong) while `get_all_for_subject()` correctly still returned A
(seq order). `best()` is "the primary method used by the ODE engine to
look up parameters" per its own docstring -- a higher-stakes
inconsistency than the one already fixed for `get_all_for_subject()`
alone, even though not yet reachable by any current production caller
(no shipped code reorders a snapshot's array today).

**Fix**: `query()`'s final sort now uses the same negate-and-sort-
ascending pattern as `get_all_for_subject()`, with
`self._insertion_seq[p.parameter_id]` as an explicit final tiebreak,
replacing the old `sorted(results, key=self._priority_score,
reverse=True)`. Verified the new sort key is ordering-equivalent to the
old one for every non-tie case (negating each rank component and
sorting ascending is algebraically identical to sorting descending on
the un-negated components -- tuple comparison short-circuits on the
first differing element, so the new `seq` component can only ever
matter when the first three are already exactly equal). The now-dead
`_priority_score()` helper (confirmed via repo-wide grep to have no
other callers anywhere) was deleted rather than left as unreferenced
code. Corrected the misleading `__init__` comment on `_insertion_seq`
that used to claim this fix wasn't needed.

+1 test (`test_query_and_best_use_seq_not_array_order_after_a_reordered_
snapshot`, `TestPersistence`, immediately after the sibling
`test_insertion_seq_persists_and_survives_reload`): reproduces the
exact scenario above, asserting `query()`'s full returned order and
`best()`'s result both match `get_all_for_subject()`'s already-correct
order (`[id_a, id_b]`), not the reordered array's order. RED-proofed via
a scoped `git stash` on `store.py` alone -- failed with the exact
predicted mismatch (`best()`/`query()` returning B, not A) pre-fix.
Full suite: 1742 -> 1743 passed, 2 skipped. All 6 clinical benchmarks
confirmed byte-identical (pure parameter-database tie-breaking fix, no
drug/dosage/physiology/calculation code touched).

**Review-process note**: this doesn't touch drug/dosage/physiology/
genetics/calculation code, so only the mandatory code-reviewer pass
applied (no security-reviewer trigger) -- ran successfully, APPROVE, 0
CRITICAL/HIGH/MEDIUM. Independently re-derived the sort-key equivalence
algebraically, independently RED/GREEN-proved the regression test,
independently re-ran the full suite and all 6 clinical benchmarks, and
confirmed `_priority_score()`'s deletion has no other callers anywhere
in the repo. Two LOW notes, both addressed before finalizing: the new
test only asserted `query()[0]`, not the full order (strengthened to
assert `[id_a, id_b]` exactly, closing a real ruff F841 unused-variable
warning on `id_b` in the process); this DONE entry and the
MASTER_PLAN.md row were still pending at review time (added now).

### DONE — Wired `CouplingSpec.validate()` into `CompositePathway.__init__` (Track 3, MASTER_PLAN 3.2)

`CouplingSpec.validate()` (checking source/target pathway registration,
no self-coupling, the source signal is actually exported, the target
input is actually accepted) has existed since its own earlier
regression fix, but was never actually CALLED anywhere in production --
a typo'd `signal_name`/`target_input` in any pathway-extension wiring
silently composed into an inert, zero-effect coupling with no error at
all. This is exactly KNOWN BUGS #7's own class of defect (an entire
earlier session was lost tracking down a silently-inert
`CompositePathway` coupling). Wired `validate()` into
`CompositePathway.__init__` so this now fails fast at construction,
matching this project's established convention for catching a
programmer error at the earliest point (`DrugEvent.__post_init__`, the
disease-state exclusivity checks, etc.).

**Systematic sweep performed before wiring anything in** (not just
trusting the existing couplings would pass): checked every real
`*_couplings()` function's `target_input` against its target pathway's
declared `descriptor.input_signals`, and every `signal_name` against its
source pathway's declared `descriptor.output_signals`, across all 8
extension pathways (cortisol, hepatic, nefa, glp1, exercise, renal,
exogenous-insulin, meal-absorption). Found exactly one real gap:
`MealAbsorptionPathway`'s `meal_absorption_couplings()` targets a
genuinely dynamic, one-per-meal signal name
(`meal0_remaining_mM`, `meal1_remaining_mM`, ...) that
`GlucoseInsulinPathway`'s static `input_signals` list can't enumerate
(a scenario's meal count is unbounded). Fixed by adding `fnmatch`-based
wildcard support to `CouplingSpec.validate()` (a `target_inputs` entry
containing `*` is glob-matched; a plain equality check runs first so
ordinary non-wildcard names stay an exact match) and a new
`"meal*_remaining_mM"` wildcard entry to GI's own `input_signals`.
Also fixed, while auditing this area: a stale docstring example in
`HepGlucPathway`'s class docstring (`target_input="hepatic_egp"`,
missing the `_delta` suffix `hepatic_couplings()` actually uses) --
documentation only, never executable.

**Verified this doesn't break any real composition** -- the full suite
initially surfaced 19 failures + 13 errors on first wiring this in
(every scenario composing GLP1+meal-absorption, since the wildcard
entry hadn't landed yet, plus 4 synthetic test-double failures whose
own descriptors declared `input_signals=[]` -- correct for testing
`CompositePathway`'s signal-*accumulation* mechanism generically, not
real pathway-contract validation, a different concern this milestone
adds). Fixed by giving `_RecordingTargetPathway` (the test double) a
wildcard `input_signals=["*"]` and updating one test's locked-in
expected-signal-set to include the new wildcard entry. Final state: the
exact same 6 registered clinical benchmarks pass, byte-identical.

**Mandatory code-reviewer and security-reviewer passes both ran
successfully**, both APPROVE overall. Security-reviewer: 0 CRITICAL/
HIGH/MEDIUM -- independently composed all 9 production pathways
simultaneously (a maximal T2D+metformin+stress+exercise+semaglutide+
dapagliflozin+exogenous-insulin scenario) and confirmed no false-
positive validation failure; confirmed every `CouplingSpec(` call site
in the codebase uses only hardcoded literals/`.name` properties, never
user/REST input, so the new `fnmatch` wildcard support introduces no
injection surface. Code-reviewer: APPROVE with one real MEDIUM, fixed
before finalizing -- `fnmatch.fnmatch()` normalizes both operands via
`os.path.normcase()` first, which lowercases on Windows but is a no-op
on POSIX, so a case-mismatched typo against the wildcard entry (e.g.
`"Meal0_remaining_mM"`) would have silently PASSED validation on a
Windows dev machine while correctly failing on Linux CI/production --
exactly the class of typo this milestone exists to catch, made
platform-dependent instead of deterministic. Fixed with
`fnmatch.fnmatchcase()` (always case-sensitive regardless of OS),
RED-proofed directly on this Windows environment (confirmed the new
case-sensitivity test genuinely fails with plain `fnmatch.fnmatch()`
here, reproducing the reviewer's exact prediction, before restoring
`fnmatchcase()`).

+6 tests in a new `TestCompositePathwayCouplingValidation` class
(`test_pathway_expansion.py`): a typo'd target_input/signal_name/
pathway-name each raise a `ValueError` at construction naming the exact
typo'd string, the meal-absorption wildcard coupling does NOT raise,
the case-sensitivity fix (found by review), and every one of the 8
real production extension pathways composes with GI without raising.
RED-proofed via a scoped `git stash` -- the 3 core "did this catch a

### DONE — Fixed `IDRegistry.from_mapping_files()`'s transitive-merge-history loss (Track 3, MASTER_PLAN 3.3)

An earlier session fixed `IDRegistry.to_dict()`/`from_dict()` so a
transitive merge chain (entity A deprecated into B, then B itself later
deprecated into C) survives a full serialization round trip -- by
serializing the registry's raw, flat `_deprecated_index` directly
(each surviving record's own `deprecated_canonical_ids` only captures
its OWN one-hop deprecation; C's record lists only `[B]`, never `[A]`,
since A's hop only ever lived on B's now-removed record) and restoring
it via `.update()` after `from_dict()`'s main registration loop.

`IDRegistry.from_mapping_files()` -- described in the class's own
module docstring and inline comments as "the class's own documented
PRODUCTION deserialization entry point," alongside `from_dict()` --
never got the equivalent fix. It only ever reconstructed the one-hop
deprecations via `register()`'s own restoration, so a transitive chain
loaded through THIS entry point (rather than `from_dict()`) silently
lost the A->B hop: A became permanently unresolvable (`ResolutionError:
No record found`), with no reference to C or the live migration path
at all, even though a real one exists.

**Fix**: `from_mapping_files()`'s per-file loop (it iterates multiple
JSON files in a directory, one per entity type) now calls
`registry._deprecated_index.update(data.get("deprecated_index", {}))`
after registering that file's own records, mirroring `from_dict()`'s
equivalent step -- accumulating additively across the whole directory
rather than the last file processed silently discarding others'.
Docstring updated to document the new key as OPTIONAL (a mapping file
without it still loads correctly, just without the deeper chain
history restored -- the same graceful-degradation convention
`from_dict()` already established).

+2 tests in `TestSerialization` (`test_resolver.py`), next to the
existing `test_from_mapping_files`:
`test_transitive_merge_chain_survives_mapping_files_roundtrip` (mirrors
`TestDeprecation`'s existing `from_dict()`-focused chain test, but
through `from_mapping_files()`) and
`test_from_mapping_files_without_deprecated_index_key_still_loads` (a
pure backward-compatibility check, explicitly labeled as such -- it
passes identically before and after this fix, since pre-fix code never
looks for the key at all). RED-proofed the first test via a scoped
`git stash` on `registry.py` alone -- confirmed it fails pre-fix with
`get_record(a)` raising `ResolutionError: No record found for canonical
ID ...` (A absent from the reloaded registry's deprecation index
entirely, not merely pointing at a stale intermediate id -- a small
wording correction from this entry's own first draft, caught by the
mandatory code-reviewer pass, which independently traced the exact
`_deprecated_index` contents by hand before and after the fix).

Full suite: 1749 -> 1751 passed, 2 skipped. All 6 clinical benchmarks
unaffected (pure id-resolver data-layer fix, no drug/dosage/physiology
code touched -- only the mandatory code-reviewer pass applied, APPROVE,
0 CRITICAL/HIGH/MEDIUM).

### DONE — Wired `_compute_lay_summary()` to actually read `UQResult` (Track 2, MASTER_PLAN 2.1)

`SimulationRunner._compute_lay_summary()` accepted a `uq` parameter (the
optional Monte Carlo `UQResult`, populated only when
`ScenarioDefinition.run_uncertainty=True`) but never read it --
`LaySummary.confidence_note`/`is_high_confidence` were derived solely
from the point-estimate Boolean watchdog score
(`metrics.overall_watchdog_confidence >= 0.8`), structurally blind to
whether the UQ ensemble itself showed a high sample-failure rate or wide
confidence bands under real parameter uncertainty. `uq` had been an
accepted-but-unused parameter here since before this project's own
uncertainty-package overhaul (Bayesian calibration, the
`pathway_factory` composite-pathway fix, `mean_relative_width()`'s
near-zero floor) -- every one of those fixes improved the ensemble's
own *content* without this lay-facing signal ever looking at it. A
scenario could genuinely report "high confidence" from a clean point
estimate while its own UQ ensemble showed the glucose trajectory was
highly sensitive to parameter uncertainty, or largely failed to solve
at all.

Fixed: added `UQ_WIDE_GLUCOSE_RELATIVE_WIDTH = 0.15` (module-level
constant in `runner.py`, disclosed as an engineering choice -- same
category as `MIN_GB_THRESHOLD_MARGIN_MM`/`ConfidenceBand
.mean_relative_width()`'s own `floor_fraction` -- not a literature-
derived statistic). `_compute_lay_summary()` now, whenever `uq is not
None`: forces `is_high_confidence=False` and appends a note naming the
success rate/overall confidence if `not uq.is_reliable` (checked FIRST,
before touching `uq.bands`, so an all-samples-failed ensemble's empty
`bands={}` can never raise `KeyError`); otherwise forces
`is_high_confidence=False` and appends a "wide range of plausible
glucose trajectories" note if `"G" in uq.bands` and
`uq.bands["G"].mean_relative_width() > UQ_WIDE_GLUCOSE_RELATIVE_WIDTH`.
When `uq is None` (the default, `run_uncertainty=False`), behaviour is
byte-for-byte unchanged from before this fix.

+7 tests in a new `TestLaySummaryUQWiring` class
(`test_simulation_api.py`): `uq=None` unaffected, a reliable/narrow
ensemble doesn't downgrade, an unreliable ensemble (high failure rate)
downgrades a high watchdog score with a "reliability" note, a wide
glucose band downgrades with a "wide range" note, a band just under the
threshold does not downgrade, a low-watchdog-confidence case with a
clean UQ ensemble stays low with no spurious extra note (closing the
exact "watchdog vs. UQ" attribution gap), plus one real end-to-end
`SimulationRunner.run()` sanity check. RED-proofed via a scoped `git
stash` on `runner.py` alone -- the two discriminating tests (unreliable
ensemble, wide band) both failed with `is_high_confidence=True` against
the pre-fix code, the other five passed either way (confirming they
test preserved/non-discriminating behaviour, not the fix itself).

### DONE — Added `UQResult.species_pathway` provenance (Track 2, MASTER_PLAN 2.3)

`UQResult.bands` (Monte Carlo confidence bands, keyed by bare species
name -- "G", "I", "GLP1", etc.) had no way to say which pathway produced
a given species. Purely presentational (species names are already
globally unique across this platform's pathway set, so nothing depends
on this for correctness) -- useful for a future UI that wants to group
confidence bands by pathway rather than listing every one flat.

Fixed: added `UQResult.species_pathway: dict[str, str]` (bare species
name -> producing pathway name, e.g. `"GLP1" -> "glp1_v1"`, `"G" ->
"glucose_insulin_v1"`) and a `pathway_for(species)` convenience accessor
(`None` on unknown, deliberately NOT raising like the sibling `band()`
method -- this field is documented as optional/presentational, matching
its own graceful-degradation contract: empty for a hand-constructed
`UQResult`). Also added `species_pathway` to `uncertainty_summary()`'s
reporting dict.

`MonteCarloEngine.propagate()` computes this once, via a new
`_species_pathway_map(pathway)` helper, from the first successful
sample's own pathway -- mirrors `ODESystem.simulate()`'s own
`"<pathway_name>.<species>"` prefix-stripping exactly (`bare_name =
name.rsplit(".", 1)[-1]`, `system.py`), so the mapping's keys line up
with `bands`'/`SimulationResult.species`'s own bare keys. For a bare
(non-composite) pathway, `species_names` carries no prefix at all --
every species is attributed to the pathway's own `.name` in that case.
Verified via grep that no real pathway name in this codebase
(`glucose_insulin_v1`, `glp1_v1`, `renal_clearance_v1`, `cortisol_v1`,
`hep_gluc_v1`, `nefa_v1`, `exercise_v1`, `exogenous_insulin_v1`,
`meal_absorption_v1`) contains a `.`, and `CompositePathway.species_names`
only ever inserts exactly one `.` per name (composites are never
nested, per this project's own architecture rule) -- so `rsplit(".", 1)`
always splits cleanly.

+11 tests: 5 in a new `TestUQResultSpeciesPathway` class
(`test_uncertainty.py`) -- a bare pathway maps every species to its own
name, a GLP1-composed pathway attributes "GLP1"/"G"/"I" to their real
respective pathways, an all-samples-failed ensemble leaves the mapping
empty, a hand-constructed `UQResult` defaults to empty, and
`uncertainty_summary()` includes the mapping -- plus 1 end-to-end
`SimulationRunner` test (`test_simulation_api.py`) confirming a real
semaglutide scenario's `output.uq.species_pathway` is correctly wired
through the production `_build_pathway()` path. RED-proofed via a
scoped `git stash` on the two changed source files -- all 5 new
`test_uncertainty.py` tests failed with a clean `AttributeError`/
`KeyError` pre-fix.

### DONE — Sample extension-pathway-specific parameters in UQ (Track 2, MASTER_PLAN 2.2)

Prior Track 2 work (`pathway_factory`) made a Monte Carlo UQ ensemble see
the SAME composed pathway STRUCTURE (GLP1, renal/SGLT2i, cortisol,
hepatic, ...) as the point estimate. A narrower gap remained: extension-
pathway-SPECIFIC parameters (e.g. `RenalClearanceParameters.beta`) stayed
FIXED at their point-estimate value in every sample -- a drug scenario's
band correctly reflected uncertainty in p1/p2/p3/ke/EC50_mTOR but
silently treated the drug's own calibrated effect size as if it were
exactly known.

**Scoped via `architect` before implementing** (both mandatory review
agents were mid-way through an earlier fix's verification when this
milestone started, and the follow-on `computational-biologist` scoping
pass hit a session-quota outage almost immediately -- per this project's
standing rule, did not retry identically; instead independently
re-derived the one literature question directly, see below). The
architect's key findings, all independently verified before implementing
rather than trusted:

- **`GLP1Parameters`/`RenalClearanceParameters` are NOT frozen
  dataclasses** -- mutable, hand-written `__init__`. Post-construction
  mutation looks tempting but is ruled out by this codebase's own worst
  bug class: both pathways compute `y0` from these parameters AT
  CONSTRUCTION TIME (`self._y0 = [self.params.glp1_basal *
  self.params.agonist_scale]`, `self._y0 =
  [self.params.target_delta_mM_per_min(...)]`); mutating a param
  afterward leaves `_y0` stale -- exactly KNOWN BUGS FIXED #10-#14.
  Sampled extension values must reach the CONSTRUCTOR, never a
  post-hoc mutation.
- **Design: a wholly separate, additive parameter pair**
  (`extension_distributions`/`extension_pathway_factory`), not a change
  to `pathway_factory`'s existing 2-argument contract -- extension
  parameters don't live on `PathwayParameters` at all (a frozen
  dataclass with a fixed field set), they live on separate objects
  (`GLP1Parameters`, `RenalClearanceParameters`) a pathway constructs
  from. Every existing 2-arg `pathway_factory` (SimulationRunner's real
  one, `calibration.py`, every pre-existing test) is completely
  unaffected. Rejected `inspect.signature`-based arity-detection on the
  EXISTING `pathway_factory` param (doesn't solve the real problem --
  namespacing which sampled names are core vs. extension -- and is
  "magic, undocumented behaviour").
- **Dotted extension keys** ("renal.beta") mirror
  `_species_pathway_map()`'s own "<pathway_name>.<species>" convention,
  making collision with a core field name structurally impossible.

**Implementation** (`propagation.py`): `ExtensionPathwayFactory` type
alias (`(params, meals, extension_overrides) -> BasePathway`). Three
fail-fast validations in `propagate()`: `pathway_factory`/
`extension_pathway_factory` mutually exclusive; `extension_distributions`
non-empty requires `extension_pathway_factory` (else a sampled value has
nowhere to go and is silently discarded -- the "computed but discarded"
bug class this project has repeatedly found and fixed); no key collision
between core/extension distribution names. New `_sample_extension_values()`
deliberately does NOT apply `_sample_params()`'s own positivity floor --
an out-of-range extension draw reaches the extension parameter object's
own constructor validation (e.g. `RenalClearanceParameters` rejects beta
outside `[0, 1)`) and is counted as a real, reasoned entry in
`failure_reasons`, not silently reinterpreted as "the drug does
nothing." `UQResult.parameter_names`/`sampled_parameter_values` merge
both namespaces.

**Literature verified directly** (the `computational-biologist` scoping
pass's own outage meant this needed independent verification, done via
live `PubMedFetcher` calls, not trusted from the architect's own report
alone): re-fetched both PMID:23735727 (DeFronzo 2013) and PMID:28428225
(Al-Jobori 2017) abstracts live. Confirmed PMID:28428225's abstract does
NOT disambiguate SD-vs-SEM for its "459+/-53 vs. 337+/-25 mg/min" TmG
figures -- gates the architect's own proposed "empagliflozin TmG"
extension candidate as a documented, not-yet-actionable blocker (see
below), rather than guessing. Confirmed the existing
`SGLT2I_BETA_CLASS_DEFAULT` derivation's own already-committed code
comment (PMID:23735727's discussion-section quote) is real and
unchanged from an earlier session's verification.

**Only `renal.beta` sampled this milestone -- `GLP1Parameters
.agonist_scale` deliberately NOT assigned a CV.** `for_semaglutide()`'s
`agonist_scale = 1.0 + occupancy * 8.0` has NO reported dispersion
anywhere in its own evidence base (already disclosed elsewhere in this
file: none of its coefficients are individually cited to Lau et al.
2015). Assigning an invented CV to an invented point estimate would be
a STRICTLY WORSE anti-pattern than the already-rejected `KG_secretion~200`/
glucagon-EGP-coefficient cases: a confidence band is itself a claim
about precision, so fabricating one layers a second guess on top of the
first while presenting it as quantified uncertainty. Also: `agonist_scale`,
`glp1_basal`, `max_incretin`, and `max_emptying_reduction` are all
driven by the SAME `occupancy` term -- sampling one in isolation would
produce parameter combinations the model's own dose-response
construction cannot generate, the wrong uncertainty SHAPE, not just the
wrong magnitude.

**`RENAL_BETA_CV = 0.08` derivation** (`renal_pathway.py`), honestly
disclosing that the source states the same fact two inconsistent ways
rather than picking whichever is convenient: PMID:23735727's own
discussion statement gives BOTH "60-80 g/day" UGE (-> beta range
[0.364, 0.485], width 0.121, SD via uniform approx = 0.121/sqrt(12) =
0.0350, CV relative to the 0.40 anchor = 0.088) AND "40-50% of filtered
load" (-> beta range [0.40, 0.50] directly, SD = 0.10/sqrt(12) = 0.0289,
CV = 0.072). `RENAL_BETA_CV = 0.08` is their average, anchored to
`SGLT2I_BETA_CLASS_DEFAULT` (0.40) itself rather than either phrasing's
own slightly-higher range mean -- keeps the UQ band's median matching
the point estimate.

`for_dapagliflozin()`/`for_empagliflozin()` both gained an optional
`beta_class_default: float = SGLT2I_BETA_CLASS_DEFAULT` parameter --
for empagliflozin this is the PRE-scaling class-wide default, still
multiplied by the existing `fraction_of_day14` onset scaling afterward
(NOT the already-duration-scaled final beta), so an override still
respects the day2/day14 onset shape. Omitting it reproduces each
classmethod's exact prior behaviour byte-for-byte.

**Production wiring** (`runner.py`): `_build_pathway()`/`_detect_renal()`
both gained an optional `extension_overrides: Mapping[str, float]`
parameter (default `{}`, forwarded transparently -- every existing call
site unaffected). The UQ block now calls `self._detect_renal(scenario)`
once to check if an SGLT2i drug is active; if so, builds
`extension_distributions = {"renal.beta": LogNormalDistribution
.from_mean_cv(SGLT2I_BETA_CLASS_DEFAULT, cv=RENAL_BETA_CV)}`, and
switches to `extension_pathway_factory` UNCONDITIONALLY (not just when
SGLT2i is active) -- with an empty `extension_distributions` this is
behaviourally identical to the old 2-arg `pathway_factory` for every
non-SGLT2i scenario.

**Mandatory code-reviewer and security-reviewer passes both ran
successfully.** Code-reviewer: APPROVE, 0 findings -- independently
recomputed the CV=0.08 arithmetic, confirmed the `for_empagliflozin()`
scaling uses the override (not the module constant), confirmed
backward compatibility (`calibration.py`/`sobol_sensitivity.py` never
pass either new parameter), and confirmed the positivity-floor
asymmetry is safe (at CV=0.08 mean=0.40, `P(beta>=1.0)` requires an
~11.5-sigma draw, astronomically negligible). Security-reviewer:
0 CRITICAL/HIGH, traced NaN/Inf safety end-to-end (a bad draw reaches
`RenalClearanceParameters.__init__`'s bounds check before `self.beta`
is ever assigned, caught by `propagate()`'s existing `try/except`, never
crashes the whole call), confirmed zero double-counting with the
point-estimate simulation (which never passes `extension_overrides`,
so it's unaffected by anything the UQ ensemble samples). One real LOW
finding, fixed before finalizing: `extension_pathway_factory`'s arity
was never validated eagerly, so a wrong-signature factory would raise
the identical `TypeError` on every one of `n_samples` samples instead
of failing once with a clear diagnostic -- added an eager
`inspect.signature(...).bind(None, None, {})` dry-bind check at
`propagate()`'s own entry validation block (raises `ValueError`
immediately, not per-sample). The second LOW finding (the dotted-key
convention isn't mechanically enforced beyond exact-string collision
detection) was confirmed NOT currently exploitable -- informational
only, not fixed.

+17 tests: 8 in `TestMonteCarloExtensionParameters` (`test_uncertainty.py`
-- mutual exclusivity, orphaned-distributions guard, key-collision
guard, default-matches-no-extensions-exactly, genuine band-widening

All discriminating tests RED-proofed via scoped `git stash`(es) per

### DONE — Extend Sobol/OAT sensitivity analysis to extension-pathway parameters (Track 2, MASTER_PLAN 2.4)

Direct follow-on to MASTER_PLAN 2.2 (which added `extension_distributions`/
`extension_pathway_factory` to `MonteCarloEngine.propagate()` so Monte
Carlo UQ could sample extension-pathway-specific parameters like
`RenalClearanceParameters.beta`). This milestone gives the identical
additive treatment to the OTHER two sensitivity-analysis classes in the
same package -- `OATSensitivityAnalyzer` and `SobolSensitivityAnalyzer`
-- as the architect's own 2.2 scoping pass predicted would be "cheap
after this." Pure library/analysis-tooling generalization: not wired
into `SimulationRunner`'s production pipeline at all, no drug-dosage/
biological-output calculation touched -- only extends what curation-
prioritization tooling in `biosim_uncertainty` can analyze.

**`OATSensitivityAnalyzer`** (`sensitivity.py`): gained
`extension_pathway_factory`/`extension_base_values`. Unlike Sobol (below),
OAT perturbs a single center point up/down, so it needs an explicit "what
value am I perturbing FROM" for each extension parameter --
`extension_base_values` (a dotted-key dict, e.g.
`{"renal.beta": 0.40}`) fills the role `self.base_params` plays for core
`PathwayParameters` fields, which extension parameters don't live on at
all. `analyze()`'s `parameter_names` can now mix ordinary field names
with dotted extension names (e.g. `["p1", "renal.beta"]`) in one call --
routed by `"." in param_name`: extension names look up their base value
in `extension_base_values` (an unknown name returns `None` and is
silently skipped, mirroring the EXISTING "unknown core field -> skip"
convention for `getattr(self.base_params, param_name, None)`); the
up/down perturbations merge into `{**self.extension_base_values,
param_name: perturbed_value}` so every OTHER extension parameter stays
at its own base value, exactly like every other core field not
currently being perturbed stays at its own `base_params` value.

**`SobolSensitivityAnalyzer`** (`sobol_sensitivity.py`): gained
`extension_pathway_factory` only -- no `extension_base_values` needed,
since Sobol's own `distributions: dict[str, LogNormalDistribution]`
already supplies mean+CV for every sampled parameter uniformly, core or
extension alike. A dotted name in that SAME dict is simply routed
differently at evaluation time: `analyze()`'s per-row loop splits
`row_values` into `core_values` (no ".") fed to
`dataclasses.replace(self.base_params, **core_values)` and
`extension_values` (has ".") fed as `_run()`'s new 4th argument.

Both `_run()` methods gained an `extension_overrides` parameter and the
same mutual-exclusivity + eager `inspect.signature(...).bind(None, None,
{})` arity check `propagate()` already has (fail once, at construction,
rather than identically on every one of 2*n_parameters+1 (OAT) or
n_base_samples*(2k+2) (Sobol) simulations).

**One pre-existing test needed updating, not just new tests added**:
`test_failure_raises_runtime_error_not_silently_dropped` monkeypatches
`analyzer._run` with a fixed-3-arg replacement function -- broke once
`analyze()` started unconditionally calling `self._run(params, meals,
duration_s, extension_values)` (4 positional args). Fixed by adding
`extension_overrides=None` to the test double's own signature and
forwarding it, rather than complicating the real call site to
conditionally omit the argument.

**Mandatory code-reviewer pass found a real MEDIUM finding, fixed before
finalizing** (not a drug/dosage/physiology/genetics/calculation change,
so no security-reviewer pass was owed): neither analyzer had the
identical guard `propagate()` already has for "a sampled/perturbed value
with nowhere to go." Reproduced directly by the reviewer: `OATSensitivity
Analyzer(extension_base_values={"glp1.agonist_scale": 9.0})` with no
`extension_pathway_factory` silently produced a MISLEADING "this
parameter has zero influence" result (upper/lower perturbation runs were
identical, since the override never reached the pathway) rather than an
error; the Sobol equivalent crashed with an opaque `TypeError` deep
inside `SALib.analyze.sobol` (zero-variance output) instead of a named
diagnostic. Both are the same "computed but discarded" bug class this
project has repeatedly found and fixed elsewhere. Fixed with the same
guard shape `propagate()` already uses: `OATSensitivityAnalyzer.__init__`
raises `ValueError` if `extension_base_values` is non-empty with no
factory; `SobolSensitivityAnalyzer.analyze()` raises if any dotted key
in `distributions` has no factory to route to (checked once before the
sampling loop, not per-row).

+10 tests: 5 in a new `TestOATSensitivityExtensionParameters` class
(`test_uncertainty.py` -- mutual exclusivity, wrong-arity guard, a real
substantial sensitivity score for a synthetic extension parameter, core
+ extension analyzed together in one call, unknown extension name
silently skipped, the new "no factory" guard) and 3 in a new
`TestSobolSensitivityExtensionParameters` class
(`test_sobol_sensitivity.py` -- mutual exclusivity, wrong-arity guard,
core + extension in one `distributions` dict with a real first-order
index, the new "no factory" guard), plus 1 fixed pre-existing test.
RED-proofed via a scoped `git stash` on both source files -- all new/
changed tests fail with the exact predicted `TypeError` pre-fix. Full
suite: 1781 -> 1791 passed, 2 skipped. All 6 clinical benchmarks
confirmed byte-identical (pure analysis-tooling generalization, no
simulation math touched).

### DONE — Resolved the Neo4j invariant-4 decision (Track 3, MASTER_PLAN 3.4)

`infra/neo4j/002_reference_queries.cypher`'s invariant 4 ("no active
entity has two accessions from the same ontology source") was flagged
this session as a real, unresolved tension: `registry.py`'s own
already-shipped merge-inheritance fix (see the earlier "IDRegistry's
merge workflow left deprecated entities' data permanently stale" entry)
makes exactly this outcome legitimate and routine, contradicting this
schema's own "no constraint stricter than the Python invariant" rule.

**Verified the tension directly, not assumed**: ran a real `IDRegistry`
merge -- entity A (UniProt P00001) merged into entity B (UniProt
P99999) -- and confirmed B's `cross_references` legitimately end up as
`{'uniprot': ['P99999', 'P00001']}`, `get_external_id()`/
`cross_reference()` deterministically return 'P99999' (Python's
insertion-order `refs[0]` -- the new entity's own restated accession
comes first, the inherited one second), and BOTH accessions remain
independently resolvable. Invariant 4 as originally written would have
flagged this correct, working state as a data-integrity violation.

**Found something worse while investigating, not just a false-positive
constraint**: `cross_reference()`'s own Cypher query already had a
comment acknowledging it used `ORDER BY accession ASC LIMIT 1`
(alphabetically-first) specifically BECAUSE invariant 4 was assumed to
guarantee at most one candidate ever existed. Since that assumption is
false, the query would have silently returned 'P00001' (alphabetically
first) for the scenario above -- disagreeing with Python's real answer
('P99999') -- a genuine equivalence-suite-breaking semantic divergence
between the two stores, not merely an overly strict invariant.

**Resolved by making Python's already-deterministic insertion order an
explicit, persisted graph property**, rather than fighting it (the
option MASTER_PLAN's own row framed as "make Python's cross-reference
ordering deterministic" -- it already was; the schema just didn't
capture it):
- Step 2's write path (`register()`'s Cypher equivalent) now stamps
  each `IDENTIFIES` edge with `rank` (0-based position in Python's own
  `cross_references[source]` list at backfill time), set `ON CREATE`
  only -- matching this project's existing "`IDENTIFIES` edges are
  immutable by convention" rule.
- `cross_reference()`'s query now orders by `r.rank ASC` instead of the
  accession string, matching Python's real `refs[0]` semantics exactly.
- Invariant 4 rewritten: no longer rejects multiplicity itself, only
  flags two DISTINCT accessions sharing the SAME rank for one (entity,
  source) pair -- the actual ambiguity `cross_reference()` depends on
  not having, not multiplicity, which is expected and correct.
- `get_record()`'s query also returns each cross-reference's `rank` for
  completeness.

**Mandatory code-reviewer pass**: APPROVE, 0 CRITICAL/HIGH -- hand-traced
the rewritten invariant-4 query against both a legitimate case (ranks
0/1, correctly not flagged) and a genuine bug case (two accessions both
at rank 0, correctly flagged), confirmed `rank` is scoped per (entity,
source) correctly in both the write path and the invariant, and
independently re-executed `register()`/`get_record()`/`cross_reference()`
by hand against the new test's exact scenario, confirming every claimed
fact. One real MEDIUM finding, fixed before finalizing: invariant 4 can
only detect rank AMBIGUITY (two accessions sharing a rank), not rank
MISASSIGNMENT (a backfill bug producing unique-but-wrong-order ranks,
e.g. a reversed list) -- "zero rows from invariant 4" means
"unambiguous," not "correct," and only the not-yet-built equivalence
suite (Track 3.8) can catch a unique-but-wrong-order bug. Added an
explicit disclosure of this limit to both the Cypher comment and
`MIGRATION_PLAN.md`'s own entry, so a future implementer of the backfill
script (3.7) doesn't mistake "invariant 4 passes" for "ranks are
correct." One LOW finding also fixed: two comments referenced a
non-existent `EntityRecord` class instead of the real `ResolutionRecord`
(`types.py`) -- corrected in both `002_reference_queries.cypher` and
`MIGRATION_PLAN.md`.

**Python side needed zero source changes** -- its behavior was already
correct; this was purely a schema-design fix plus a documentation/
regression-lock test. Added
`test_merge_producing_two_accessions_for_one_source_keeps_the_new_ones_own_as_primary`
(`test_resolver.py`) -- runs the exact P00001-into-P99999 scenario
through the real `IDRegistry` and asserts every fact this schema
decision now depends on (cross_references order, primary selection,
both accessions still resolvable), since this is now a load-bearing
contract a future Neo4j backfill relies on matching exactly, not just
an incidental behavior.

entry with the full decision, verified evidence, and the flagged
