### DONE — Recalibrated post-exercise p3-boost coefficient (B1)

Continuing the deep-search plan's priority order after Group A, ran
Group B's two literature-curator searches in parallel: B1 (post-
exercise insulin-sensitivity magnitude) and B2 (during-exercise
clearance/secretion). B1 succeeded; B2's finding is a genuine negative
result (see the entry directly below).

**Literature, independently re-verified live**: `physiology/exercise.py`'s
`ExerciseBout.post_exercise_modifiers()` had an uncited `max_p3_boost =
1.0 + 0.50*volume`. Two real clamp studies found: **Mikines KJ, Sonne
B, Farrell PA, Tronier B, Galbo H. "Effect of physical exercise on
sensitivity and responsiveness to insulin in humans." Am J Physiol.
1988. PMID:3126668** (n=7 healthy untrained men, 60min 150W cycling,
euglycaemic hyperinsulinaemic clamps at rest vs. immediately post-
exercise: Km 52->43 microU/mL, Vmax 9.5->10.9 mg/min/kg) and **Wang X
et al. "A ~60-min brisk walk increases insulin-stimulated glucose
disposal..." J Appl Physiol. 2013. PMID:23493357** (n=10 nonobese
older women, ~60min brisk walk, 2-stage hyperinsulinaemic-euglycaemic
clamp: Rd 78.4->88.0 umol/kg FFM/min).

**Derivation** (worked out by a dispatched `computational-biologist`,
independently spot-checked): using either study's Vmax/Rd shift alone
discards the other half of the same measurement (Mikines reports BOTH
a sensitivity AND a responsiveness shift). Applying one consistent
rule to both -- ratio of insulin-STIMULATED disposal above basal
insulin, evaluated at this platform's own validated OGTT peak insulin
(354 pM) -- gives +21.8% (Mikines) and +16.0% (Wang). Converting each
to this model's own `volume = relative_intensity * duration_hours`
needed an explicit, DISCLOSED, not-independently-verified assumption
about each study's own %VO2max (Mikines' 150W assumed ~70% via the
standard ACSM cycling equation; Wang's "brisk walk" assumed ~50%,
since neither paper states an exact intensity) -- giving implied
coefficients of 0.311 and 0.321 respectively. **The two studies
converge to within 3% despite different sex/age/modality** -- not
forced into agreement. Adopted **0.31** (honest range 0.29-0.36 across
plausible intensity assumptions). The functional form itself (linear
in `volume`) remains unanchored -- neither study varied volume, so
this coefficient is only directly supported near volume~0.5-0.7.

Verified basal-invariance unaffected (`ExercisePathway`'s own t=0
signals stay exactly neutral for p1/p3/gb regardless of this
coefficient, confirmed by direct execution -- the "during" branch
never reads `post_exercise_modifiers()` at all). Re-measured
`post_exercise_meal()` vs `sedentary_meal()`'s own demonstration
magnitude with the new coefficient: peak -1.52%, AUC -1.89% --
essentially unchanged from the pre-recalibration ~1.5% (p3's own
absolute magnitude is already small post the earlier Bergman-1981
correction; other effects dominate the composed dynamics more than
this specific coefficient). All 6 clinical benchmarks confirmed
byte-identical (none compose an exercise bout).

**Disclosed, not fixed**: Mikines' subjects were specifically
UNTRAINED -- this coefficient represents the acute effect for an
untrained person; it composes multiplicatively alongside
`fitness_modifiers()`'s own separate CHRONIC-training p3 multiplier
(two real, distinct mechanisms, not double-counting), but the acute
magnitude itself isn't adjusted for the person's own fitness level (a
real, pre-existing model limitation, not introduced or fixed by this
recalibration).

("resets Aug 15, 3pm Europe/London") on launch, no partial result from

**Clearance (`extra_g_clearance_modifier`)**: real citations found --
**DeFronzo RA, Ferrannini E, Sato Y, Felig P, Wahren J. "Synergistic
interaction between exercise and insulin on peripheral glucose
uptake." J Clin Invest. 1981. PMID:7033285** (n=10 healthy men,
euglycaemic clamp, 30min bicycle at 40% VO2max: exercise-alone
increment in glucose uptake 1.43+/-0.30 mg/kg/min) and **Wahren J,
Felig P, Ahlborg G, Jorfeldt L. "Glucose metabolism during leg
exercise in man." J Clin Invest. 1971. PMID:5129319** (postabsorptive
men, arteriovenous-difference method: leg glucose uptake rose 7-20x
during exercise). Both real, both live-verified. But
`extra_g_clearance_modifier` multiplies a rate CONSTANT contributing
`extra_g_clearance*(G-Gb)` mM/min -- exactly zero at G=Gb, confirmed
directly: `dydt()` at y0 gives `dG=0.0` regardless of the modifier's
value (tested up to 100.0). DeFronzo's number was measured AT
clamp-held euglycemia -- the one condition this term's own formula
contributes nothing under. Matching it would require (G-Gb)=1.198 mM,
a value the study deliberately excluded by design (that's what a
euglycaemic clamp means). Same "wrong shape" class as the already-
documented SGLT2i/GLP1-gastric-emptying architecture findings
elsewhere in this file. Would need a NEW additive rule-11 signal (mM/min,
mirroring `renal_glucose_clearance_delta`) to use this citation at
all -- and Wahren 1971 additionally reports splanchnic glucose
production rising 3-5x during exercise, so an uptake-only additive
term would need a paired EGP term too, or fasted glucose would
silently drop ~0.69 mM below basal. A real milestone, not a
recalibration.

**Secretion (`secretion_scale_modifier`)**: real citation found --
**Jarhult J, Holst J. "The role of the adrenergic innervation to the
pancreatic islets in the control of insulin release during exercise
in man." Pflugers Arch. 1979. PMID:230455** (n=6 bilaterally
adrenalectomized patients + 6 matched controls, exhaustive ergometer
exercise, phentolamine alpha-blocker sub-experiment: "mean plasma
insulin concentration fell by about 50%... phentolamine effectively
abolished the fall"). Real, live-verified, mechanistically on-target.
But `secretion_scale_modifier` multiplies `delta_secretion`/
`first_phase_secretion`, both structurally zero at basal glucose/no
meal -- confirmed directly: `secretion_scale_modifier=0.0` at y0 gives
`dI=0.0`. Jarhult measured a fall in FASTED, BASAL plasma insulin
during exercise -- a quantity this parameter cannot move at all under
this model's own architecture; it only scales the POSTPRANDIAL
increment, and equating the two would be an unstated, unjustified
assumption. Separately, Wahren 1971 confines the insulin fall to
HEAVY exercise specifically, contradicting the current model's own
linear-in-intensity form (`1.0 - 0.30*relative_intensity`, which
predicts 15% suppression even at LIGHT intensity with no support) --
catecholamine-mediated suppression is more likely threshold-like than
linear, but a threshold form would itself be an uncited architectural
guess, not resolvable from this citation alone.

**Decision**: neither coefficient changed. `during_exercise_modifiers()`
remains at its prior, uncited values (`clearance_boost=1.0+4.0*
relative_intensity`, `secretion_suppress=1.0-0.30*relative_intensity`).
A genuine, valuable negative result -- real citations exist, but using
them correctly needs new model architecture (an additive clearance
signal + a paired EGP term; a postprandial-increment-vs-basal
reframing or a threshold-intensity form for secretion), not a
parameter substitution. Matches this project's own repeated precedent
(the glucagon-EGP-coefficient rejection, the GLP1-gastric-emptying
architecture question) for a citation that's real but the wrong shape.

No code changed this entry. Full suite unaffected: 2067 passed, 2
skipped.

and its negative result -- not "not started," but genuinely
architecturally blocked pending a larger milestone.

### DONE — NEFA pathway deep-search (Group C): two real recalibrations, one negative result, one disclosed-but-unchanged finding

Continuing the deep-search plan's priority order, ran Group C's four
searches (C1-C4, `nefa_pathway.py`'s uncited constants) in parallel.

**C1 (basal-vs-obese concentration) -- blocked.** Best-titled candidate,
Opie & Walfish 1963 (PMID:13940209, exact topical/MeSH match), is a
pre-1975 record with no abstract and no accessible full text
(subscription required) -- could not extract a single quotable number.
A real, live-verified counter-evidence finding surfaced instead: **Curry
TB et al., Am J Physiol Endocrinol Metab. 2011. PMID:21304064**
(n=15 lean + 16 obese + 15 gastric-bypass) states directly: "Fasting FFA
were not significantly different between the three study groups" --
contradicting, not supporting, the premise that obesity elevates basal
NEFA. `NEFA_BASAL_UM`/`NEFA_OBESITY_UM` left unchanged, disclosed as
still uncited.

**C2 (plasma half-life) -- DONE, a genuine, large error corrected.**
`NEFA_HALF_LIFE_MIN` recalibrated from an uncited 90.0 to **3.7**,
anchored to **Heiling VJ, Miles JM, Jensen MD. "How valid are isotopic
measurements of fatty acid oxidation?" Am J Physiol. 1991;261(5 Pt
1):E572-7. PMID:1951681** (n=11 healthy volunteers, tracer-kinetics,
independently re-fetched and re-verified TWICE this session given how
consequential a claimed ~24x discrepancy would be): "After stopping
tracer infusions, the half-life of plasma [14C]FFA was 3.7 +/- 0.1
min." A dedicated second verification pass independently corroborated
this against a SEPARATE research group using a different tracer/fatty-
acid species: **Hagenfeldt L, Hagenfeldt K, Wennmalm A. Horm Metab Res.
1975;7(6):467-71. PMID:1213651** -- fractional turnover rate 0.47-0.80
min^-1 (men/women), implying an even FASTER t1/2~0.87-1.5 min via
t1/2=ln(2)/k. Both sources agree on the same order of magnitude (a few
minutes) -- the prior 90-minute value was a genuine, large error, not
just an uncited-but-plausible placeholder, consistent with the well-
established physiological fact that the small, fast-turning-over
plasma NEFA pool clears far faster than glucose/insulin.

**Verified this doesn't break the pathway's own fixed-point invariant**
(mathematically independent of the rate constant, confirmed for
half_life_min in {3.7, 90.0, 1.5} across all three presets --
default/obesity/exercise -- and via a 600-minute fasted composed
trajectory staying exactly at 350.0 uM throughout). **Verified solver
robustness** given the much faster time constant creates a real
stiffness concern (NEFA now equilibrates ~24x faster than before,
relative to glucose/insulin's own ~10-100min timescales) -- ran all
three presets through a 1000-minute composed simulation with `Radau`
(this project's own implicit stiff-solver choice): all three succeeded
cleanly (900s of function evaluations, no blow-up).

**C3 (insulin IC50 for antilipolysis) -- DONE, a small, clean
recalibration.** `NEFA_INSULIN_IC50_PM` recalibrated from an uncited
80.0 to **68.0**, anchored to **Stumvoll M, Jacob S, Wahl HG, Hauer B,
Loblein K, Grauer P, Becker R, Nielsen M, Renn W, Haring H.
"Suppression of systemic, intramuscular, and subcutaneous adipose
tissue lipolysis by insulin in humans." J Clin Endocrinol Metab.
2000;85(10):3740-5. PMID:11061533** (n=13 lean healthy volunteers,
three-step hyperinsulinaemic-euglycaemic clamp, independently re-
verified twice): "The insulin concentrations resulting in a half-
maximal suppression (EC50) of systemic lipolysis, adipose tissue, and
muscle lipolysis were 51, 68, and 44 pmol/L, respectively." Uses the
ADIPOSE-TISSUE-specific value (68 pM, this pathway's own stated
mechanism), not the systemic (51 pM) or muscle (44 pM) values from the
same paper.

**C4 (NEFA's own insulin-resistance dose-response) -- real citations
found, deliberately NOT adopted numerically.** **Gormsen LC et al.
JCEM. 2007. PMID:17341555** (a genuine 4-level Intralipid dose-response
study, self-described: "these data constitute comprehensive dose-
response curves for FFAs") states "progressively decreased glucose
disposal... at FFA levels above 500 micromol/liter" -- coincidentally
the same numeral as the existing `NEFA_IR_EC50_UM=500`, but Gormsen's
own number is an ABSOLUTE FFA threshold, not the excess-above-basal
EC50 this pathway's own formula requires (`excess_nefa = nefa -
NEFA_IR_REFERENCE(350)`) -- at Gormsen's own 500 uM absolute threshold,
the implied excess above this pathway's 350 uM reference is only ~150
uM, not 500. **Boden G et al. J Clin Invest. 1994;93(6):2438-46.
PMID:8200979** (a real 3-level graded clamp, glucose uptake fell from
~9 to ~4 mg/kg/min across ~50-750 uM FFA, a ~56% reduction) doesn't
cleanly match `NEFA_IR_MAX=0.40` either. Forcing a numeric change from
either ambiguous mapping would repeat this project's own rejected
curve-fitting-without-grounding anti-pattern -- both real citations
corroborate the right order of magnitude and confirm a genuine graded
dose-response exists in the literature, but the specific numeric
re-derivation isn't resolvable from what's accessible. Left unchanged,
both citations added as disclosed partial corroboration in the
module's own constant comments.

regression guards for pre-existing, unaffected behaviour).

+5 tests (`test_pathway_expansion.py`'s new `TestNEFACitationRecalibration`
class): both new citation values pinned, fixed-point invariance

### DONE — Track 4 DNL flux benchmark (F1)

Continuing the deep-search plan (2026-08-12), item F1: found and
independently verified live (via `PubMedFetcher`, full text) a real
flux-type benchmark for hepatic de novo lipogenesis (DNL), the
dependency MASTER_PLAN row 4.3d's own scoping had flagged as missing
before any PPP/DNL reactions could be safely added to the hand-curated
hepatic network.

**Literature**: **Rosqvist F, Kullberg J, Stahlman M, Cedernaes J,
Heurling K, Johansson HE, Iggman D, Larsson A, Ahlstrom H, Boren J,
Riserus U. "Overeating Saturated Fat Promotes Fatty Liver and Ceramides
Compared With Polyunsaturated Fat: A Randomized Trial." J Clin
Endocrinol Metab. 2019;104(12):6207-6219. PMID:30721918** -- confirmed
via full-text fetch (not just abstract): a pooled, 5-cohort cross-
sectional analysis (n=149, BMI 19.5-39.5, nondiabetic adults), fasted
(overnight fast) deuterated-water (2H2O) labeling with VLDL-TG
palmitate GC-MS measurement -- "the fasting hepatic DNL was 6.5% (range
0.1-38.7%)" (median, IQR 3.8-11.5%). This is a genuine fractional-
contribution measurement (what fraction of VLDL-TG palmitate carbon
originates from de novo synthesis, not dietary/adipose-derived fat),
not a flux RATE -- a real category distinction from the existing
`FluxBenchmark` (Adkins 2003/Drouin 1998, both absolute umol/kg/min
rates convertible to mM/min via glucose's own distribution volume).

**New**: `FractionalContributionBenchmark` (`biosim_metabolism
/flux_benchmarks.py`, new frozen dataclass -- fields: `name,
pubmed_id, fraction, fraction_low, fraction_high, population,
condition, method, caveat=""`), deliberately NOT a subclass or variant
of `FluxBenchmark` -- forcing a dimensionless fraction through
`FluxBenchmark.value_mM_per_min()`'s own body-weight/distribution-
volume conversion machinery would be a category error, so the new
class exposes no such method at all (verified via a dedicated
structural-guard test: `not hasattr(ROSQVIST_2019_FASTED_HEPATIC_DNL,
"value_mM_per_min")`). New constant `ROSQVIST_2019_FASTED_HEPATIC_DNL`
pins the median (0.065) and IQR bounds (0.038/0.115) exactly as quoted
above, with a `caveat` explicitly warning against attempting the
`FluxBenchmark`-style unit conversion. Exported from
`biosim_metabolism/__init__.py` alongside the existing `FluxBenchmark`
exports.

+11 tests (`test_flux_benchmarks.py`'s new `TestRosqvist2019FastedHepaticDNL`
class -- 9 tests: PMID match, fraction/range match, fraction-within-
range, method-is-2H2O, caveat present and discloses "not a flux rate",
is-a-`FractionalContributionBenchmark`-not-a-`FluxBenchmark`, has-no-
`value_mM_per_min`-method; plus `TestFractionalContributionBenchmarkGenericConstruction`,
2 tests, generic construction/default-caveat, independent of the real
citation). Full repo suite: 2065 -> 2077 passed (net effect combined
with A6's own tests below), 2 skipped.

**Not built this pass**: the actual PPP/de novo-lipogenesis reactions

### DONE (partial) — Tirzepatide Gb-lowering component (A6)

Continuing the deep-search plan (2026-08-12), item A6, per the user's
explicit "yes do all in sequence" instruction: implemented the
distinct fasting/basal Gb-lowering mechanism for tirzepatide that the
prior tirzepatide scoping pass (row 1.5, "DONE (scoping only)")
identified as needed -- deliberately NOT the second, separately-real
ISR7.2/beta-cell-sensitivity mechanism, which remains blocked on
paywalled full text (Heise 2022/Mather 2024).

**Literature, independently re-verified live twice this session**
(once for the week-8-vs-placebo deltas, once via a dedicated follow-up
agent specifically to fetch each arm's own baseline FPG values needed
to convert an absolute mg/dL reduction into a fraction): **Furihata K,
Mimura H, Urva S, Oura T, Ohwaki K, Imaoka T. "Tirzepatide, a GIP and
GLP-1 receptor agonist, in Japanese patients with type 2 diabetes: A
randomized, double-blind, phase 1 multiple-ascending-dose trial."
Diabetes Obes Metab. 2022** -- placebo-controlled, T2D, multiple doses
(5/10/15mg). Baseline FPG (from the trial's own Table 1, fetched
specifically for this purpose): placebo 173.9, 5mg 164.5, 10mg 181.2,
15mg 170.7 mg/dL. Each arm's own fractional reduction relative to ITS
OWN baseline (not this platform's own, notably lower, T2D preset Gb --
a deliberate choice to avoid a population mismatch) was computed
directly: 5mg -> 0.680, 10mg -> 0.619, 15mg -> 0.596 (a real, disclosed
saturating, non-linear shape -- the 10mg->15mg gain is far smaller than
the 5mg->10mg gain).

**Design**: `TIRZEPATIDE_GB_DOSE_MG = (5.0, 10.0, 15.0)`,
`TIRZEPATIDE_GB_MULTIPLIER = (0.680, 0.619, 0.596)`,
`tirzepatide_gb_factor(dose_mg)` -- piecewise-LINEAR interpolation
across the 3 real anchor points (a deliberately more conservative
choice than fitting an unverified parametric saturating-exponential
shape to only 3 data points), with disclosed extrapolation policy at
both ends: linear-to-neutral (1.0) below 5mg, clamped at the 15mg value
above it (no extrapolation past the highest tested dose). `Drug
.TIRZEPATIDE` added to the `Drug` enum. `_glp1_agonist_modifiers()`
dispatches `{"Gb": tirzepatide_gb_factor(dose.dose_mg)}` for
tirzepatide specifically (zero-dose returns `{}`), while every other
GLP-1-class drug it handles is unaffected (unchanged `{}` return).

**The double-counting question resolved by NOT building the second
mechanism yet, rather than by careful coupling design**: `Drug
.TIRZEPATIDE` is deliberately NOT added to `GLP1_DRUGS` -- verified
directly via `SimulationRunner._detect_glp1()` that a tirzepatide-only
scenario composes no `GLP1Pathway` at all (`_detect_glp1(...) is

to double-count against. This sidesteps the double-counting question
entirely rather than resolving it through careful signal design --
correct for the piece actually implemented (a pure static modifier,
same category as metformin's own static Gb effect), but means the

need this decision revisited (composing `GLP1Pathway` for tirzepatide

### DONE — Warn when a safety clamp overrides a calibrated drug/disease effect

The project owner then asked for a project self-evaluation (goals/quality/direction/
coding) plus a `/verify` pass on the A6/F1 commit. The `/verify` pass
drove the real production REST server (`uvicorn biosim_rest:create_app
--factory`) with actual HTTP requests rather than trusting the passing
test suite, and found a genuine, previously-unnoticed finding: a real
75g-meal dose-response sweep across tirzepatide 5/10/15mg produced
**byte-identical output** (baseline 4.80mM, peak 10.24mM, peak_time
24.1min for all three doses) through this platform's own default T2D
preset (Gb=6.5mM). Traced directly (not assumed): `tirzepatide_gb_factor()`
in isolation IS correctly monotonic (0.68/0.619/0.596 across
5/10/15mg, independently re-confirmed), but every one of those values
gets floored by the pre-existing `MIN_GB_THRESHOLD_MARGIN_MM` safety
clamp before reaching the simulated output -- computed the exact
crossover: a patient's `Gb` needs to exceed ~7.06 mM for 5mg's effect
to survive the clamp at all, and ~8.05 mM for the full 5mg-vs-15mg
range to show up unclamped. This platform's own shipped
`TYPE_2_DIABETES` preset (6.5 mM) sits below both thresholds.
Ironically, Furihata et al. 2022's own trial population (baseline FPG
9.1-10.1 mM) sits comfortably above the crossover -- the calibration
is sound for the population it was measured in, it just can't be
observed through this platform's own lower-Gb defaults. Not a bug in
either piece individually (the clamp does its documented job; the
factor function is correctly unit-tested) -- an interaction between
two independently-reasonable pieces that silently defeats the clinical
signal, invisible to any test that checks the factor in isolation or a
single dose against baseline.

The self-evaluation's own proposed fix (item C1, MASTER_PLAN.md 1.23):
make the clamp's engagement observable, reusing the exact pattern
`GLP1Pathway`'s own disease-elevated-Gb-magnitude warning already
established (a `SimulationOutput.warnings` entry, not a silent
override). The project owner approved the improvement plan and asked to save it to
MASTER_PLAN.md and start executing.

**Fix**: added `PhysiologicalPersonalizationResult.clamp_warnings:
list[str]` (`personalizer.py`, default empty list -- backward
compatible, confirmed via grep this dataclass has exactly one
construction site in production code). The existing
`MIN_GB_THRESHOLD_MARGIN_MM` block now captures the REQUESTED Gb value
(what raw modifier composition alone produced) before overwriting it,
and -- only when the clamp actually moves the value by more than
float noise (`> 1e-9`, guarding against a request landing exactly on
the floor) -- appends a warning naming both the requested and clamped
value, `G_threshold`, and the margin. `SimulationRunner.run()`
(`runner.py`) now extends its own `warnings` list with
`physio_result.clamp_warnings` right after the glucocorticoid block's
`dataclasses.replace()` step, confirmed (via grep) to be the only
`replace()` call site on `physio_result` and to leave `clamp_warnings`
untouched (only `personalized_params` is specified in that replace).

**Self-performed verification** (per the newly-named Q2 checklist,
folded into this file's own standing discipline paragraph in the same
session): double-counting N/A (a warning-only addition, changes no
simulated value); fixed-point invariance N/A (doesn't touch `dydt()`
or `overrides["Gb"]`'s actual value, only records a string alongside
the same clamped value already being applied); extreme-value/NaN N/A
(no new numeric computation, reads values already validated upstream
by `PathwayParameters.__post_init__`); safety-clamp interaction is the
literal subject of this fix, tested directly; RED-proofed via a scoped
`git stash` on both source files.

+4 tests (`test_physiology.py`'s `TestPhysiologicalPersonalizer`):
the clamp fires a warning naming both values for a 15mg tirzepatide
dose (requested ~2.98mM, clamped 4.8mM); no warning for the unmodified
default profile; no warning for a mild alcohol dose that stays clear
of the margin (confirms the check is genuinely conditional, not firing
whenever any Gb-lowering drug is present); an end-to-end test through
the real `SimulationRunner` confirming the warning survives the
glucocorticoid-block replace and reaches `SimulationOutput.warnings`.
RED-proofed via a scoped `git stash` on `personalizer.py`/`runner.py`
together -- all 4 failed cleanly (`AttributeError: no attribute
'clamp_warnings'` / a clean assertion failure on the end-to-end check)
against the pre-fix code, then restored. Full suite: 2102 -> 2106
passed, 2 skipped. All 6 registered clinical benchmarks confirmed
byte-identical (`ModelValidator().validate_all()`, all `PASS` -- a

### DONE (scoping only, no code change) — Corrected the scope of PPP/DNL reaction additions (4.3d)

With the process/quality improvement plan and a citation re-audit both
complete, picked the next chunk per the established process (MASTER_PLAN
Section 9): row 4.3d ("extend the hand-curated hepatic network with
PPP + de novo lipogenesis reactions") was the next genuinely unblocked
item -- its own dependency, a real DNL flux benchmark, had already been
acquired (item F1). Dispatched a `computational-biologist` agent to
scope the exact reaction set before writing any code, per this
project's own established practice (matching 4.3b's own pathway-
scoping precedent).

**The scoping pass found the original plan doesn't survive contact
with the primary literature -- independently re-verified the two most
load-bearing claims before accepting any of it, not trusted at face
value.**

**Finding 1, independently confirmed via a second live full-text
fetch**: `ROSQVIST_2019_FASTED_HEPATIC_DNL` (F1's own benchmark) is not
usable as a validation target for this specifically fasted-state
network. Re-fetched Rosqvist et al. 2019's full text directly and
found, word-for-word matching what the scoping agent had already
quoted: "The evening before the study day (~12 h before assessment),
subjects consumed 2H2O... over the course of the evening... Subjects
were advised to consume a low-fat dinner the evening before measurement
of DNL. After an overnight fast, subjects came to the Clinical Research
Unit, and a blood sample was taken." The isotope label is dosed the
evening before, overlapping with dinner, and accumulates into VLDL-TG
palmitate over that whole ~12h window -- only the final BLOOD DRAW
happens after an overnight fast, not the labeled synthesis itself.
"Fasting hepatic DNL" describes when the sample was taken, not when
the measured synthesis occurred.

**This directly contradicted the already-committed code's own claim**:
`flux_benchmarks.py`'s comment previously stated "This is a genuinely
FASTED-state measurement... unlike most DNL literature (which measures
the much-higher fed/postprandial state -- a real mismatch this citation
specifically avoids)." Fixed immediately, both the human-readable
comment and the machine-readable `caveat` field on
`ROSQVIST_2019_FASTED_HEPATIC_DNL` itself, with a new regression test
(`test_caveat_discloses_the_label_is_dosed_the_evening_before`)
locking in the corrected disclosure so a future edit can't silently
revert to the overreaching claim. RED-proofed via a scoped `git stash`
on `flux_benchmarks.py` alone -- confirmed the new test fails cleanly
against the pre-fix caveat text, then restored.

**Finding 2, independently confirmed via a separate live citation
fetch**: adding ACC/FAS (de novo lipogenesis) reactions alongside the
network's existing FAO (beta-oxidation) reaction would violate the
network's own already-documented futile-cycle exclusion policy.
Malonyl-CoA (FAS's product) is CPT1's own physiological inhibitor --
confirmed directly from Swanson, Foster & McGarry 1998 (PMID:9794789,
*Biochem J*, re-fetched live): "carnitine palmitoyltransferase I (CPT
I) plays a major role in the regulation of fatty acid entry into the
mitochondrial matrix for beta-oxidation by virtue of its inhibition by
malonyl-CoA." Running both pathways at appreciable flux simultaneously
is regulatorily self-contradictory, not merely numerically wasteful --
the scoping agent measured (scratch reconstruction, not yet
independently re-executed by me) that adding them inflates FAO's
currently literature-pinned FVA range by 3.6-5.8x.

**Finding 3 (a logical/mathematical argument, verified by reasoning
through it directly rather than re-running code)**: the row's own
stated driving question -- "is hepatic DNL NADPH-limited by
pentose-phosphate-pathway flux?" -- is structurally unanswerable by
Flux Variability Analysis either way. With oxidative PPP as the sole
cytosolic NADPH source, the answer is fixed by stoichiometric
arithmetic alone (FAS needs 14 NADPH per palmitate; oxidative PPP
yields 2 NADPH per G6P; therefore G6P-through-PPP flux = 7 x the FAS
flux, an equality, not something an LP needs to solve). The moment a
second NADPH source (e.g. malic enzyme) exists with no independent
bound tying it to the first, FVA reports the full feasible range for
each and resolves nothing -- a genuine flux-PARTITION question needs
isotopomer/tracer data, not constraint-based bounds. This is a property
of the method, not a modeling gap that more reactions could close.

**Decision: no code written this pass.** Per this project's own
"don't force a fix, don't build with an incoherent validation target"
discipline (matching the precedent already set by Track 4.4's own
scoping-only deferral), the original 4.3d plan is not implemented.
`MASTER_PLAN.md` row 4.3d rewritten to record this scope correction in
full, split into two smaller, better-scoped, genuinely-answerable
follow-on items: **4.3d-i** (acquire a real ABSOLUTE fasted VLDL-TG/
palmitate secretion-RATE benchmark -- a genuine `FluxBenchmark`, not a
`FractionalContributionBenchmark` -- needs its own fresh literature
search, not yet done) and **4.3d-ii** (once 4.3d-i exists: treat the
resulting rate as a PINNED INPUT, not a predicted output, and ask what
it costs `EGP_MAX_MM_MIN`'s own ceiling via an `egp_sensitivity.py`-
style bracketed table, running FAO/FAS as mutually exclusive named
scenarios -- mirroring the existing glycogen-depletion scenario
convention -- rather than adding both reactions unconditionally).

**What was independently re-verified by me directly, vs. what remains
the scoping agent's own claim, disclosed honestly**: the two most
load-bearing citations (Rosqvist 2019's labeling-window timing;
Swanson/McGarry 1998's CPT1/malonyl-CoA regulation) were both
independently re-fetched live and confirmed word-for-word. The detailed
elemental-balance tables, IDRegistry accession lookups, and the exact
FVA numerical results (3.6-5.8x range inflation, the [0%, 72-83%]
DNL-fraction envelope) are the scoping agent's own reported work,
verified only by logical consistency (the arithmetic checks out) and
not yet independently re-executed against the real codebase by this

### DONE — Resolved NEFA's insulin-resistance EC50 (1.22 fresh-angle retry)

Directly continuing the search above: dispatched a second
`literature-curator` agent for row 1.22 (NEFA insulin-resistance dose-

**Found and independently re-verified live (twice -- once by the

Mandarino L, Kashyap S, Wirfel K, Pratipanawatr T, Berria R, Defronzo
RA, Cusi K. "Dose-response effect of elevated plasma free fatty acid
on insulin signaling." Diabetes. 2005;54(6):1640-1648. PMID:15919784.
Confirmed exactly: title, all 8 authors, year, journal, and the quoted
numbers -- n=21 lean healthy normal-glucose-tolerant subjects, graded
4h Liposyn infusion (30/60/90 ml/h) + 2h euglycaemic insulin clamp:
"Basal plasma FFA concentration (~440 micromol/l) was increased to
695, 1,251, and 1,688 micromol/l after 4 h of Liposyn infusion and
resulted in a dose-dependent reduction in insulin-stimulated glucose
disposal (Rd) by 22, 30, and 34%, respectively (all P<0.05 vs. saline
control)."

**Why this resolves the original ambiguity**: this paper reports its
OWN basal FFA (440 uM, a real physiological value) alongside three
graded absolute levels in the SAME cohort -- excess-above-basal is
directly computable from this one paper's own numbers (255, 811, 1248
uM excess at 22%, 30%, 34% reduction respectively) without importing a
second study's differently-defined reference, which is exactly what
blocked Gormsen/Boden's adoption last time.

**Independently re-derived the fit myself** (not copied from the
agent's own report) using `scipy.optimize.curve_fit` against

percentage point) -- matching the agent's own independently-reported

Every named Track 1 candidate in MASTER_PLAN.md was DONE, permanently

**Scoping result (not trusted at face value -- every headline citation

anchors (chronic kidney disease, thiazolidinediones/pioglitazone, sleep
restriction), plus one useful negative result (pramlintide/amylin --
real citations found, both routes hit the same "wrong shape for this
model's architecture" failure class as the already-documented row
1.18: no absolute denominator to compute a fractional effect one way,
a genuine unrepresentable gastric-emptying lag phase the other way).
Full detail in MASTER_PLAN.md's new "Fresh Track 1 scoping" summary row
and rows 1.24-1.26. Picked the CKD candidate first (highest confidence
per the scoping agent's own ranking: settled literature, one clean
primary source giving both crude and covariate-adjusted numbers, plus
existing plumbing -- `ke` was already a supported `_PARAM_BOUNDS` key).

**Citation, independently re-verified live via `PubMedFetcher.fetch_by_pubmed_id()`
before any code was written** (title/authors/journal/year all matched
the scoping agent's own report exactly): de Boer IH, Zelnick L,
Afkarian M, Ayers E, Curtin L, Himmelfarb J, Ikizler TA, Kahn SE,
Kestenbaum B, Utzschneider K. "Impaired Glucose and Insulin Homeostasis
in Moderate-Severe CKD." J Am Soc Nephrol. 2016;27(9):2861-71.
PMID:26823551. Cross-sectional, n=59 nondiabetic CKD (mean eGFR 37.6
ml/min/1.73m2) vs. n=39 healthy controls, hyperinsulinaemic-euglycaemic
clamp plus IVGTT/OGTT. Confirmed verbatim: "Participants with CKD had
lower insulin sensitivity than participants without CKD (mean[SD]
3.9[2.0] versus 5.0[2.0] mg/min per uU/ml; P<0.01)... Insulin
clearance... was also lower in participants with CKD than controls
(876[226] versus 998[212] ml/min; P<0.01)." And critically: "Adjustment
for physical activity, diet, fat mass, and fat-free mass in addition to
demographics and smoking partially attenuated associations of CKD with
insulin sensitivity (adjusted difference, -0.7... mg/min per uU/ml) and
insulin clearance (adjusted difference, -85... ml/min)."

**Why the adjusted numbers, not the crude ratios**: this platform
already applies `bmi_modifiers()`/fitness modifiers separately from any
disease-state preset. The crude ratios (3.9/5.0=0.78, 876/998=0.878)
would double-count body-composition/lifestyle effects this platform's
own existing modifiers already represent. This is the rare case where
the source paper itself hands over the CKD-specific residual after
controlling for exactly those confounds, rather than leaving the
double-counting question to inference: `p3 = (5.0-0.7)/5.0 = 0.86`,
`ke = (998-85)/998 = 0.915`.

**A genuinely new shape for this platform's disease-state presets**:
every prior `DiseaseState` modifier touches some combination of
p1/p3/Gb/secretion_scale -- none previously touched `ke` (insulin
clearance). `ke` was already a supported `_PARAM_BOUNDS` key
(0.01-0.50) with no prior disease-state consumer, and is fixed-point-
safe by construction (rule 2's `dI = -ke*(I-Ib) + delta_secretion` is
exactly zero at `I=Ib` for any `ke` value) -- reducing it changes only
postprandial insulin-decay kinetics, with zero effect on the basal
steady state.

**Disclosed uncertainty, not smoothed over**: the adjusted insulin-
sensitivity difference's own 95% CI is -1.4 to 0.0 mg/min per uU/ml --
the upper bound touches exactly zero, meaning this specific adjusted
effect is not fully statistically robust in this n=59 cohort, unlike
every other disease-state citation in this codebase. Used anyway,
matching this project's own established "an imperfect real anchor
beats an invented one" convention (same discipline as NEFA's own
pairwise-uncertainty disclosure above), but stated honestly in the
code comment rather than presented as equally solid.

**Deliberately not derived from this citation**: Gb (fasting glucose)
and Ib (fasting insulin). The source reports clamp/tolerance-test-
derived rates, not absolute fasting concentrations for either, and its
own full text blocks XML download via PMC -- no absolute anchor was
extractable. Inventing either from the crude (non-adjusted) ratios
would risk double-counting against `ke`'s own already-applied
reduction, since fasting insulin is itself a function of both basal
secretion and clearance. Left as a real, disclosed gap for a future
chunk, not guessed.

**Deliberately not added to any mutual-exclusion pair** in `profile.py`
(unlike HYPOTHYROIDISM/HYPERTHYROIDISM or TYPE_1_DIABETES/TYPE_2_DIABETES/
INSULIN_RESISTANT) -- CKD is a real, common comorbidity with T2D/T1D/
anything else in this enum, not a contradictory diagnosis, so it
composes freely.

**Verified end-to-end via a real `SimulationRunner` scenario run** (not
just unit-level modifier checks, per the G1 "survives composition"
acceptance criterion): a 75g-carbohydrate meal scenario shows a real,
non-zero shift for the CKD preset vs. healthy (peak glucose 10.504 ->
10.541 mM, AUC and insulin peak both rise, consistent with reduced
clearance); a fasted (zero-meal) scenario correctly shows no change in
glucose baseline for either (Gb is untouched by this preset), confirmed
directly rather than assumed -- this is the disclosed model limitation
working as intended, not a bug.

**Mandatory code-reviewer pass: APPROVE with one real MEDIUM, fixed
before finalizing.** Found that 2 of the first 5 new tests
(`test_ckd_does_not_touch_secretion_or_fasting_levels`,
`test_ckd_result_is_a_genuine_fixed_point`) were not actually RED-proof
discriminating for CKD's own fix -- both passed identically against a
no-op `{}` modifier (confirmed by the reviewer's own targeted `git

### DONE — Pioglitazone (thiazolidinedione) drug addition (fresh Track 1 scoping)

Continuing the same `/loop continue` cycle immediately after the CKD
milestone above -- picked up row 1.25 from the same fresh Track 1
scoping fan-out (medium-high confidence per that agent's own ranking).

**Citation, independently re-verified live via `PubMedFetcher.fetch_by_pubmed_id()`
before any code was written** (title/authors/journal/year matched the
scoping agent's own report exactly): Miyazaki Y, Matsuda M, DeFronzo
RA. "Dose-response effect of pioglitazone on insulin sensitivity and
insulin secretion in type 2 diabetes." Diabetes Care. 2002;25(3):
517-23. PMID:11874940. A 5-arm (placebo/7.5/15/30/45mg), 26-week,
randomized, DIET-TREATED T2D cohort (n=58, no sulfonylurea background
confound). Confirmed verbatim: "Patients treated with 7.5 or 15 mg/day
of pioglitazone had NO CHANGE in fasting plasma glucose (FPG) and
fasting plasma insulin (FPI) concentrations or in plasma glucose (PG)
and insulin concentrations during the OGTT." And: "Whole-body ISI...
increased significantly in patients treated with 30 mg (1.8+/-0.3 to
2.5+/-0.3, P<0.05) or 45 mg (1.6+/-0.2 to 2.7+/-0.6, P<0.05) per day of
pioglitazone."

**A new drug class, mechanistically distinct from everything this
platform models**: pioglitazone is a PPAR-gamma nuclear-receptor
insulin sensitizer -- not a secretagogue, incretin, glucosuric agent,
or absorption blocker (the mechanism classes of every drug already in
this codebase).

**Implementation, mirroring `tirzepatide_gb_factor()`'s existing shape
exactly**: new `Drug.PIOGLITAZONE`; `PIOGLITAZONE_P3_DOSE_MG = (0.0,
7.5, 15.0, 30.0, 45.0)`, `PIOGLITAZONE_P3_MULTIPLIER = (1.0, 1.0, 1.0,
2.5/1.8, 2.7/1.6)`; `pioglitazone_p3_factor(dose_mg)`, a piecewise-
linear interpolation including the two EMPIRICALLY NULL anchor points
(7.5mg, 15mg) rather than an assumed monotonic curve, clamped at the
45mg value above it (the drug's own labeled maximum daily dose --
"don't extrapolate past tested data," same convention as tirzepatide's
15mg cap); `pioglitazone_modifiers(dose)` dispatched via
`_DRUG_FUNCTIONS[Drug.PIOGLITAZONE]`.

**Deliberate, disclosed partial implementation, not an oversight**:
only the whole-body-ISI/p3 route is implemented. The same paper also
reports a hepatic-ISI improvement (0.13->0.21 at 30mg) and an
insulinogenic-index rise (compensatory secretion) -- stacking all three
from one dataset would repeat KNOWN BUG #14's over-determination
mistake (three independently-chosen "improvement" multipliers from a
single study, none separately identifiable). A Gb-additive route was
also explicitly considered and REJECTED: applying the paper's own FPG
deltas (-66/-97 mg/dl) additively to this platform's T2D preset
(Gb=6.5mM, G_threshold=4.5mM) would have 54-68% of the calibrated
effect swallowed by `MIN_GB_THRESHOLD_MARGIN_MM` -- the same
composition-boundary failure tirzepatide's row 1.5 hit before row
1.23's clamp_warnings fix. p3 is not Gb/G_threshold-adjacent, so no
such clamp interaction applies to the route actually used.

**Verified end-to-end via a real `SimulationRunner` T2D scenario run**
(per the G1 "survives composition" acceptance criterion): a 75g-meal
scenario at 7.5mg (the null zone) produces BYTE-IDENTICAL output to no
drug at all (peak glucose 12.299386594016354 mM both ways) -- confirming

wiring bug. The same scenario at 45mg produces a real, measurable shift

but real and dose-differentiated. All 6 registered clinical benchmarks

### DONE — Sleep restriction as a physiological personalization axis (fresh Track 1 scoping)

Third and final candidate from the same fresh Track 1 scoping fan-out
(MASTER_PLAN row 1.26), continuing the same `/loop continue` cycle
immediately after the pioglitazone milestone above.

**Citation, independently re-verified live via `PubMedFetcher.fetch_by_pubmed_id()`
before any code was written** (title/authors/journal/year matched the
scoping agent's own report exactly): Buxton OM, Pavlova M, Reid EW,
Wang W, Simonson DC, Adler GK. "Sleep restriction for 1 week reduces
insulin sensitivity in healthy men." Diabetes. 2010;59(9):2126-33.
PMID:20585000. A 12-day inpatient General Clinical Research Center
study, n=20 healthy men (age 20-35, BMI 20-30), diet/activity
controlled: 10h/night in bed for >=8 nights (sleep-replete) vs. 5h/
night for 7 nights (sleep-restricted). Confirmed verbatim: "insulin
sensitivity assessed by clamp was reduced by 11+/-5.5% (P<0.04) after
sleep restriction." And: "Changes in insulin sensitivity did not
correlate with changes in salivary cortisol (increase of 51+/-8% with
sleep restriction, P<0.02)... without significant alterations in the
insulin secretory response."

**A genuinely new personalization axis**: sleep DURATION/debt, distinct
from `time_of_day_hours` (circadian PHASE, already modelled by
`chronobiology.py`). New `PhysiologicalProfile.sleep_hours:
Optional[float]` field (0-24, `None` = no adjustment -- same convention
as `time_of_day_hours`).

**Anchor choice, disclosed**: the clamp-derived figure (11+/-5.5%
reduction) was used as the primary anchor, NOT the IVGTT-derived figure
also reported in the same paper (20+/-24% -- an SD of 24 on a mean of
20 makes it far noisier than the clamp's 5.5 on 11). The clamp
technique is this platform's own established gold-standard reference
elsewhere (the CKD preset two milestones above uses clamp-derived
numbers for the identical reason).

**Implementation, mirroring `age_modifiers()`/`bmi_modifiers()`'s
existing shape**: `SLEEP_REPLETE_HOURS=10.0`, `SLEEP_RESTRICTED_HOURS=
5.0`, `SLEEP_RESTRICTED_P3_FACTOR=0.89`; new `sleep_modifiers(sleep_
hours)` in `modifiers.py`, piecewise-linear between the paper's own two
conditions, returning `{}` (not an explicit `{"p3": 1.0}`) at/above
10h -- matching `circadian_modifiers()`'s own `None`-returns-`{}`
convention exactly -- and clamped (not extrapolated) below 5h, since no
data exists beyond either boundary in this source. `secretion_scale`
deliberately never appears in the returned dict, matching the source's
own confirmed null ("without significant alterations in the insulin
secretory response").

**Double-counting risks, disclosed rather than resolved by fiat** (in
the module's own citation comment): cortisol rose 51% in the same
cohort -- exactly the signal `CortisolPathway`'s `stress_level`
mechanism represents. The quoted non-correlation between the insulin-
sensitivity change and the cortisol change is real support for treating
this as an INDEPENDENT p3 effect, but it is a non-correlation in ONE

A second risk exists via NEFA: Broussard JL et al., Diabetologia 2015,

### DONE (partial disclosure, no code change) — Cited/disclosed post_exercise_modifiers()'s remaining uncited p1/Gb coefficients

Continuing the same `/loop continue` cycle: with Track 1's three fresh-
scoping candidates (1.24-1.26) landed and Track 2's own named
candidates all done (only a Track-5-gated speculative extension, row
2.5, remains), re-checked whether Track 1 was genuinely exhausted a
second time before moving down the track order, per Section 9's own
process -- rather than immediately dispatching another broad fan-out,
re-read the existing pathway code for anything already flagged as
uncited. Found one: `exercise.py`'s `post_exercise_modifiers()` already
has a properly-cited `max_p3_boost` (0.31, Mikines 1988/Wang 2013), but
the SAME function's `p1_boost` (0.10) and `gb_suppression` (0.03)
coefficients sat quietly uncited right next to it -- a genuinely new,
previously-unnoticed finding, not a re-tread of any already-parked row.

**Citations, independently re-verified live via `PubMedFetcher.fetch_by_pubmed_id()`
before acting on the search agent's report** (title/authors/journal/
year/key-numbers all matched exactly):
- **Hayashi Y, Nagasaka S, Takahashi N, Kusaka I, Ishibashi S, Numao S,
  Lee DJ, Taki Y, Ogata H, Tokuyama K, Tanaka K. "A single bout of
  exercise at higher intensity enhances glucose effectiveness in
  sedentary men." J Clin Endocrinol Metab. 2005;90(7):4327-33.
  PMID:15840752.** n=6 healthy men, single 20min cycle bout: a
  two-compartment glucose-uptake-specific glucose-effectiveness metric
  (S_G(2)*, units dl/kg/min) rose +237.1+/-50.5% at 70% VO2max
  (P<0.05), not significant at 50%.
- **Farkas GJ, Swartz AM, Gorgey AS, Berg AS, Gater DR. "Acute exercise
  improves glucose effectiveness but not insulin sensitivity in
  paraplegia." Disabil Rehabil. 2022;44(2):343-9. PMID:33905292.** n=11
  paraplegia + n=6 able-bodied controls, single 45min arm-crank bout:
  in the able-bodied controls -- the population closest to this
  platform's own healthy baseline -- "Sg was not different at all
  timepoints (p>0.05)" (min^-1, the SAME minimal-model SG unit
  convention this platform's own `p1` uses).
- **Bordenave S, Brandou F, Manetta J, Fedou C, Mercier J, Brun JF.
  "Effects of acute exercise on insulin sensitivity, glucose
  effectiveness and disposition index in type 2 diabetic patients."
  Diabetes Metab. 2008;34(1):50-7. PMID:18448376.** n=7 T2D patients,
  single ~20min bout: "S(G) remained unchanged" despite a large
  (+773%) S(I) rise in the SAME cohort -- a real, same-cohort null on
  the exact mechanism this coefficient represents.
- **Nakayama A et al. "Effect of downhill walking on next-day muscle
  damage and glucose metabolism in healthy young subjects." J Physiol
  Sci. 2019;69(4):511-9. PMID:29679309** -- the one design-matched
  candidate found for Gb (single 30min bout, healthy young adults,
  next-day fasting glucose): confirmed lower after the uphill trial
  (P<0.01), but no extractable number in the abstract, and its full
  text is confirmed genuinely blocked (Europe PMC: "The publisher of
  this article does not allow downloading of the full text in XML
  form").

**Why this was NOT upgraded to a derived point estimate for p1,
despite real positive evidence existing**: Hayashi's effect is large
and statistically significant, but it measures a DIFFERENT metric
(S_G(2)*, a two-compartment index) than this platform's own single-
compartment minimal-model SG that `p1` represents -- and the TWO
studies that use the platform's own SG convention are both NULL in
exactly the populations that matter most (the able-bodied control
group in Farkas, and T2D patients in Bordenave). Deriving a coefficient
from Hayashi alone while setting aside two metric-matched nulls would
manufacture false precision, the identical failure mode this project
has already explicitly rejected for `KG_secretion~200` and the
joint-fit `p1~0.008` lead elsewhere in this codebase (see CLAUDE.md's
own "Process lessons worth keeping" section). Direction is plausible;
magnitude is not derivable from convergent evidence.

**Why Gb remains a genuinely open gap, not just under-searched**: two
independent search angles (direct SG/Gb terms, and fasting-glucose-
recovery-timing terms) converged on either non-quantitative or
design-mismatched sources. Wang et al. 2013 (already cited for
`max_p3_boost`, same cohort) reports a null on basal glucose Ra (a
flux, not the concentration Gb represents) in the same design window.
Borer et al. 2009 (PMID:19568199) has a real number (-20.2%) but a
mismatched design (two 2h bouts, meal-timing-dependent). A T2D
meta-analysis (MacLeod et al. 2013, PMID:24038928) found fasting
glucose non-significantly lower after exercise (P=0.13). None of these
is usable as this function's own anchor.

**Fix**: both coefficients' VALUES are unchanged (0.10 and 0.03,
confirmed via `git diff` showing the `return {"p3": ..., "p1": ...,
"Gb": ...}` statement itself is byte-identical) -- this is a pure
disclosure pass, not a recalibration. `post_exercise_modifiers()`'s own
docstring extended with the full citation trail and honest reasoning
for declining to derive new values from divergent/insufficient
evidence; the module-level `Literature:` list extended for the p1
citations (correctly NOT extended for Gb, since no usable citation was
actually found there).

**Mandatory code-reviewer pass: clean APPROVE, zero findings.**
Independently confirmed the citation reasoning holds together (doesn't
cherry-pick the convenient result, surfaces the strongest counter-
evidence before declining to derive a number), the two "value
unchanged" tests are legitimate regression guards (not dead weight),
and the two docstring-assertion tests pin substantive claims rather
than trivially matching incidental text (confirmed `"convergent
evidence"` appears exactly once, in the intended sentence). Confirmed
this genuinely required no security-reviewer dispatch -- a pure
docstring/comment change with the underlying code untouched.

+4 tests in `test_physiology.py` (new `TestPostExerciseP1AndGbCitationDisclosure`
class: 2 lock in the p1/Gb values are genuinely unchanged by this pass;
2 pin the docstring's own specific PMIDs and disclosure phrasing).
RED-proofed via a scoped `git stash` on `exercise.py` -- the 2
discriminating docstring-assertion tests fail cleanly (the citations
genuinely don't exist pre-fix); the 2 value-unchanged tests correctly
pass either way, disclosed honestly as legitimate non-discriminating
guards for a different claim ("this pass changes no behavior"), not
weak duplicates.

### DONE — Dietary protein co-ingestion (fresh Track 1 re-scoping)

User instruction: "continue track one if needed, if not track 5."
Dispatched a dedicated `computational-biologist` fan-out to check
honestly whether Track 1 still had real, implementable candidates left
after rows 1.24-1.27 (three milestones already mined from one earlier
fan-out, plus a fourth citation-disclosure pass) -- explicitly
instructed not to pad the report if it came up empty, since over-mining
a track risks diminishing returns. It found three real candidates
(dietary protein, PCOS disease state, an `EGP_MAX_MM_MIN` provenance
gap) plus a documented negative result (pramlintide/amylin) and several
checked-and-rejected angles (dietary fat, acromegaly, fructose,
Staub-Traugott). Picked dietary protein first: highest confidence, and
the only one of the three not gated behind either the composition-
boundary audit (PCOS, per two consecutive security reviews flagging
`p3`-floor stacking) or paywalled full text (the EGP provenance check).

**The gap**: this platform's entire food model was carbohydrate-only
(`MealEvent.carbs_g`) -- protein's real, direct insulinotropic effect
(distinct from its effect on satiety/gluconeogenesis) was completely
unrepresented, despite being clinically well-established and directly
relevant to any low-carb/high-protein meal scenario.

**Citations, both independently re-verified live via
`PubMedFetcher.fetch_by_pubmed_id()` before any code was written**
(title/authors/journal/year/exact-quoted-numbers all matched the
scoping agent's own report):
- **Krezowski PA, Nuttall FQ, Gannon MC, Bartosh NH. "The effect of
  protein ingestion on the metabolic response to oral glucose in
  normal individuals." Am J Clin Nutr. 1986;44(6):847-56. PMID:3538843.**
  n=8 healthy (non-diabetic) subjects, 50g protein / 50g glucose / both
  as a single meal. Confirmed verbatim: "Protein stimulated only a
  modest insulin rise and the area above fasting baseline was only 28%
  of that after glucose... The sum of the serum insulin area following
  protein ingestion and that following glucose ingestion was 100.4% of
  the combination meal... the effect on insulin secretion is not
  synergistic."
- **Nuttall FQ, Mooradian AD, Gannon MC, Billington C, Krezowski P.
  "Effect of protein ingestion on the glucose and insulin response to a
  standardized oral glucose load." Diabetes Care. 1984;7(5):465-70.
  PMID:6389060.** The SAME experimental design, in Type II diabetic
  subjects: a genuinely SYNERGISTIC combined effect (247 microU.h/ml
  observed vs. an additive 97+83=180 microU.h/ml) -- directly
  contradicting Krezowski's own normal-subject additivity finding.

**Why the normal-subject (Krezowski), not the T2D (Nuttall), result
governs this mechanism's shape**: this platform's core ODE (Bergman
1981) is calibrated on a normal/healthy cohort -- the exact same
"which regime does this function actually represent" resolution
already used for metformin's own p3/p1 removal (`drug_interactions.py`'s
`metformin_modifiers()` docstring). Krezowski's additive result is
representable by a simple additive rule-11 signal; Nuttall's T2D
synergy would need a genuinely different (multiplicative,
glucose-gated) mechanism this implementation does not attempt --
disclosed as an out-of-scope divergence, not silently ignored.

**Implementation, mirroring `ExogenousInsulinPathway`'s existing
shape** (same "stateless, closed-form, additive-to-dI, exactly-zero-
before/without-the-mechanism" pattern): new `MealEvent.protein_g`/
`MealInput.protein_g` field; new `packages/ode-engine/src/biosim_ode/
nutrient_secretion_pathway.py` (`NutrientSecretionParameters`,
`NutrientSecretionPathway`) computing a monoexponential-decay
secretion-rate curve per protein-bearing meal (NOT the two-compartment
Bateman shape exogenous insulin uses, since only ONE real calibration
anchor exists here -- a total AUC ratio, not a Tmax+Cmax pair -- so
only one free parameter, the magnitude, could be legitimately fit; the
timing constant is a disclosed, unanchored assumption reusing this
platform's own default glucose-absorption rate constant). New rule-11
signal key `nutrient_secretion_delta`, additive to `dI` alongside
`exogenous_insulin_delta`. Wired into `SimulationRunner._build_pathway()`
(composed only when at least one meal has `protein_g > 0`) and exposed
over REST (`MealEventIn.protein_g`).

**Calibration, disclosed as a genuine engineering back-solve** (the 28%
ratio is literature-quoted; the pM/g scale needed to reproduce it
through THIS platform's own composed ODE is not, same category as
`INSULIN_REGULAR_PM_PER_UNIT`): measured this platform's own 50g-carb-
alone meal's insulin AUC-above-baseline over a 240min window (matching
Krezowski's own ~4h protocol) = 28567.0 pM.min; targeted 0.28x that =
7998.8 pM.min for a 50g-protein-alone meal; ran the real composed ODE
with a trial scale, then rescaled linearly (confirmed empirically near-
exactly linear, not assumed) to `NUTRIENT_SECRETION_PM_PER_G=14.93`,
reproducing the target to within 0.02% (7999.31 pM.min measured, via
both a direct pathway construction and the real `SimulationRunner`
path independently).

**Additivity cross-check, disclosed honestly rather than forced**:
composing a 50g-carbs+50g-protein meal in this platform's own ODE gives
combined_AUC/(glucose_AUC+protein_AUC) = 0.977, not exactly 1.0 -- a
real, expected consequence of composing two mechanisms in a genuinely
coupled nonlinear system (protein's extra insulin blunts the glucose
excursion, reducing glucose-driven secretion in the combined run
relative to the sum of the two "alone" runs), not a fabricated synergy
or calibration error. Close to Krezowski's own 1.004 (both within ~3%
of exact additivity, itself just a point estimate from n=8 subjects) --
not forced closer.

**Deliberately does NOT model glucagon's counter-regulatory rise**:
both source papers report protein also raises glucagon (Krezowski:
"Addition of glucose to a protein meal results in a delayed rise in
AAN and glucagon"), and row 1.1 (glucagon's own fasting/basal EGP
effect) remains permanently blocked -- no citable dose-response gain
exists at the perturbations this mechanism would need. This means the
implementation will OVER-PREDICT glucose lowering for protein-dominant
meals, disclosed as a real, load-bearing limitation in the module's own
docstring.

**Mandatory code-reviewer pass: APPROVE, one real MEDIUM, fixed before
finalizing.** The glucagon-limitation was disclosed only in source
comments, not surfaced as a runtime warning -- unlike this same
`runner.py`'s own existing convention for `GutAbsorptionModel.for_gi()`'s
uncalibrated-timing limitation, which DOES emit a warning. Fixed:
`SimulationRunner.run()` now appends a warning whenever a meal's
`protein_g > carbs_g` (a disclosed engineering heuristic for "protein-
dominant," not a literature cutoff), matching the `for_gi()` warning's
own "loud, not silently trusted" convention exactly. +4 regression
tests (warning fires for protein-dominant, absent for carb-dominant/
no-protein/exactly-equal splits), RED-proofed via a scoped `git stash`
on `runner.py` -- the one discriminating test fails cleanly pre-fix.

**Mandatory security-reviewer pass: one real HIGH, one real MEDIUM,
both fixed before finalizing.**
- **HIGH**: no plausibility ceiling on the composed insulin output --
  the dose-response has no saturating/Hill term (a single literature
  data point cannot support fitting one), so nothing prevented an
  arbitrarily large, REST-legal `protein_g` from producing an
  implausible hyperinsulinemic spike. The reviewer independently
  measured a 300g-protein-ALONE meal (the prior REST ceiling) pushing
  `peak_insulin_pM` to ~1136-1262 pM, roughly 3.2-3.6x this platform's
  own validated OGTT `peak_insulin` reference (350 pM). Fixed with a
  new `MAX_PLAUSIBLE_PROTEIN_G_PER_MEAL=150.0` in
  `NutrientSecretionParameters.__init__` (an engineering plausibility
  ceiling, not a literature maximum -- same category and reasoning as
  `ExogenousInsulinPathway`'s own `MAX_PLAUSIBLE_SC_INSULIN_DOSE_UNITS`,
  independently re-verified by re-measuring the composed insulin peak
  across 50-300g protein before choosing 150.0) and a matching REST
  bound (`MealEventIn.protein_g`'s `le=` lowered from 300.0 to 150.0).
- **MEDIUM**: `MealEvent.protein_g.__post_init__` validated only
  `< 0`, not NaN/+inf, unlike `DrugEvent`/`InsulinDoseEvent` in the SAME
  file, which already guard explicitly via `math.isfinite()` (a pattern
  whose own docstring records exactly why: "`< 0` does not reject NaN

### DONE — Built biosim_context_registry and curated CKD/sleep-restriction context entities (5.1 chunks 11-12, D4)

Follow-on to chunk 10's own flagged design gap: CKD (row 1.24) and
sleep restriction (row 1.26) have no plausible molecular-entity subject
to attach a `ParameterStore` registration to -- both are a disease
state / physiological axis, not a drug/hormone/metabolite, and
`IDRegistry`'s `EntityType` enum (`PROTEIN, METABOLITE, PATHWAY, GENE,
REACTION, COMPARTMENT`) has no member for either. Rather than deciding
this unilaterally, surfaced the question directly. The project owner's own explicit
architectural guidance, given in full:

> If `IDRegistry` is currently specifically an identifier registry for
> molecular entities, I'd not expand it yet. Disease states and
> physiological axes are semantically different from genes/proteins/
> compounds and could make the registry muddled. A cleaner architecture
> would be something like: `IDRegistry` (gene/protein/metabolite/
> compound/...) plus a separate `ContextRegistry`/`PhenotypeRegistry`
> (disease_state/physiological_axis/intervention/phenotype). Don't make
> IDRegistry absorb these types just because the immediate
> implementation needs them -- create a deliberate boundary between
> molecular identifiers and biological context/phenotype entities.

**New package, `biosim_context_registry`** (`packages/context-registry/`),
built genuinely simpler than `IDRegistry`, not a mirror of it --
confirmed by reading `IDRegistry`'s own `registry.py` in full first: its
real complexity (auto-incrementing per-type ID counters, an external
cross-reference index with collision detection, multi-hop deprecation/
merge chain resolution, fuzzy name search) exists specifically to
reconcile *competing external-database claims* about a single
molecule's identity (UniProt/ChEBI/HMDB/Reactome/KEGG) -- a need that
does not exist for context entities, since this platform has no
MeSH/ICD-10/SNOMED-CT/HPO integration. `ContextID` is instead a fully
deterministic string, `CONTEXT:<entity_type>:<normalized_name>` (e.g.
`CONTEXT:DISEASE_STATE:chronic_kidney_disease`), requiring no registry
state to construct or predict -- a context entity's own normalized name
IS its identity. `ContextRegistry` has only `register()`/
`resolve_by_name()`/`get_record()`/`is_registered()`/`stats()` -- no
cross-reference index, no deprecation/merge machinery.

`ContextEntityType` scoped to `DISEASE_STATE`/`PHYSIOLOGICAL_AXIS`
only -- deliberately NOT the full four-member sketch the project owner gave
("something like... disease_state/physiological_axis/intervention/
phenotype"), reading his own wording ("something like") as illustrative
of the *boundary*, not a mandate to scaffold all four immediately.
`INTERVENTION`/`PHENOTYPE` have no real chunk needing them today; adding
either speculatively would be exactly the "build for hypothetical
future requirements" this project's own coding-style YAGNI rule rejects
(the module docstring says explicitly: add a new member "when a real
chunk actually needs one"). Flagged this scope decision explicitly to
the mandatory code-reviewer pass as something to scrutinize given it's
a partial, not literal, implementation of the project owner's own sketch -- reviewer
confirmed it faithful to the stated intent, citing this project's own
prior precedent for scoped, add-when-needed decisions (Track 4 GEM
deferral, Track 3 Docker-gated deferrals).

**Key discovery that avoided over-engineering**: confirmed
`ParameterBuilder.for_subject(canonical_id: str)` accepts a plain
string with zero dependency on `IDRegistry`'s own `CanonicalID` type --
so `str(ContextID(...))` drops in as a `ParameterStore` subject with no
adapter layer needed, and no reason to mirror `IDRegistry`'s own
richer type machinery just to satisfy an interface.

**Curated**: chunk 11, CKD's `p3_factor`=0.86/`ke_factor`=0.915 (both
GOLD, de Boer et al. 2016, PMID:26823551) under
`CONTEXT:DISEASE_STATE:chronic_kidney_disease`; chunk 12, sleep
restriction's `p3_factor_at_5h_reference`=0.89 (GOLD, Buxton et al.
2010, PMID:20585000) under
`CONTEXT:PHYSIOLOGICAL_AXIS:sleep_restriction`. Both citations were
already independently verified and in active use in
`physiology/modifiers.py` from this same session's own earlier Track 1
work -- this is a provenance re-registration into `ParameterStore`
(Track 5's own knowledge-infrastructure purpose), not a new unverified
claim. `parameter_seed.py`'s `seed_parameter_store()`/
`create_seeded_store()` gained an optional `context_registry` parameter
(defaults internally to a freshly-seeded one) -- confirmed both
pre-existing single-argument call sites
(`loader.py`/`session.py`) are unaffected.

**Both mandatory review passes dispatched together** (code-reviewer +
security-reviewer, since this is a genuine new architectural boundary,
not a routine parameter addition -- Q5's staggering rule reserves the
security pass for exactly this kind of change). Both returned APPROVE,
zero CRITICAL/HIGH, all MEDIUM/LOW findings fixed:
- **MEDIUM (both reviewers, independently)**: `normalize_name()`
  performed no character-set validation, so a name containing `:` would
  be accepted and registered, but `ContextID.from_string()` (a public,
  documented API) could never parse the resulting string back (splits
  on `:`, expects exactly 3 parts). Not currently triggered (only two
  developer-authored literals are ever registered), but a real latent
  round-trip break. Fixed: `normalize_name()` now rejects any character
  outside `[a-z0-9_]` after normalization (colons included) and enforces
  a `MAX_CONTEXT_NAME_LENGTH=200` cap, with the check applied inside
  `ContextID.__post_init__` too (so direct construction is covered, not
  just `register()`/`resolve_by_name()`).
- **MEDIUM (code-reviewer)**: `register()`'s duplicate-entry error
  message told the caller to "remove the old registration first" for an
  intentional rename -- but no `deregister()`/`rename()` method exists
  anywhere on `ContextRegistry`, so the message promised a capability
  that doesn't exist. Fixed: reworded to point at constructing a new
  registry or editing `context_seed.py` directly, matching what the
  class can actually do.
- **LOW (code-reviewer)**: `normalize_name()` only replaced single
  spaces, so "chronic kidney disease" and "chronic  kidney disease"
  (double space) would normalize to two different strings and evade
  the duplicate check entirely. Fixed with a `re.sub(r"\s+", "_", ...)`
  whitespace-run collapse.
- **LOW (code-reviewer)**: `ContextRecord` was a plain mutable
  dataclass (unlike `ContextID` right above it in the same file,
  already `frozen=True`), and `get_record()` returned the live internal
  reference -- a caller could silently mutate the registry's own state
  with no method call. Fixed: `ContextRecord` is now `frozen=True` too,
  matching `ContextID`'s own convention and this project's standing
  immutability rule.
- **LOW (code-reviewer)**: a test's own comment overclaimed what it
  demonstrated (claimed to test entity-type-aware key collision, but
  CKD/sleep-restriction never share a subject regardless of that
  property) -- corrected to describe what it actually exercises
  (`ParameterStore`'s pre-existing `custom_kind_name`-aware conflict
  detection), with a pointer to the test that genuinely covers the
  entity-type-collision property.
- **LOW (security-reviewer)**: no length/charset bound on registrable
  names at all -- addressed by the same `MAX_CONTEXT_NAME_LENGTH`/
  charset fix above (cheap defense-in-depth; not currently exploitable,
  since `register()` is only ever called from `context_seed.py`'s own
  hardcoded literals, not from any external/request-time surface).

**Confirmed by both reviewers, independently**: zero code path from the
new `ParameterStore` registrations back into `physiology/modifiers.py`
or the ODE engine (grepped both `packages/physiology/src` and
`packages/ode-engine/src` for any reference to `ContextRegistry`/
`biosim_context_registry`/`ParameterStore` -- no matches in either) --
this is a one-directional, provenance-only knowledge-infrastructure
addition; corrupting or deleting it cannot silently alter a simulated
patient outcome. CKD and sleep restriction can never spuriously
conflict with each other or with any `BIOSIM:`-prefixed molecular
subject (different ID prefix entirely, `CONTEXT:` vs. `BIOSIM:`), and
`CanonicalID.from_string()`'s existing `try/except` fallback in
`curation_bridge.py` already handles a `CONTEXT:`-prefixed subject
string gracefully without crashing (pre-existing defensive code, no
change needed).

+36 tests for the initial package/wiring (`test_context_registry.py`:

**Registered the constant**: `gb_reduction_fraction_at_max_dose`=0.147
(BRONZE, DeFronzo et al. 1991, J Clin Endocrinol Metab, PMID:8923861 --
verified live via NCBI efetch this session; see `drug_interactions.py`'s
own `metformin_modifiers()` docstring for the full mechanism-weighting
investigation this constant resolves). The source is a placebo-
controlled, chronic (15-week), T2D tracer study: basal hepatic glucose
production fell 12.9 -> 11.0 umol/kg.min (-14.7%, P<0.01). BRONZE, not

PRODUCTION rate (a flux), while this platform's `Gb` is a steady-state

approximately the same %-concentration-reduction, explicitly flagged
as an approximation, not an exact derivation. The 0.147 value has no
named module-level constant (confirmed via grep -- it's an inline
literal inside `metformin_modifiers()`'s own return statement), so it's
duplicated as a literal in the new registration, same convention CKD
used for its own uncited-constant case.

### DONE — Fixed alcohol's glucose mechanism (Track 1 row 1.31)

First genuinely new Track 1 (biological realism) mechanism milestone
this session, following a dedicated `computational-biologist` scoping
fan-out dispatched specifically to find new Track 1 candidates (Track 5
provenance curation had grown thin on easy chunks, and none of chunks
11-20 count toward Track 1's own D1 composition-boundary audit
trigger). The agent's report was NOT trusted at face value -- every
load-bearing claim below was independently re-verified via live NCBI
efetch and, for the core bug, by directly executing the real composed
ODE.

**The finding**: `drug_interactions.py`'s `alcohol_modifiers()` was
already flagged (KNOWN BUGS #9-era citation audit) as having an
uncited effect magnitude. The fresh scoping pass found it was worse
than uncited -- it was ACTIVELY WRONG. The function reduced `Gb`
(`PathwayParameters`'s fasting glucose CONCENTRATION set-point), but
both real primary sources located directly contradict this:
- Siler SQ, Neese RA, Christiansen MP, Hellerstein MK. "The inhibition
  of gluconeogenesis following alcohol in humans." Am J Physiol.
  1998;275(5):E897-907. PMID:9815011 -- verified live via NCBI efetch
  twice. Normal men, overnight-fasted, 48g oral alcohol vs. placebo,
  stable-isotope tracers: "Hepatic glucose output decreased 12% after
  alcohol consumption... but did not change following the placebo,"
  and explicitly "no effect on plasma glucose concentrations."
- Shelmet JJ, Reichard GA, Skutches CL, Hoeldtke RD, Owen OE, Boden G.
  "Ethanol causes acute inhibition of carbohydrate, fat, and protein
  oxidation and insulin resistance." J Clin Invest. 1988;81(4):1137-45.
  PMID:3280601 -- verified live. IV ethanol (0.75g/kg), six normal
  males: real basal glucose appearance (-30%) and clamp glucose
  disposal (-36%) effects, but explicitly "had no effect on glucose
  tolerance" -- independent confirmation the fasting/ambient glucose
  CONCENTRATION itself doesn't move.

**Route-matched anchor choice**: Siler (oral, 48g), not Shelmet (IV),
since this platform's alcohol `DrugDose`/`ScenarioDefinition` events
are oral doses (`drug_scenarios.alcohol_before_meal()` converts grams
directly to `dose_mg`) -- the same "which regime does this function
actually represent" resolution already used for metformin's own p3/p1
removal and `NutrientSecretionPathway`'s Krezowski-vs-Nuttall choice.
Does not mean Shelmet's numbers are wrong -- route (oral vs. IV
first-pass hepatic metabolism) plausibly explains part of the
magnitude difference.

**Empirically confirmed the bug was worse than "wrong target,
uncited magnitude" alone would suggest**: because `Gb` is a
`PathwayParameters` field baked into the ODE's own basal state at
simulation setup (not a live, in-integration signal), the OLD
`alcohol_modifiers()` computed a single Gb value from
`dose.hours_since_ingestion` evaluated ONCE, then held it CONSTANT
for the entire simulated window. Directly verified: a fasted
(zero-meal), 48g-alcohol scenario under the old code produced a
glucose trajectory flat at 4934.1 uM for all 6 simulated hours --
it never actually resolved within one run, despite the function's own
docstring and the existing regression tests (`test_hours_before_
actually_changes_the_effect`, `test_alcohol_effect_resolves_as_time_
passes`) implying a real peak-then-resolve time course. The only
"time-varying" behavior came from comparing SEPARATE scenario runs
with different `hours_before` values, each producing a different but
still-constant-for-that-run wrong Gb -- not genuine in-simulation
resolution.

**The fix**: a new stateless (zero-species), genuinely time-varying
pathway, `biosim_ode.alcohol_hepatic_pathway.AlcoholHepaticPathway`,
modeled directly on `NutrientSecretionPathway`'s own established shape
(closed-form peak-then-decay curve, additive rule-11 signal, per-event
summing). Injects a transient, NEGATIVE contribution into the
ALREADY-EXISTING `hepatic_egp_delta` signal (confirmed already in
`coupling.py`'s `ADDITIVE_SIGNAL_KEYS`, so it correctly sums with
`HepGlucPathway`'s own contribution if both are active in one scenario,
e.g. a T2D patient on metformin who also has an alcohol dose) rather
than inventing a new signal key. Peak amplitude
(`ALCOHOL_EGP_REDUCTION_FRACTION_AT_TESTED_DOSE = 0.12`) is Siler's own
directly-reported figure, applied to this platform's own
`EGP_BASAL_MM_MIN`; dose scales linearly up to `ALCOHOL_TESTED_DOSE_G
= 48.0` (Siler's own tested dose) and caps there (no extrapolation past
tested data, matching the tirzepatide/pioglitazone convention). The
peak-then-decay TIMING SHAPE (peak at 2h, resolves by 6h) is explicitly
disclosed as an unanchored assumption carried over from the old
implementation's own timing curve -- neither citation reports a
time-resolved curve, only a single value over a multi-hour window.

**Deliberately NOT built as an `EGPParameters`/`HepGlucPathway` chronic
preset** (unlike T2D/hyperthyroidism/metformin) -- those all represent
CHRONIC, steady-state conditions where the elevated/suppressed EGP
rate is itself the ODE's own analytic fixed point. Alcohol is
fundamentally ACUTE and self-resolving -- the same category distinction
this platform already draws between `ExogenousInsulinPathway` (acute,
time-varying) and the chronic modifier-based drugs. Forcing alcohol
into the chronic-preset pattern would make the suppression CONSTANT
for the whole simulation, reproducing the exact bug being fixed.

`alcohol_modifiers()` now returns `{}` unconditionally, matching the
existing "this drug's real effect is ODE-coupled, not a static
modifier" pattern already used for GLP-1/SGLT2i/sulfonylureas.
`SimulationRunner._detect_alcohol()` collects ALL `Drug.ALCOHOL` events
in a scenario (unlike several sibling `_detect_*()` methods'
"first event wins" convention), since multiple doses at different
times are a real, plausible scenario and `AlcoholHepaticPathway`
correctly sums them.

**Corrected, not just re-passed, code that depended on the old
(wrong) behavior**: two existing tests
(`test_gb_threshold_margin_never_collapses_below_safety_bound`,
`test_gb_threshold_margin_clamp_bounds_the_insulin_spike` in
`test_physiology.py`) originally stacked a metformin dose WITH an
alcohol dose to demonstrate the `MIN_GB_THRESHOLD_MARGIN_MM` safety
clamp engaging. Verified directly that alcohol no longer contributes
to `Gb` at all (byte-identical result with/without the alcohol dose)
-- removed the now-inert dose from both tests rather than leaving dead
weight, and corrected their comments. A `personalizer.py` comment
naming alcohol as a Gb-reducing drug (with a specific, now-wrong
worked numeric example) was corrected. `drug_scenarios.
alcohol_before_meal()`'s docstring, previously "Mechanism: alcohol
inhibits gluconeogenesis... citation unverified," was corrected to
describe the real mechanism and cite the real PMIDs. The 4 pre-existing
tests in `test_drug_scenarios.py` (`TestAlcoholBeforeMealScenario`)
were NOT modified -- verified they still pass unchanged with the new
mechanism, since the qualitative direction (more recent alcohol ->
lower glucose peak; effect resolves with time) happens to hold with
both old and new mechanisms, just with different (now correctly-
anchored) magnitudes.

**Mandatory code-reviewer pass: APPROVE, 2 MEDIUM, both fixed.** The
reviewer independently re-fetched both PMIDs live, built a real
T2D+metformin+alcohol scenario and drove it through
`SimulationRunner._build_pathway()` directly to confirm
`HepGlucPathway` and `AlcoholHepaticPathway` correctly compose (both
target `hepatic_egp_delta`, `_combine_signal_values()` sums them,
confirmed via observed contributions `[0.0, -0.00384]` -> `-0.00384`),
and independently confirmed the byte-identical-Gb claim for the
`test_physiology.py` fix. Findings: (1) `MASTER_PLAN.md` Section 11's
own D2 population x mechanism coverage matrix still had a stale
"Alcohol" row claiming a 0.950 Gb factor / 5.053mM crossover that no
longer exists -- corrected, with the row removed and the "Alcohol's
own small effect..." bullet replaced with an explicit correction note;
(2) no committed regression test exercised `AlcoholHepaticPathway`
composed TOGETHER with `HepGlucPathway` (only the reviewer's own ad hoc
verification did) -- added
`test_hepatic_egp_delta_sums_across_alcohol_and_metformin_t2d` in
`test_simulation_api.py`, directly exercising `CompositePathway.
_combine_signal_values()` on both pathways' real signal outputs plus a
full composed-scenario run.

**Mandatory security-reviewer pass (Q5 -- dosing/hepatic-mechanism
change): 1 MEDIUM, fixed; 2 LOW, fixed.** Confirmed the REST-layer
50-event cap on `drug_events` (`ScenarioIn`'s own pre-existing
`max_length=50`) applies to alcohol events with no drug-type
carve-out, and confirmed each INDIVIDUAL dose's contribution is safe
by construction (the `dose_factor = min(dose_g/48.0, 1.0)` formula
saturates regardless of `dose_mg`'s magnitude -- verified `dose_g=1e6`
produces a byte-identical `peak_delta_mM_per_min` to `dose_g=48.0`).
**Real MEDIUM finding**: no ceiling on the AGGREGATE `hepatic_egp_delta`
when many doses' active windows overlap -- empirically drove the real
composed ODE with 50 near-simultaneous saturating alcohol doses (the
REST-legal worst case) and measured simulated glucose dropping to
~1.65 mM (severe-hypoglycemia range), despite every individual dose
being correctly bounded, since the raw additive signal has no floor
tying the AGGREGATE to the physical fact that hepatic glucose output
cannot fall below zero (unlike `HepGlucPathway`'s own Hill-inhibition
EGP, inherently bounded in `[0, egp_max]`). Fixed: `AlcoholHepaticPathway
.output_signals()` now floors the summed delta at `-egp_basal_mM_min`
(the aggregate can never imply more than 100% suppression of the
reference basal EGP at any instant), with a dedicated 50-dose
