### DONE — Added intermittent hypoxia's p1/p3 personalisation axis (Track 1 row 1.32)

Picked next per Track 1 priority order: alcohol (row 1.31) was Track 1
scoping candidate #1, this is candidate #2. Dispatched a
`computational-biologist` scoping pass to independently verify the
candidate citation before writing any code (per this project's own
"verify the candidate is real" discipline). The citation was then
independently re-verified a SECOND time, directly, by this session
(live NCBI `efetch`, matching the project's own "verified twice, by
two separate parties" convention) -- both fetches returned byte-
identical abstract text.

**Louis M, Punjabi NM. "Effects of acute intermittent hypoxia on
glucose metabolism in awake healthy volunteers." J Appl Physiol
(1985). 2009;106(5):1538-44. PMID:19265062.** n=13 healthy volunteers,
5h of intermittent hypoxia or normoxia during WAKEFULNESS (randomized
crossover, 2 separate days) -- oxyhemoglobin desaturation events
induced at 24.3 events/h average. IVGTT analyzed via the Bergman
minimal model directly (the same convention this platform's own p1/p3
are built on). Confirmed verbatim: "intermittent hypoxia was
associated with a decrease in S(I) [4.1 vs. 3.4 (mU/l)-1.min-1;
P=0.0179] and S(G) (1.9 vs. 1.3 min-1x10-2, P=0.0065)." Pancreatic
insulin secretion was "comparable" between conditions -- a real,
measured null.

**The scoping pass caught and corrected the original candidate's own
framing before any code was written**: it had been characterized as
an "insulin sensitivity" candidate, but the LARGER, more statistically
robust effect in the paper is on glucose effectiveness (S(G)/p1,
-31.6%, P=0.0065), not insulin sensitivity (S(I)/p3, -17.1%,
P=0.0179) -- a p3-only implementation would have captured only the
weaker half of the paper's own finding. Both factors are implemented.

**Architectural classification, decided deliberately, not defaulted**:
unlike alcohol (row 1.31), this is NOT a new stateful, time-varying ODE
pathway. The source measures only a single pre/post state -- no
repeat-IVGTT timepoint, no decay half-life, no washout kinetics at
all. Built as a static multiplicative personalisation-layer modifier
(new `intermittent_hypoxia_modifiers()` in `modifiers.py`, structurally
identical to the existing `sleep_modifiers()`), not a new coupled
pathway -- no new rule-11 ODE-coupling signal was needed or added.

**Implementation**: new `PhysiologicalProfile.desaturation_events_per_hour:
Optional[float] = None` field (validated finite and non-negative),
`intermittent_hypoxia_modifiers()` piecewise-linear between neutral
(1.0, 1.0) at 0 events/h and the paper's own two measured factors
(p3=3.4/4.1≈0.829, p1=1.3/1.9≈0.684) at 24.3 events/h, clamped (not
extrapolated) above 24.3 -- no dose-response data exists beyond this
single tested rate, matching this file's own established convention
(`sleep_modifiers()`, `PIOGLITAZONE_P3_DOSE_MG`). `secretion_scale`
deliberately left untouched, per the paper's own measured Results null
(its broader discussion/hypothesis sentence about OSA in general
speculates about secretion too, but the measured Results explicitly
report it unchanged -- implemented what was measured, not the
narrative gloss). Wired into `PhysiologicalPersonalizer.personalize()`
alongside the existing layers, plus REST wire-schema/service-layer
plumbing (`PhysiologicalProfileIn.desaturation_events_per_hour`,
bounded `ge=0, le=200` as a defense-in-depth ceiling -- the modifier's
own internal clamp at 24.3 makes anything above that inert regardless).

**Double-counting audit, disclosed rather than assumed clear**: genuinely
orthogonal to `sleep_modifiers()` (the source study deliberately induces
hypoxia DURING WAKEFULNESS, explicitly isolating it from sleep loss/
fragmentation) and to `CortisolPathway`/`stress_level` (the source
directly measured "serum cortisol levels after intermittent hypoxia and
normoxia were similar" -- a stronger, directly-measured null than sleep
restriction's own disclosed cortisol risk, which only has a
non-correlation). No sympathetic-nervous-system/catecholamine pathway
exists anywhere in this codebase to double-count against (the source's
own R-R-interval sympathetic-activation finding has no analogue here).

**Evidence-strength caveats, disclosed honestly, not papered over**:
single small study (n=13), single hypoxia intensity (no dose-response
curve), no dispersion statistics reported in the abstract for either
factor (P-values only), and no independent human minimal-model
replication located this session. A directionally different result in a
materially different regime (Mackenzie et al. 2012, PMID:22278428:
sustained moderate hypoxia + exercise in T2D patients IMPROVED insulin
sensitivity by HOMA-IR/FIRI) is disclosed as a real caveat, not a
contradiction -- different exposure pattern, different population,
different outcome measure. This axis is scoped explicitly to the
RESTING, cyclical-desaturation regime this source actually measured,
not a general OSA/sleep-apnea disease-state claim.

Mandatory code-reviewer pass: APPROVE, 1 LOW, fixed -- `profile.py`'s
`__post_init__` used a plain `< 0` check for the new field (silently
accepts NaN, since `float('nan') < 0` is `False` in Python), unlike
`sleep_hours`'s own chained-range check which incidentally rejects NaN
too. Fixed with an explicit `math.isfinite()` check for parity, plus a
new regression test. Mandatory security-reviewer pass (Q5, new
physiology/disease-mechanism composition path): APPROVE, 0 CRITICAL/
HIGH, 1 MEDIUM already resolved on disk by the time of review (the same
NaN-validation fix above, independently confirmed fixed and tested),
1 LOW informational note (no upper bound on the field at the dataclass
level, but confirmed harmless since the modifier's own internal clamp
makes any value above 24.3 inert regardless). Also independently
confirmed: the existing generic `_PARAM_BOUNDS` clamp in
`personalizer.py` already covers p1/p3 after ALL modifiers compose
(not hypoxia-specific, needed no new code) -- live-tested stacking
sleep restriction + intermittent hypoxia + GDM + CKD simultaneously,
confirmed both parameters stay comfortably within bounds with no
clamping engaged.

+17 tests (`test_physiology.py`: 16 -- modifier unit tests covering
zero/neutral, exact reference-rate match, above-reference clamping,
monotonic interpolation, negative/NaN rejection, the p1-vs-p3 asymmetry,
secretion non-touch, profile-level validation including the NaN fix,
personalizer end-to-end composition, `validate_y0(tolerance=1e-8)`
fixed-point check, and composition with `sleep_hours`;
`test_rest_api.py`: 2 -- end-to-end REST composition (confirms the
calibrated effect actually reaches simulated glucose output, per this
project's own G1 "survives composition" discipline) and out-of-range
rejection). RED-proofed via a scoped `git stash` on all touched source
files -- all discriminating tests failed cleanly pre-fix (a collection-
level `ImportError` for the physiology tests since the function didn't
exist yet, assertion failures for the REST tests), then again in

### DONE (negative result, no code change) — Composition-Boundary Behavioral Audit, rows 1.24-1.32

First-ever run of the D1 protocol (formalized but never executed). Was
overdue: 6 new drug/disease milestones landed since row 1.23's own
marker (CKD 1.24, pioglitazone 1.25, sleep restriction 1.26, dietary
protein 1.28, alcohol 1.31, intermittent hypoxia 1.32), past the
protocol's own 5+ trigger. Just-published Section 2a roadmap flagged
this as the immediate blocker before implementing any more `p3`-
touching mechanism (rows 1.33-1.36), so run now rather than deferred.

**Method**: launched the real production REST server (`uvicorn
biosim_rest:create_app --factory`, matching `/verify`'s own convention),
drove `POST /simulate` across each mechanism's full dose/severity
range, composed with a T2D preset, both fasted and real-meal scenarios,
per the protocol's own step 2.

**No silently-flattened signal (the bug class this protocol exists to
catch) was found.** Every mechanism's calibrated effect reaches
simulated output and genuinely differentiates dose-to-dose/severity-
to-severity:
- Pioglitazone: correctly FLAT at 7.5/15mg (the paper's own
  empirically-null anchor points, per row 1.25's own disclosure -- not
  a bug), differentiates at 30/45mg in both healthy and T2D.
- CKD/sleep restriction/protein/intermittent hypoxia: all differentiate
  monotonically across their own tested ranges, both standalone and
  composed with T2D.
- Alcohol: initial sweep used the wrong wire-format units (passed grams
  directly as `dose_mg` instead of the established `dose_mg = grams *
  1000` convention documented in `drug_scenarios.py` -- a testing
  mistake, not a platform bug, caught and corrected mid-audit). With
  correct units, the nadir differentiates cleanly (5.0000 -> 4.9330mM
  at 48g, healthy fasted; 5.5445 -> 5.4840mM composed with metformin+
  T2D), correctly clamps at the 48g tested-dose ceiling (72g produces
  an identical result to 48g, not a larger one), and composes correctly.
- Intermittent hypoxia + T2D, FASTED (no meal): stays exactly flat
  (6.5000mM regardless of exposure rate) -- confirmed this is the
  CORRECT fixed-point behavior, not a flattening bug: a pure p1/p3
  multiplicative modifier cannot move a basal steady state, since
  (G-Gb) and X are both exactly zero there by construction --
  independently matches `validate_y0()`'s own finding for this
  mechanism.

**One real, interesting, but NOT actionable finding**: pioglitazone's
and sleep restriction's `p3`-driven effect on `glucose_peak_mM`
specifically is dramatically smaller in RELATIVE terms when composed
with the T2D preset than in healthy (e.g. pioglitazone 45mg: -1.68%
healthy vs. -0.054% T2D, ~31x smaller). Investigated directly (not
assumed): confirmed via `PhysiologicalPersonalizer.personalize()` that
`p3` itself moves by the EXACT expected multiplicative amount in both
cases (T2D-alone p3=4.968e-7 -> +pioglitazone 8.383e-7, ratio
0.55->0.928, matching the drug's own 1.6875x multiplier applied
correctly to T2D's own 0.55x baseline) -- `p3` is nowhere near its
`_PARAM_BOUNDS` floor (1e-8) in either case, so this is NOT a silent
clamp. It is genuine nonlinear ODE sensitivity: `glucose_peak_mM`
specifically is less sensitive to `p3` changes when baseline `p3` is
already low, since peak height is dominated by early absorption/`p1`
dynamics while `p3`'s effect (mediated through the slower remote-
insulin compartment X) shows up more in AUC/time-to-return than in
peak height. Not a bug, and outside the scope of a code fix -- noted
here as a real, disclosed observation for anyone building a future
`validate_pioglitazone()`/`validate_sleep_restriction()` benchmark:
`glucose_peak_mM` alone would be a weak/misleading discriminator for
either mechanism in the T2D population; AUC or time-to-return would
carry more signal.

**Quantitative finding that concretely validates the Section 2a
roadmap's own sequencing decision**: swept the most extreme currently-
composable disease/physiological stack (gestational_diabetes +
insulin_resistant + hypothyroidism + chronic_kidney_disease +
sleep_hours=5 + desaturation_events_per_hour=24.3) and confirmed `p3`'s
own `_PARAM_BOUNDS` floor (1e-8, with NO `clamp_warnings` equivalent --
only `Gb`/`G_threshold` have one, from row 1.23) is **not yet breached**
by any currently-shippable combination -- the closest observed value
(`p3`=5.65e-8, ratio 0.0626 of default) sits ~5.7x above the floor, not
imminently clamped. But arithmetically demonstrated (by composing the
same stack with each Tier A candidate's own reported factor from
Section 2a: indinavir ~0.66, growth hormone ~0.61, menstrual-luteal
~0.516) that stacking even ONE of the newly-scoped candidates on top of
this already-extreme base would bring the composed `p3` within roughly
2x of the floor, and stacking two would very plausibly breach it
silently, with zero warning surfaced anywhere today. This is exactly
the concern Section 2a's own sequencing already anticipated
(implement rows 1.33-1.36/1.29 only after this audit) -- now backed by
real numbers rather than suspicion alone. **Recommended follow-on
(not built here, a design decision for whoever implements rows
1.33-1.36)**: extend row 1.23's `clamp_warnings` convention to cover
`p3` (and likely `p1`, `ke`, `secretion_scale` -- the other
`_PARAM_BOUNDS`-clamped fields with no warning today), the same
mechanism-agnostic fix already proven to work correctly for `Gb`/
`G_threshold` across every mechanism the D2 matrix has swept so far.

No code changed -- this is a pure diagnostic pass; the one finding
worth act­ing on (a `p3`/`p1`/`ke`/`secretion_scale` clamp-warning
extension) is recorded as a recommendation for the next implementer,
not built speculatively here.

**Audit marker**: ran at commit `42045b2`, 6 mechanisms swept (rows

New `Drug.HYDROCHLOROTHIAZIDE` -- this platform's FIRST antihypertensive

### DONE — Added growth hormone's p3 mechanism (Track 1 row 1.35)

Picked next per the Section 2a roadmap's own sequencing -- third and
final Tier A candidate. Independently re-verified both citations live
before writing any code.

**Fowelin J, Attvall S, von Schenck H, Smith U, Lager I.
"Characterization of the insulin-antagonistic effect of growth hormone
in man." Diabetologia. 1991;34(7):500-6. PMID:1916055.** n=11 healthy
subjects, GH infused at 3 rates for 1h, euglycemic clamp + isotopic
glucose turnover, vs. a saline control. Confirmed verbatim: "The
insulin-antagonistic effect of growth hormone started after
approximately 2 h, was maximal after 4-5 h (approximately 39%
inhibition of glucose infusion rate between control and growth hormone
24 mU.kg-1.h-1) and lasted for 6-7 h after peak levels... Growth
hormone infusion of 12 mU.kg-1.h-1 induced a similar insulin-
antagonistic effect as the higher infusion rate whereas 6 mU.kg-1.h-1
induced a smaller response." Corroborated directionally (no extractable
magnitude) by Krag et al. 2007, PMID:17132823 (independently
re-verified live): "Insulin resistance was induced by GH irrespective
of concomitant acipimox."

New `Drug.GROWTH_HORMONE`, `GROWTH_HORMONE_P3_FACTOR`=0.61 (1-0.39).
**Deliberately NOT dose-scaled, unlike every other acute drug mechanism
in this file (indinavir, hydrochlorothiazide, both earlier this
session)** -- a genuinely different design decision, chosen and
disclosed rather than defaulted to the established ramp-then-clamp
convention: the source abstract is internally UNIT-INCONSISTENT
(Methods: "6, 12 or 24 mU.kg-1.min-1"; Results: "growth hormone 6
mU.kg-1.h-1... 12... 24..." for the SAME three numbers -- a 60x
discrepancy in the same abstract), so a dose-scaled implementation
would have to silently pick one unit reading, manufacturing false
precision from an ambiguous source. Even setting units aside, the
reported shape is SATURATING, not linear (12 and 24 produce a
"similar" effect) -- a linear ramp would misrepresent this specific
source's own shape regardless. `dose_mg` is therefore used purely as a
PRESENCE flag (>0 = GH administered), not a scaling axis.
`secretion_scale`/`hepatic_egp_delta` deliberately NOT touched -- the
source's own hepatic-component mention has no separate extractable
magnitude (same KNOWN BUG #14 avoidance as the prior two mechanisms).
Confirmed `validate_y0(tolerance=1e-8)` clean and no `_PARAM_BOUNDS`
clamp interaction. Zero double-counting risk confirmed: grepped
`packages/` directly -- the only pre-existing GH references are
unrelated entity-registry metadata (a UniProt "growth hormone" protein
entity in `registry_seed.py`, and a test mentioning IGF-1's own
description), neither a `Drug`/modifier mechanism.

**Forward-looking non-overlap note with row 1.37 (acromegaly, not yet
implemented)**: structurally the same underlying mechanism (chronic GH
excess) at a different exposure duration, but non-overlapping by
construction, not coincidence -- this drug-dose mechanism touches ONLY
p3 (no Gb magnitude extractable from this acute-infusion source), while
acromegaly's own citation (Moller et al. 1992, PMID:1569148) will
supply ONLY a Gb magnitude (no p3 magnitude extractable there either).
A scenario combining both would compose correctly without double-
counting either number, since neither is borrowed from the other study.

Mandatory code-reviewer pass: APPROVE, 1 MEDIUM (fixed), 1 LOW (noted,
consistent with established pattern, not fixed) -- the MEDIUM was a
genuine self-contradiction in my own first-draft docstring: it claimed
the flat presence-flag design "match[es] the study's own lowest
effective rate" (implying a conservative, lower-bound effect), but the
code and its own test (`test_different_nonzero_doses_produce_the_
identical_factor`) actually apply the study's MAXIMAL/24 mU.kg-1.h-1-
derived effect at any nonzero dose, including a trace amount -- the
opposite of what the comment claimed. Fixed by correcting the docstring
to state plainly that the maximal-effect magnitude is applied
regardless of dose (since no real number exists for the lower tier to
use instead -- inventing one would fabricate precision, the same
row-1.30 precedent this file already cites elsewhere). The LOW
(a redundant "reduces p3" test fully subsumed by the exact-match test)
was left as-is -- consistent with the same redundant-but-clarifying
test pattern already present in the indinavir/hydrochlorothiazide
chunks immediately preceding it, not a new inconsistency. Not
security-reviewer-gated per Q5: small, well-precedented diff, no new
infrastructure.

### DONE (negative result, no code change) — Formally parked nicotine (Track 1 row 1.42)

Picked next per the Section 2a roadmap's own sequencing -- the second
informally-scoped candidate from the earlier alcohol-fix fan-out
(priority candidate #4, explicitly lower priority than atorvastatin
due to a flagged dose-route mismatch). Unlike atorvastatin, this
needed a fresh scoping pass, not just a citation re-check, per the
roadmap's own note ("does this platform's Drug/DrugDose model have a
sensible unit for a nicotine dose at all?").

Dispatched a `computational-biologist` scoping pass. Independently
re-verified its single most load-bearing citation live (Axelsson et
al. 2001, PMID:11422660) before accepting its recommendation, per this
project's own "agent output is a hypothesis, never truth" discipline.

**Finding, confirmed sound**: the healthy-subject effect is a verified
NULL across three independent controlled designs, not a missing
citation:
- **Axelsson T, Jansson PA, Smith U, Eliasson B. "Nicotine infusion
  acutely impairs insulin sensitivity in type 2 diabetic patients but
  not in healthy subjects." J Intern Med. 2001;249(6):539-44.
  PMID:11422660.** IV nicotine infusion (0.3 microg/kg/min, 2h) during
  a 4h euglycaemic clamp -- the cleanest possible single-route,
  unambiguous-unit dose of any candidate found. n=6 T2D + n=6 matched
  healthy controls. "This insulin resistance was further aggravated by
  the nicotine infusion in DM2 but not in Ctr (4.6 +/- 0.3 vs. **10.9
  +/- 0.3** mg kg-1 LBM min-1)" -- the healthy arm's GIR is EXACTLY
  unchanged (10.9 -> 10.9) at the reported precision. T2D factor
  4.6/6.7=0.687 (-31.3%) IS real and extractable, but disease-
  conditional only.
- **Morgan et al. 2004, Metabolism, PMID:15131760** -- 14mg transdermal
  patch (a real, single-route mg dose), n=34, 75g OGTT: every reported
  endpoint non-significant (fasting QUICKI P=.11, 60-min glucose
  P=.12, glucose AUC P=.33, insulin AUC P=.79) -- yet the abstract's
  own Conclusion sentence says nicotine patches "may lead to" mild
  hyperglycemia/lowered sensitivity DESPITE every p-value failing
  significance. Flagged explicitly as a fabricated-support trap this
  pass avoided (this project has been burned by conclusion-vs-results
  mismatches before -- exactly the discipline this catch validates).
- **Mora-Martinez et al. 2004, PMID:18370691** -- transdermal, n=12
  healthy, clamp: also null (P=.60/.34 across two subgroups).
- **A within-study route-dissociation finding directly confirms the
  originally-flagged confound**: Attvall et al. 1993, PMID:8463765 --
  matched plasma nicotine levels via smoking vs. snuff (non-combustion)
  in the same n=7 healthy subjects: "Smoking, but not snuffing,
  impaired insulin action" -- i.e. the positive findings in the
  smoking literature are attributable to COMBUSTION products, not
  nicotine itself.

**Genuine, unresolved conflict disclosed, not resolved by fiat**:
Eliasson et al. 1996, PMID:8790020 (observational, no dose, n=20 vs.
20) concludes "nicotine is the major constituent in cigarette smoke
that leads to insulin resistance" for CHRONIC exposure -- weaker
evidence (cross-sectional, no randomization, no dose) than the acute
null studies above, but a real finding from the same research group
pointing the other way. The acute-vs-chronic regimes may genuinely
differ; this platform has no chronic-nicotine anchor with a dose
either way.

**Architectural note, disclosed for whoever revisits this**: the one
real magnitude (Axelsson's T2D -31.3%) would require an unprecedented
pattern -- `drug_modifiers()` currently has no disease-state-
conditional-MAGNITUDE mechanism (only the sulfonylurea/T1D on/off
gating bypass in `personalizer.py` exists today), so implementing
this single number would need new architecture, not just a citation.

**Decision: formally PARKED, not implemented** -- matching the same
"documented negative result, not a forced fix" discipline already
established for the NEFA basal-vs-obese candidate (row 1.19) and the
Section 2a documented negatives (niacin, coeliac disease, chronic
pancreatitis, etc.). Named unblock route recorded in `MASTER_PLAN.md`

**Valdes CT, Elkind-Hirsch KE. "Intravenous glucose tolerance test-
derived insulin sensitivity changes during the menstrual cycle." J Clin
Endocrinol Metab. 1991;72(3):642-6. PMID:1997519.** n=8 cycling women,
tolbutamide-modified IVGTT analyzed via the Bergman MINIMAL MODEL
directly -- the same convention this platform's own p1/p3 are built
on, and the paper's own stated motivation ("this method has never been
applied" to the menstrual cycle before). Confirmed verbatim: "The mean
SI... decreased in a stepwise fashion from the follicular level of 6.20
+/- 0.91 to a midcycle level of 4.95 +/- 0.73 and was lowest in the
luteal phase (3.20 +/- 0.25; P less than 0.007). No change in glucose
effectiveness occurred as a function of the menstrual cycle."

**A real correction to the original candidate scoping, caught while
implementing, not carried over uncritically**: the abstract's own
CLOSING sentence states "these findings indicate a significant decrease
in insulin sensitivity in the luteal phase... but NO SIGNIFICANT CHANGE
AT MIDCYCLE." The original scoping's proposed 3-point piecewise ramp
(1.0/0.798/0.516 across follicular/midcycle/luteal) would have modelled
midcycle as a real, if smaller, effect -- directly contradicted by the
paper's own explicit disclaimer. Corrected the design to a CATEGORICAL
modifier instead of a continuous ramp: new `MenstrualCyclePhase` enum
(FOLLICULAR/MIDCYCLE/LUTEAL) on `PhysiologicalProfile`, new
`menstrual_cycle_modifiers()` returning neutral for None/FOLLICULAR/

this file's own established null-zone discipline already applied to

appropriately discrete (matching the source's own 3 sampled timepoints,
not an invented continuous "cycle day" interpolation this single small
study cannot support). p1 confirmed untouched per the same source's own
direct null.

normal cycle physiology, and from any future PCOS entry). Double-
counting audit: zero prior reference to menstrual cycle/luteal/
follicular/midcycle phase anywhere in the codebase, confirmed by grep.

### DONE (scoping only, no code change) — Scoped Cushing's syndrome, found and documented a structural CortisolPathway ceiling bug (Track 1 row 1.38)

Next per the roadmap's own recommended sequencing (item 4) -- row 1.38
was explicitly flagged as needing a design decision, not just a
citation, before implementing. Dispatched a `computational-biologist`
scoping pass rather than guessing at the decision.

**Q1, confirmed by reverse-engineering the code's own arithmetic**:
`CORTISOL_BASAL_NM=0.28`/`EC50_GR_NM=0.15` in `cortisol_pathway.py` are
an internal RELATIVE scale ("basal-equivalents"), not real nanomolar
plasma cortisol -- `for_prednisone()`'s own conversion chain shows
`CORTISOL_BASAL_NM` appearing only as a multiplier on a dimensionless
mg-ratio, with no distribution-volume term anywhere (confirmed
verbatim in that function's own docstring). This rules out plugging a
literal literature cortisol concentration in directly -- only a
within-study RATIO (matching this project's own established convention
for PCOS/CKD/GCK-MODY) can be used safely.

**Q2, a real ratio WAS found, independently live-verified (full text,
not just abstract)**: **Ježková J, Ďurovcová V, Wenchich L, et al.
"The relationship of mitochondrial dysfunction and the development of
insulin resistance in Cushing's syndrome." Diabetes Metab Syndr Obes.
2019;12:1459-1471. PMID:31695455** -- open access, fetched in full via
Europe PMC. Table 1, morning (08:00) plasma cortisol, same RIA assay:
controls 527+/-51 nmol/L (n=22) vs. active Cushing's 822+/-80 nmol/L
(n=24, P<0.05) -- ratio 822/527=1.560.

**Q3, this is where the chunk stopped being straightforward**: composing
this ratio through the EXISTING `CortisolPathway` machinery (raising
`cortisol_basal` by 1.560x, recomputing `gr_occ_basal` to avoid KNOWN
BUG #10's exact fixed-point-drift pattern) lands `p3_modifier` at only
~0.971 -- a ~3% reduction, nowhere close to the original candidate
citation's clamp-derived 0.513 ratio (Nosadini et al. 1983, PMID:6348064).
**Independently re-verified this is a genuine structural ceiling, not a
ratio-tuning problem**: `p3_modifier = max(0.3, 1.0 -
CORTISOL_P3_SENSITIVITY * excess_gr)`, and `excess_gr` is bounded above
by `1.0 - GR_REFERENCE` (~0.2817) because `gr_occ` is a Hill-activation
output that asymptotically approaches but never reaches 1.0. With the
current, UNCITED `CORTISOL_P3_SENSITIVITY=0.25`, this means
`p3_modifier` can NEVER fall below ~0.9296 no matter how large the
cortisol input is -- confirmed twice: directly sweeping `gr_occ` from
0.72 to 0.99999 in `output_signals()` (converges on exactly 0.9296,
matching the closed-form calculation), and running the REAL production
`SimulationRunner` with a glucocorticoid `DrugEvent` swept from 10mg to
500mg (glucose peak moves only 10.5044 -> 10.5058 mM across a 50x dose
range). **This is a pre-existing bug in an ALREADY-SHIPPED mechanism,
not something introduced by this scoping pass** -- it directly
contradicts `glucocorticoid_modifiers()`'s own docstring ("Acute
effect: reduces p3 ~30%") and that same function's own note that
`CortisolPathway` is the SOLE path the real `SimulationRunner` uses for
glucocorticoid p3/Gb effects, meaning the documented ~30% figure has
never actually reached simulated output. Also affects `stress_level`
(shares the same `p3_modifier` formula). `gb_modifier` is NOT similarly
capped (different, unbounded-until-soft-saturation formula), so fasting-
glucose elevation still scales with dose -- only the p3/insulin-
sensitivity side is affected.

**Q4, a genuine unresolved literature conflict, disclosed not
resolved**: Nosadini's own abstract attributes its 0.513 ratio to a
RESPONSIVENESS/Vmax defect ("without any significant difference in the
levels of insulin half-maximally effective"), not a sensitivity/ED50
defect (which is what Bergman `p3` represents) -- directly undermining
whether 0.513 should ever have been mapped to `p3` at all. **Cohen P,
Barzilai N, Barzilai D, Karnieli E. Metabolism. 1986;35(8):744-9.
PMID:3526086** ("Sensitivity to insulin was decreased in all three
abnormal groups") argues the opposite. **Tessari P, et al. JCEM.
1989;68(2):256-62. PMID:2645306** confirms impairment "at each clamp
step" (i.e. even at more physiological insulin levels than Nosadini's
supraphysiological 1200 mU/m²/min) but has no extractable quantitative
ratio in the abstract (paywalled). All three citations independently
live-verified.

**Decision: park row 1.38, do not force an implementation.** Shipping
route (a) now, given the structural ceiling and the unresolved
mechanism-shape conflict, would produce a Cushing's preset with a
barely-perceptible and possibly wrong-shaped effect -- worse than no
preset at all for a condition this clinically significant. Route (b)
(a static disease-state modifier) remains not recommended, unchanged
from the original scoping, for the same double-counting risk with
`CortisolPathway`/`stress_level`/glucocorticoid dosing. Added a new
open item to `MASTER_PLAN.md` Section 8 (cross-cutting housekeeping
backlog) documenting the `CORTISOL_P3_SENSITIVITY` ceiling bug in full,
recommending a dedicated future chunk to derive a literature-anchored
value and resolve the sensitivity-vs-responsiveness conflict as part of
the same fix -- at which point row 1.38's own 1.560 ratio (PMID:31695455)
is immediately ready to use with no further citation work needed.

No code changed this pass (pure scoping, matching this project's own
"DONE (scoping only, no code change)" pattern from the Track 4.4 GEM
scoping and nicotine's own row 1.42) -- no test suite change, no review
pass owed.

`MASTER_PLAN.md` row 1.38 marked PARKED with the full finding; a new
open item added to Section 8's housekeeping backlog.

### DONE — Fixed CORTISOL_P3_SENSITIVITY's unreachable floor and a related p3_eff clamp-bypass gap (Section 8 housekeeping)

Picked up the housekeeping item logged during row 1.38's own scoping
pass. `cortisol_pathway.py`'s `p3_modifier = max(0.3, 1.0 -
CORTISOL_P3_SENSITIVITY * excess_gr)` had an uncited constant (0.25)
with a structural consequence: `excess_gr` is bounded above by `1.0 -
GR_REFERENCE` (~0.2817), a Hill-saturation ceiling, so `p3_modifier`
could never fall below ~0.9296 (a ~7% max reduction) regardless of
cortisol level -- independently verified via a `gr_occ` sweep and a
real `SimulationRunner` glucocorticoid-dose sweep (10-500mg moved
glucose peak only 10.5044->10.5058 mM).

Dispatched a `literature-curator` agent to find a real, quantitative
insulin-SENSITIVITY (not Vmax/responsiveness) anchor. Found: **Rizza
RA, Mandarino LJ, Gerich JE. "Cortisol-induced insulin resistance in
man: impaired suppression of glucose production and stimulation of
glucose utilization due to a postreceptor detect of insulin action." J
Clin Endocrinol Metab. 1982;54(1):131-8. PMID:7033265** -- already
cited in this module, a 24h IV cortisol infusion (2 ug/kg/min) in 6
healthy volunteers vs. saline, a known controlled cortisol elevation
(measured ratio 37/14=2.643 -- the abstract's own "~4-fold" phrasing
does not match its own numbers, disclosed rather than used uncritically)
with two reported ED50 shifts: hepatic EGP-suppression (81->31 uU/mL)
and peripheral glucose-utilization (104->64 uU/mL). Only the
PERIPHERAL shift is used (target p3_modifier=64/104=0.6154 at the
measured ratio) -- primarily a shape-matching argument (Bergman p3
represents peripheral disposal specifically), secondarily because
using the hepatic figure would be a redundant representation of the
same finding if a scenario ever composed both CortisolPathway and the
separate HepGlucPathway/EGPParameters mechanism (confirmed via direct
code reading that no such coupling exists today, so this is not a
literal double-count, just the wrong-shape argument reinforced).

`CORTISOL_P3_SENSITIVITY` re-derived (not hand-tuned) to ~1.9422,
computed the same way `GR_OCC_BASAL` is (solved algebraically from the
Rizza anchor, not hardcoded) so it can never drift out of sync with
`GR_REFERENCE`/`EC50_GR_NM`/`HILL_GR`/`CORTISOL_BASAL_NM`. New
theoretical floor as cortisol->infinity: ~0.453 (up from ~0.9296).
Disclosed literature conflict, not silently resolved: Nosadini et al.
1983 (PMID:6348064, row 1.38's own original candidate anchor) reports
a similar-looking 0.513 ratio but attributes it to a RESPONSIVENESS/
Vmax defect explicitly ("without any significant difference in the
levels of insulin half-maximally effective"), not sensitivity/ED50 --
Rizza's number is used specifically because it matches the SHAPE p3
represents, not because Nosadini is wrong.

### DONE (scoping only, no code shipped) — Second attempt at row 1.38 found a deeper, pre-existing CortisolPathway structural bug

With the `CORTISOL_P3_SENSITIVITY` blocker resolved, attempted row
1.38 (Cushing's syndrome) a second time. Built the full implementation:
`CortisolParameters.for_cushings()` (`cortisol_basal =
CORTISOL_BASAL_NM * 1.560`, the Jezkova et al. 2019 ratio already
found and verified during the first scoping pass; `gr_occ_basal`
recomputed via `hill_activation()`, matching KNOWN BUG #10's own "never
leave a Hill-relaxation basal out of sync" lesson), a new
`ScenarioDefinition.cushings_syndrome` field composable with
`stress_level`/glucocorticoid dosing through the same shared
`CortisolPathway` instance `_detect_cortisol()` already builds for
those, and full `runner.py`/REST wiring. A quick t=0 check matched the
predicted `p3_modifier~=0.778` exactly.

**Before finalizing, verified the composed effect over a realistic
simulation window, not just at t=0 -- and it did not hold.**
`validate_y0()` flagged CRH as not a fixed point (`d/dt=-0.0989`), and
integrating 4 hours showed the effect genuinely decaying: `p3_modifier`
moved from 0.778 at t=0 to 0.863 by t=4h -- the intended chronic
disease effect visibly weakening by nearly half within a single
simulated meal.

Traced this to a genuine algebraic impossibility, not a wrong
constant -- the same class of bug as KNOWN BUG #12 (NEFA), where no
finite parameter choice permits an exact fixed point and a
normalization/restructuring is needed instead of a constant swap.
`CortisolPathway.dydt()`'s `dCortisol` formula requires `y0.crh ==
p.crh_basal` exactly for the Cortisol state to be a fixed point (since
`cortisol_production` scales with `crh/crh_basal`); `dCRH`'s own
formula requires `y0.crh == crh_basal*(1+stress_level*2)*
suppression(gr_occ_basal)` for the CRH state to be one. Both hold
simultaneously ONLY when `(1+stress_level*2)*suppression(gr_occ_basal)
== 1` exactly -- satisfied only by the trivial default case (stress=0,
gr_occ_basal==GR_REFERENCE) this code was originally built and tested
against.

**Confirmed this is NOT a Cushing's-specific bug -- it independently
affects the ALREADY-SHIPPED `stress_level` feature, alone, with no
Cushing's/dose involved at all**: `CortisolParameters(stress_level=1.0)`
fails `validate_y0()` (`CRH: d/dt=0.693147`). This has been silently
present since `stress_level` was built -- undetected because every
existing test only checks the glucose peak shape, never a
long-trajectory CRH invariant, the exact same blind-spot class KNOWN
BUG #10 was originally found through.

Likely fix, not applied here: normalize `cortisol_production`'s
crh-scaling term against the CURRENT parameters' own `crh_target`
(`crh / crh_target(gr_occ_basal, stress_level)` in place of the raw
`crh / crh_basal` ratio), mirroring NEFA's own `suppression_ratio`
normalization exactly, so whatever CRH's true feedback-adjusted steady
state is, cortisol production balances clearance there by
construction, for any `stress_level`/`gr_occ_basal` combination. Not
fixed in this pass -- this changes already-validated `stress_level`/
glucocorticoid-dosing dynamics and needs its own careful
fix-and-full-revalidation pass, not a drive-by change mid-
implementation of an unrelated row.

**Decision: reverted the entire in-progress implementation.** Confirmed
via `git status`/`git diff` clean back to the `CORTISOL_P3_SENSITIVITY`
commit -- no code shipped this pass, matching this project's own
"pure scoping, no code change" pattern (Track 4.4's own GEM scoping,
this same row's own first parking). Shipping a disease preset whose
own effect visibly decays as a modeling artifact, not real biology,
would be worse than not shipping it at all.

`MASTER_PLAN.md` row 1.38 re-parked with the full second-attempt
finding appended to its own history (not overwriting the first
attempt's record); a new Section 8 housekeeping item added for the
CRH/Cortisol structural fix, recommending a dedicated future chunk
that also closes the exact blind spot (a long-trajectory CRH-invariant
regression test for `stress_level` alone) that let this go undetected
since the feature was first built.

### DONE (no code shipped) — Attempted the CRH/Cortisol structural fix, found the first approach was wrong, reverted

Picked up the Section 8 housekeeping item logged during the second
Cushing's attempt. Tried the recommended NEFA-style normalization:
`cortisol_production`'s crh-scaling term changed from `crh/crh_basal`
to `crh/crh_reference`, where `crh_reference =
crh_steady_state(crh_basal, stress_level, gr_occ_basal)` is a new
helper computed once from the instance's own basal parameters (mirrors
`GR_OCC_BASAL`'s own "derive, don't hardcode a duplicate literal"
precedent); `basal_state()`'s own CRH component updated to use the same
helper instead of the raw `crh_basal` parameter.

This DID close the fixed-point gap: `validate_y0()` came back clean for
every case tried (default, `stress_level=1.0` alone, prednisone alone,
and a Cushing's-style elevated `gr_occ_basal`), and a 7-day integration
of the Cushing's-style case showed the state was now genuinely stable
(no drift at all, vs. the previous ~0.778->0.863 decay by 4h).

**Before committing, ran the FULL suite -- not just the fixed-point
checks -- and 5 tests failed**, all `stress_level`-related
(`test_stress_raises_cortisol` and 4 others). Investigating why revealed
the fix, while algebraically consistent, was WRONG: normalizing against
`crh`'s own target makes `cortisol_production` always reduce to exactly
`cortisol_basal` at the fixed point, REGARDLESS of how elevated CRH's
target is -- silently eliminating `stress_level`'s entire steady-state
effect on cortisol, not just the unwanted transient drift. Reading the
failing tests confirmed this wasn't incidental: each one integrates
from `y0` and checks that a STRESSED trajectory's final cortisol
exceeds the default's -- the ONLY reason that ever passed before was the
original bug's own unintended transient drift (CRH starting low,
dragging cortisol up as it rose toward its true, buggy-but-elevated
target). There was no other mechanism by which `stress_level` affected
cortisol in this model.

This surfaced a real, unresolved design question, not just an
implementation bug: was the original intent "stress begins at t=0,
watch a physiologically-real onset transient develop" (in which case a
non-fixed-point `y0` is INTENTIONAL, the same category as
`for_metformin()`'s own documented non-fixed-point onset, KNOWN BUG
#14's closing note) -- or "a stressed/diseased patient is already at
their own chronic steady state throughout" (needed for any disease-
state preset like Cushing's, matching every OTHER disease preset's own
convention of starting already-diseased at t=0)? The correct general
fix likely needs the STEADY-STATE cortisol value to genuinely move with
`stress_level`/`gr_occ_basal` (not cancel out to a constant), which
requires solving a genuinely COUPLED nonlinear fixed point --
`cortisol_ss` and `gr_occ_ss` are mutually dependent (`gr_occ_ss`
depends on `cortisol_ss` via `hill_activation`; `crh_ss`/`cortisol_ss`
depend on `gr_occ_ss` via `suppression`) -- likely needing a small
numerical root-find in `basal_state()`, not a closed-form constant,
while keeping `dydt()`'s `cortisol_production` on something closer to
the ORIGINAL `crh/crh_basal` ratio so a genuine CRH elevation still
translates into a genuine cortisol elevation at the new joint steady
state.

**Reverted the entire attempt** -- confirmed via `git status`/`git diff`
clean back to the `CORTISOL_P3_SENSITIVITY` commit. Shipping a fix that
silently eliminates a shipped feature's real effect would be a worse
regression than the drift it was meant to close.

`MASTER_PLAN.md` Section 8's housekeeping item updated with the full
finding, explicitly documenting why the first fix approach was wrong so
a future attempt doesn't repeat it, and recommending the coupled
nonlinear-solve approach instead. Row 1.38 (Cushing's) remains parked,
still blocked on this fix.

### DONE — Fixed the CortisolPathway CRH/Cortisol coupled fixed-point bug (Section 8 housekeeping, third attempt)

Third and successful attempt at the housekeeping item logged during row
1.38's own second Cushing's attempt. `CortisolPathway.basal_state()`
used to return `[cortisol_basal, crh_basal, gr_occ_basal]` literally --
a genuine fixed point of `dydt()` only in the trivial default case
(`stress_level=0`). Any `stress_level>0` drifted from t=0 onward,
silently, since this pathway was first built -- confirmed
`CortisolParameters(stress_level=1.0)` alone already fails
`validate_y0()`.

The SECOND attempt (previous entry) tried normalizing `dydt()`'s own
`cortisol_production` formula against a fixed reference value. That
fix closed the fixed-point gap but was WRONG in a worse way: it made
`cortisol_production` always reduce to exactly `cortisol_basal`
regardless of `stress_level`'s magnitude, silently eliminating the
feature's entire real steady-state effect (5 existing `stress_level`
tests failed, revealing they only ever passed due to the ORIGINAL
bug's own transient drift). Reverted before shipping.

**This attempt solves the genuinely COUPLED nonlinear fixed point
instead, leaving `dydt()`'s own formulas UNCHANGED.** New
`solve_cortisol_crh_steady_state(cortisol_basal, crh_basal,
stress_level)`: at the true fixed point, `dCRH=0` requires
`crh_ss/crh_basal = (1+stress_level*2)*suppression(gr_occ_ss)`, and
`dCortisol=0` (with the UNCHANGED `cortisol_production =
ke*cortisol_basal*(crh/crh_basal)`) requires `cortisol_ss/cortisol_basal`
to equal that SAME ratio -- so `crh_basal` cancels out of the equation
for `gr_occ_ss` entirely, leaving a single-variable equation:

```
gr_occ_ss = hill_activation(
    cortisol_basal * (1+stress_level*2) * suppression(gr_occ_ss),
    EC50_GR_NM, HILL_GR,
)
```

Solved via `scipy.optimize.brentq`, bracketed in `[0.0, 1.0-1e-9]`. A
shared `_crh_suppression(gr_occ)` helper is now used identically by
BOTH `dydt()` and this new solver, specifically so they can never drift
apart again -- the root cause class of the original bug.

Independently verified before shipping, not just claimed: (1) the
default case reduces to EXACTLY the pre-fix behaviour
(`gr_occ_ss==GR_REFERENCE`, `cortisol_ss==CORTISOL_BASAL_NM`,
`crh_ss==CRH_BASAL_PM`) -- zero behaviour change for any existing
non-stress scenario; (2) `stress_level=0.8` gives a genuinely elevated
`cortisol_ss` (0.28->0.484, a real ~73% increase) -- confirms this fix
does NOT repeat the second attempt's own mistake; (3) plugging the
solved `(cortisol_ss, crh_ss, gr_occ_ss)` into the UNMODIFIED `dydt()`
gives derivatives at machine-epsilon (~1e-15 to 1e-17) for
`stress_level` in [0,1]; (4) a 7-day integration confirms genuine,
lasting stability for `stress_level=0.8`; (5) the full suite ran clean
the FIRST time this attempt was tried -- unlike the second attempt,
which needed reverting after breaking 5 tests -- and all 5 previously-
broken `stress_level` tests now pass for the RIGHT reason (a genuinely
elevated steady state, not a transient drift).

Mandatory code-reviewer AND security-reviewer passes both dispatched
(Q5-gated -- a core, structural fix to already-shipped dynamics used by
both `stress_level` scenarios and glucocorticoid dosing).

**Code-reviewer**: APPROVE, 2 MEDIUM fixed. (a) `brentq`'s own bracket
precondition isn't robust to an implausibly large `cortisol_basal`
(~600k-1.8M x default) -- surfaced a cryptic raw scipy `ValueError`

negative `dose_time_min` (a glucocorticoid dose already well into its

NOT-fully-closed limitation (extending the solver to also account for

**Security-reviewer**: no CRITICAL/HIGH, 3 MEDIUM, 2 fixed (the third

### DONE — Implemented row 1.38: Cushing's syndrome (third attempt, shipped)

Picked up the just-unblocked row 1.38 immediately on the now-fixed
CRH/Cortisol coupled foundation. A naive direct multiply
(`cortisol_basal = CORTISOL_BASAL_NM * 1.560`, the Jezkova et al. 2019
PMID:31695455 ratio) achieved only a ~1.287x steady-state ratio, not
1.560 -- confirmed by direct execution -- because the coupled solve's
own negative feedback damps roughly half the intended elevation.
Jezkova's ratio is the OBSERVED/ACHIEVED clinical level (already
reflecting real physiological feedback), so it is the achieved steady
state that must match the ratio, not the raw input parameter.

Added `solve_cortisol_basal_for_target_steady_state(target_cortisol_ss,
crh_basal, stress_level)` (`cortisol_pathway.py`): a `brentq`-based
inverse solver, verified monotonic by direct execution across a wide
sweep (input multiplier 1.0-3.0x default) before relying on a single
bracketed root-find. `CortisolParameters.for_cushings(stress_level=0.0,
**kwargs)` uses it to find the `cortisol_basal` input that achieves the
target ratio exactly. Verified: `p3_modifier=0.7784` (matches this
row's own previously-documented expectation), `gb_modifier=1.0` (Gb
honestly left unmodeled -- Cushing's defining fasting hyperglycemia is
NOT represented by this preset, disclosed rather than silently
implied), `validate_y0(tolerance=1e-8)==[]` (genuine fixed point), 7-day
trajectory stable, composable with `stress_level`. Wired end-to-end:
`ScenarioDefinition.cushings_syndrome`, `_detect_cortisol()` in
runner.py (composes into the SAME shared `CortisolPathway` instance as
stress/steroid, one HPA axis not independent instances -- identical
reasoning to the already-shipped stress+steroid composition),
`schemas.py`/`service.py` REST plumbing.

**Code-reviewer pass: WARNING, 1 HIGH fixed.** The inverse solver's
auto-widening bracket only widened `hi` upward
(`while f(hi) < 0.0: hi *= 2.0`), never `lo` downward. At `stress_level`
roughly >=0.9 (fully REST-legal -- both `ScenarioDefinition` and the
REST schema cap `stress_level` at 1.0), `stress_level` independently
elevates the achieved steady state enough that `f(lo)` is already
positive too (same sign as `f(hi)`), so the terminal `brentq(f, lo, hi)`
raised a raw, unwrapped scipy `ValueError: f(a) and f(b) must have
different signs` for a fully valid clinical combination -- a Cushing's
patient under severe acute stress. Confirmed by direct execution before
fixing (`stress_level=0.90`/`0.95` crashed; `0.85` did not), both via
direct `CortisolParameters.for_cushings()` calls and end-to-end through
`SimulationRunner`. Fixed by widening `lo` downward symmetrically
(halving with a floor cap at `target_cortisol_ss * 1e-6`, raising the
same clear error if unbracketable). Added
`test_composes_with_high_stress_level_without_a_bracket_failure`

### DONE — Implemented row 1.40: Cold acclimation (this platform's first p3-INCREASING axis)

Picked up the next unblocked Track 1 chunk. Row 1.40 was parked on
"needs regime scoping" -- the concern being this is the platform's

arm), 10 days of cold acclimation (14-15C). Confirmed verbatim: "10 d
of cold acclimation... increased peripheral insulin sensitivity by
~43%" -- p3 factor 1.43. A genuinely DIFFERENT regime from the same
research group, also re-verified live, was deliberately NOT modeled:
**Sellers et al. 2021, PMID:33090911** -- n=15 healthy men, a single
~1h ACUTE shivering-cold bout, found the OPPOSITE direction ("did not
subsequently increase glucose tolerance... insulin resistance post
shivering"). Scoped explicitly to Hanssen's chronic-acclimation regime
only, the same discipline row 1.32 used for its own resting-cyclical
scope decision -- no attempt to represent acute cold/shivering exposure
or generalize to "ambient temperature" broadly.

`COLD_ACCLIMATION_P3_FACTOR = 1.43` and `cold_acclimation_modifiers()`
in `modifiers.py`, wired into `PhysiologicalPersonalizer.personalize()`'s
existing composition pipeline exactly like every other boolean/Optional
profile axis (sleep_hours, desaturation_events_per_hour,
menstrual_cycle_phase). Resolved the "regime scoping" blocker with
disclosure, not a bigger new framework: since Hanssen's cohort has no
healthy-subject arm, applying the factor to a non-T2D profile is an
unverified extrapolation -- disclosed via a new `SimulationOutput

Cushing's/GLP-1/for_gi() disclosure convention. Wired end-to-end

### DONE — Built a reusable, full-text-capable citation re-verification tool (MASTER_PLAN 10, item L1)

Prompted directly by the atorvastatin-through-OSA Track 5 curation
streak's own next candidate (Cushing's syndrome, `cortisol_pathway.py`'s
`CUSHINGS_CORTISOL_RATIO = 822.0/527.0`, PMID:31695455): the code's own
comment claims this ratio comes from the paper's Table 1, but a live
`PubMedFetcher.fetch_by_pubmed_id()` call returns an abstract entirely
about mitochondrial/OXPHOS gene expression -- no mention of cortisol at
all. Rather than accept this as an unverifiable/possibly-wrong citation,
The project owner asked for the verification tooling itself to be fixed first.

**Root cause**: `PubMedFetcher` already had a `fetch_full_text=True`
constructor flag and a working Europe PMC full-text integration
(`_fetch_europe_pmc_full_text()`), but every ad-hoc verification script
this project had written across many prior sessions called
`fetch_by_pubmed_id()` with the DEFAULT constructor (`fetch_full_text=
False`), so full text was never actually attempted -- the gap was in
the verification WORKFLOW, not a missing capability in the tool.
Confirmed directly: `PubMedFetcher(fetch_full_text=True)
.fetch_by_pubmed_id('31695455').full_text` returns 34,868 characters
including the exact line "Plasma cortisol at 08:00 hrs (nmol/L)
527±51 822±80* 286±71" -- Table 1, controls vs. active Cushing's,
exactly matching the code's own claimed ratio.

**Built `packages/literature-pipeline/src/biosim_literature/
verification.py`**: `verify_citation(pubmed_id, claims, fetcher=None)`
-- always attempts full text by default, checks each claimed substring
against the abstract first, falls back to full text only if not found
there and full text is available, and reports `full_text_available`
as a field independent of the per-claim result -- so "claim genuinely
absent" and "full text wasn't available to check" are never conflated
into one ambiguous "not found." Includes `CitationVerification.as_text()`
for a human-readable report and a CLI entry point
(`python -m biosim_literature.verification <pmid> <claim> [<claim> ...]`)
so future re-verification is one command instead of a fresh
`python -c "..."` script every time.

**Real bug caught and fixed during development, not just at review**:
the CLI crashed with `UnicodeEncodeError` printing a real author name
("Ježková") on a Windows console defaulting to cp1252 -- fixed by
reconfiguring stdout to utf-8 with `errors="replace"` before printing.

Exported `verify_citation`/`CitationVerification`/`ClaimCheck` from
`biosim_literature`'s public `__init__.py`.

Added `packages/literature-pipeline/tests/test_verification.py` (10
tests, all via `MockFetcher` -- no live network calls, matching
`test_fetcher.py`'s own established convention): abstract-only match,
full-text fallback (using the real Cushing's numbers as the test
fixture), abstract-checked-before-full-text ordering, the not-found-
vs-unavailable distinction, metadata pass-through, the `as_text()`
report format, and (added after the code-reviewer's own MEDIUM finding
below) `FetchError` propagation.

RED-proofed via the established "brand-new module" convention (`git
stash` doesn't touch untracked new files): stashed the tracked
`__init__.py` change and temporarily renamed `verification.py` aside,
confirmed the test file fails cleanly with `ModuleNotFoundError`, then
restored both.

**Mandatory code-reviewer pass: 1 MEDIUM, 1 LOW, both fixed.**
- MEDIUM: the module's own documented guarantee -- "raises whatever
  the underlying fetcher raises... an unfetchable citation must fail
  loudly" -- had zero test coverage; `MockFetcher` never raises
  `FetchError`, so a future refactor that silently swallowed the fetch
  exception would have passed every existing test. Fixed: added a
  `_FailingFetcher` stub (a minimal `Fetcher` subclass that always
  raises) and `test_fetch_error_propagates_not_swallowed`.
- LOW: `full_text_norm = ... if metadata.full_text else None` (truthy
  check) vs. `full_text_available = metadata.full_text is not None`
  (identity check) on the same field -- inconsistent, and would
  silently misreport `full_text_available=True` for a hypothetical
  empty-string `full_text` (not currently reachable via any real code
  path, since `PubMedFetcher` returns `None` not `""`, but worth
  closing the gap rather than depending on an implicit caller
  contract). Fixed by aligning both checks to `is not None`.

Full suite: 2593 -> 2603 passed, 2 skipped. Zero regressions. This
tool has no import path into `biosim_ode`/`biosim_physiology`/
`biosim_api` -- cannot affect simulated biological outputs -- so no
security-reviewer pass was owed.

`MASTER_PLAN.md` Section 10's "Small chunks" table updated with item
L1. This directly unblocks re-attempting the Cushing's syndrome
Track 5 curation chunk next, using the newly-confirmed-correct
citation.

### DONE -- Fixed a fail-open where a degenerate body size silently dropped the whole physiological profile

Follow-up from the NAFLD security review's pre-existing finding M4 (loop iteration,
2026-10-19). Reproduced first through the real REST route: `height_cm=1e-300` with
`disease_states=["type_2_diabetes"]` returned HTTP 200, peak glucose 10.38 mM
(healthy-like), and only the warning "Physiological personalisation failed:
division by zero. Using base parameters." -- a requested disease state simulated as
healthy. Cause: the schema allowed any `gt=0`; `profile.bmi`'s denominator underflowed
to 0 inside `personalize()`; the runner's catch-all swallowed it and dropped the
WHOLE profile. NaN/inf weight/height also passed the old `<= 0` checks.

Fix at the right layer: `PhysiologicalProfile.__post_init__` now requires finite,
positive weight and height and a derived BMI within `MIN_PLAUSIBLE_BMI`..`MAX_PLAUSIBLE_BMI`
(5..250 -- explicitly a generous plausibility guard, NOT a cited physiological range; a
first draft's "documented extremes ~7 to 200" was unsourced and reworded). Underflow
(ZeroDivisionError) and overflow (OverflowError, found by the code review) both become
ValueError, which REST already maps to 400. The catch-all itself is deliberately unchanged.
+20 tests (parametrised rejection incl. 1e-300/1e-100/1e300/NaN/inf/absurd BMIs, exact
inclusive boundaries, constants-not-dataclass-fields, real-size accept cases down to a
3.5kg/50cm newborn, and REST `== 400` naming `height_cm`). RED first (9 failures), the
overflow case RED separately after review. Code review: APPROVE, no CRITICAL/HIGH.

Verified safe for existing callers: every in-repo construction uses 70kg/170cm or the
population sampler (BMI clipped to its own spec bounds at fixed height -- I read the
sampler; the reviewer additionally reports a 200,000-point BMI sweep across 5..250 with
zero rejections, which I did not re-run).

Still open: runner catch-all has no server-side logging / `personalization_applied`
flag; `PopulationSpec.bmi_min/bmi_max` unvalidated (would now fail mid-cohort for absurd

### DONE — Closed the 2026-10-19 safety follow-ups (Track 1 rows 1.44/1.45)

Four follow-ups logged by the HCQ/NAFLD reviews, each RED-proofed before the fix.

1. **Duplicate dose-scaled drug events rejected.** New `DOSE_SCALED_SINGLE_EVENT_DRUGS`
   in `validate_drug_combination()` (enforced at `ScenarioDefinition` -> REST 400). Two
   classes: static factors that compound per event (metformin, pioglitazone, indinavir,
   HCTZ, atorvastatin -- 2 x pioglitazone 15mg != 30mg), and first-event-only drugs whose
   later events were silently dropped (acarbose, miglitol, semaglutide, liraglutide --
   found by the security review and reproduced directly: acarbose 25+100mg peaked at
   9.74 mM, 100+25mg at 7.67 mM). Excluded after checking: sulfonylureas, DPP-4i,
   tirzepatide, SGLT2i (dose-independent here, so duplicates are inert) and time-resolved
   insulin/caffeine/alcohol/glucocorticoid. Design choice (the project owner, 2026-10-20): reject
   rather than sum doses; the error asks for one event with the total dose.
2. **Profile catch-all removed** (`runner.py`). Any personalisation failure used to
   become a warning plus a healthy-baseline simulation (HTTP 200). Now `ValueError` ->
   REST 400 and anything else propagates; `/population` and `/batch` already catch per
   item. The security review fuzzed 97 random scenarios: no non-ValueError raised.
3. **Point-of-use clamps disclosed.** `EFFECTIVE_PARAM_BOUNDS` + `raw_effective_params()`
   (shared with `dydt()` so the two cannot drift), `point_of_use_clamp_hits()`,
   `CompositePathway.injected_signals()` (extracted from `dydt()`, behaviour-preserving),
   and `SimulationResult.clamp_hits` keyed by `(field, side)` from a post-solve sweep of
   the output points; `SimulationRunner` turns each hit into a warning. NaN counts as a
   floor hit (`clamp()` maps NaN to the floor). `dydt()` cost unchanged (15.6 vs 15.8 ms);
   the sweep adds ~24% to a composite run, so `simulate(check_clamps=False)` is used by the
   UQ/OAT/Sobol ensembles, which discarded the result anyway.
4. **Cohort-mismatch warnings** for hydroxychloroquine (diabetic or BMI < 25 profile vs.
   Wasko 2015's non-diabetic overweight/obese cohort; fires for drug-only requests too,
   since the default profile's BMI is 24.2) and NAFLD (diabetic profile vs. Bugianesi's
   non-diabetic cohort; likely double-counting with INSULIN_RESISTANT/T2D/NEFA dynamics).

Reviews: code-reviewer APPROVE -- MEDIUM fixed (one field hitting floor AND ceiling
reported only the first side; now keyed by side), LOWs fixed (ensemble sweep cost, comment
wrap, ceiling-side warning test). Security-reviewer PASS -- MEDIUM-1 fixed (item 1's
first-event-only drugs); MEDIUM-2 disclosed, not fixed: the sweep samples output points
only (a sub-interval excursion can be missed) and UQ ensemble members never report clamp
hits. LOW: nested composites are skipped by the sweep (unsupported anyway).

Still open: a real end-to-end scenario that reaches a point-of-use clamp is tested only at
the engine level (the runner test patches the hit); UQ-member clamp disclosure.

Two OAT/Monte Carlo test doubles that replace `ODESystem.simulate` gained the new
`check_clamps` keyword. Tests: 2697 -> 2732 passed, 2 skipped; all 6 registered clinical
benchmarks PASS.

## Archived from CLAUDE.md (2026-10-20)

Moved verbatim from `CLAUDE.md` during the Phase 2 docs pass so `CLAUDE.md` can be
read in one pass; `CLAUDE.md` keeps a condensed summary of each section below.

#### Session close note (2026-07-28) -- read this before picking Track 1's first milestone

The three custom agents above were confirmed live and selectable by the
harness partway through the same session that authored them (a fresh
system notification listed all three as available) -- they do not need
re-authoring, just use them via the `Agent` tool by name.

**A Track 1 candidate was scoped and its headline citations personally
verified -- ready to implement, not yet started.** A `general-purpose`
background agent (the custom agents weren't registered yet at that
point) scoped adding a real ODE-coupled SGLT2-inhibitor pathway
(dapagliflozin/empagliflozin/canagliflozin -- a major T2D drug class
this platform doesn't model at all, mechanistically distinct from
GLP-1/metformin/steroids since it causes genuine glucosuria rather than
altering insulin dynamics). Its report was NOT trusted at face value --
both headline PMIDs were independently re-fetched and cross-checked
against raw NCBI XML before writing anything here, per this project's
evidence-hierarchy rule.

- **Verified correct**: PMID:28428225 (Al-Jobori H et al., *Diabetes*
  2017, "Empagliflozin and Kinetics of Renal Glucose Transport in
  Healthy Individuals and Individuals With Type 2 Diabetes") -- stepped
  hyperglycemic clamp, n=15 T2D + n=15 healthy. Baseline maximal renal
  glucose transport (TmG) 459+/-53 (T2D) vs. 337+/-25 mg/min (healthy),
  P<0.05. Empagliflozin reduced TmG 44+/-7%/53+/-6% at 48h, 65+/-5%/
  75+/-3% at day 14 (both groups respectively); lowered the urinary
  glucose-spillage threshold to <40 mg/dL in both groups -- well below
  normal fasting glucose. PMCID:PMC7301160 (full text may be available
  via the Europe PMC fetcher for deeper methodology if needed later).
- **Verified correct**: PMID:23412078 (Polidori D et al., *Diabetes
  Care* 2013, "Canagliflozin lowers postprandial glucose and insulin by
  delaying intestinal glucose absorption in addition to increasing
  urinary glucose excretion") -- n=20 healthy, crossover, canagliflozin
  300mg vs. placebo 20min before a 600-kcal mixed meal. Glucose AUC(0-2h)
  -35%, insulin AUC(0-2h) -43% (both P<0.001), UGE(0-6h) 18.2+/-5.6 vs.
  <0.2g (P<0.001) -- exact match to the agent's report, confirmed via
  the complete raw abstract, not just the truncated version
  `PubMedFetcher` itself returned (see the bug noted directly below).
  **Same-meal drug-vs-placebo shape, directly reusable for a
  `validate_sglt2i()` benchmark** exactly like `validate_semaglutide()`/
  `validate_metformin()`. Real caveat, confirmed in the abstract's own
  text: canagliflozin at this dose measurably delays intestinal glucose
  absorption via SGLT1 co-inhibition (not purely a renal/SGLT2 effect)
  -- "canagliflozin reduces postprandial plasma glucose and insulin by
  increasing UGE (via renal SGLT2 inhibition) and delaying RaO, likely
  due to intestinal SGLT1 inhibition" -- so this specific benchmark's
  35%/43% magnitude is NOT purely attributable to the renal mechanism a
  Biosim pathway would implement; a more SGLT2-selective drug
  (dapagliflozin/empagliflozin) would show a smaller effect from renal
  clearance alone. Flag this explicitly in the benchmark's docstring if
  built, same as the semaglutide/hepatic-extraction entries do for
  their own confounds.
- **Mechanistic design**: does NOT fit `extra_g_clearance_modifier`
  (that's a constant first-order rate proportional to (G-Gb), active at
  any above-basal glucose -- wrong shape for a threshold-gated,
  Michaelis-Menten-saturating renal transport mechanism). Needs a
  **new** rule-11 signal, e.g. `renal_glucose_clearance_delta`
  (additive to dG, mM/min, default 0.0 -- same pattern as
  `hepatic_egp_delta`). Open design question the agent correctly
  flagged and did not resolve: SGLT2i likely needs a two-part
  representation like metformin (a static fasting-glucose-lowering
  modifier for the threshold shift + a dynamic ODE-coupled postprandial
  clearance pathway), not one mechanism alone -- worth deciding
  deliberately before implementing, not defaulting to whichever is
  easier to code.
- **Not verified, flagged as needing a citation or an explicit
  UNVERIFIED placeholder before use**: the normal renal glucose
  threshold (~180 mg/dL / 10 mM is commonly cited in secondary sources
  but was not independently confirmed against a primary source this
  pass) and dapagliflozin-specific TmG/threshold values (only
  empagliflozin's kinetics were checked). Do not hardcode either without
  a direct citation, per this project's standing rule.
- Zero double-counting risk confirmed: grepped `physiology/
  drug_interactions.py` and `physiology/modifiers.py` directly -- no
  existing reference to renal/glucosuria/SGLT/urinary glucose anywhere.

**A real, separate finding surfaced while re-verifying the above, not
yet fixed**: `PubMedFetcher._parse_pubmed_xml()`
(`packages/literature-pipeline/src/biosim_literature/fetcher.py:238-241`)
builds `abstract` from `(el.text or "")` per `<AbstractText>` element.
In `ElementTree`, `.text` returns only the text immediately after the
opening tag, up to the *first* child element -- an abstract containing
inline markup (`<sub>`, `<i>`, common for subscripted units like
`Tm<sub>G</sub>` or italicized statistical terms like `<i>P</i>`)
gets silently truncated right at that tag. Confirmed directly:
PMID:28428225's real abstract is 1400+ characters (verified via raw
NCBI XML and plain-text `efetch`); `PubMedFetcher.fetch_by_pubmed_id
('28428225').abstract` returns only 309 characters, cutting off
mid-sentence at "...maximal renal glucose transport (Tm" -- exactly
where the first `<sub>` tag appears. Title/author/journal/year fields
were spot-checked and matched correctly for this PMID, so this is
specifically an abstract-parsing gap, not a wholesale fetch failure --
but it means **any citation-verification pass on a paper with inline
XML markup in its abstract may be silently working from a truncated,
possibly misleading fragment** without any error or warning. This is
exactly the kind of tool defect the `literature-curator` agent depends
on being correct -- worth fixing before leaning on it heavily for Track
1's literature verification. Likely fix: replace `el.text` with
`"".join(el.itertext())` per `AbstractText` element (recursively
concatenates all text including nested elements' content) -- not yet
implemented, verified, or tested this session; needs the full TDD
fix discipline (regression test with a real inline-markup fixture,
RED-proof via `git stash`, full suite) before being called done.
**RESOLVED** -- see "### DONE -- Fixed the PubMedFetcher abstract-truncation
bug" below.

### KNOWN BUGS THAT WERE FIXED — DO NOT REINTRODUCE

1. **Root file shadowing:** Never leave types.py, queue.py, __init__.py,
   or any package module in <repo root>\ root. They shadow stdlib.

2. **kinetics.py argument order:** michaelis_menten takes (substrate, vmax, km)
   not (substrate, km, vmax). Tests at line 96 in test_ode_engine.py verify this.

3. **NEFA antilipolysis:** Uses hill_activation (insulin → suppresses lipolysis)
   not hill_inhibition. At zero insulin, NEFA should RISE not stay flat.

4. **Cortisol GR reference:** Fixed at 0.15, not instance.gr_occ_basal.

5. **np.trapz → np.trapezoid:** In sensitivity.py and runner.py.

6. **Delta secretion:** dI formulation must use (current_frac - basal_frac)
   not absolute secretion rate.

7. **CompositePathway coupling was architecturally inert:**
   `GlucoseInsulinPathway.dydt()` accepted a `signals` dict but never read
   from it, so composing cortisol/hepatic/NEFA/GLP1 with GI via
   `CompositePathway` integrated successfully but had **zero effect** on
   glucose/insulin output -- every "clinical" scenario using these pathways
   was actually backed by a disconnected calculation. Fixed: `dydt()` now
   consumes `p3_modifier`, `gb_modifier`, `insulin_resistance_modifier`,
   `hepatic_egp_delta`, `incretin_effect`, `gastric_emptying_modifier`, all
   gated so the basal steady state is unaffected when absent/neutral.
   `ODESystem` was also hardcoded to `GlucoseInsulinPathway`'s fixed 6-species
   layout (species names/units, Boolean watchdog indices) and could not run
   a composite at all -- generalized to read species by name from whatever
   `BasePathway` it's given. All four extensions (cortisol, hepatic, NEFA,
   GLP1) are now wired end-to-end via `SimulationRunner._build_pathway()` --
   see PATHWAY EXTENSIONS above for activation conditions and the
   double-counting analysis behind each one's design.

8. **NEFA insulin_resistance_modifier used absolute NEFA, not excess above a
   fixed reference:** unlike cortisol's `GR_REFERENCE` pattern (item 4
   above), `NEFAPathway.output_signals()` computed the p3 modifier from the
   raw NEFA level, so composing NEFA at its own *basal* state silently cut
   insulin action by ~16.5% -- double-counting insulin resistance already
   baked into the Bergman 1981 p3 calibration cohort. Fixed with
   `NEFA_IR_REFERENCE = NEFA_BASAL_UM`; modifier is now exactly neutral (1.0)
   at basal and still correctly degrades under obesity/exercise presets
   (which have genuinely elevated NEFA above the population reference).

10. **`CortisolPathway.GR_OCC_BASAL` was not the analytic fixed point of its
    own ODE.** It was hardcoded to `0.15` -- coincidentally identical to
    `EC50_GR_NM` (also `0.15`), strongly suggesting a copy-paste error
    rather than a solved steady state. The actual fixed point of
    `dGR = GR_RELAXATION * (hill_activation(cortisol, EC50_GR_NM, HILL_GR) - GR_occ)`
    at `CORTISOL_BASAL_NM` is `~0.718`, not `0.15`. Consequence: **every**
    simulation composing `CortisolPathway` -- including the default,
    zero-stress, zero-steroid case -- silently drifted GR occupancy from
    0.15 toward 0.72 over about an hour, cutting `p3_modifier` (insulin
    action) by ~14% with nothing "abnormal" configured at all. The existing
    `test_couple_with_gi_no_stress_matches_baseline_closely` test didn't
    catch this because it only checks the glucose *peak*, which occurs
    early (~24 min for a high-sugar meal) before the remote-insulin
    compartment (X, time constant ~81 min via `p2`) has ramped up enough
    for the p3 deficit to move the peak measurably -- AUC and
    time-to-return-to-baseline would have been measurably wrong. Fixed:
    `GR_OCC_BASAL = hill_activation(CORTISOL_BASAL_NM, EC50_GR_NM, HILL_GR)`,
    computed from the module's own constants instead of a duplicated
    literal, so it cannot drift out of sync with them again; `GR_REFERENCE`
    set equal to it (same fixed-reference pattern as `NEFA_IR_REFERENCE`).
    Verified with `validate_y0()` and a standalone 60-minute integration
    confirming `p3_modifier` stays at 1.0 throughout, not just at t=0.
    **Lesson for any future pathway with a Hill-kinetics relaxation state**:
    never hardcode the "basal" value of a state that relaxes toward
    `hill_activation(...)` -- always derive it from the same formula the
    ODE uses, or `validate_y0()` won't catch a mismatch that only manifests
    as post-t=0 drift (a static y0 check at t=0 alone cannot detect this
    class of bug -- integrate forward and check, as this fix's tests now do).

### KNOWN BUGS — DISCOVERED AND FIXED THIS SESSION (follow-on to #10)

Following up on KNOWN BUGS FIXED #10, the same full-trajectory technique
(integrate standalone at default params + basal input signal, check
whether the state drifts away from y0) was run against the other single-
species extension pathways. Two more instances of the identical bug class
were found and fixed. `GLP1Pathway` was checked too and was already
correctly calibrated (its delta-formulation secretion term is exactly zero
at basal glucose) -- no fix needed there.

11. **`HepGlucPathway.EGP_BASAL_MM_MIN` (0.032) was not the fixed point of
    its own ODE at basal insulin.** Standalone integration with
    `signals={"insulin_pM": 66.0}` drifted EGP from `0.032` to `~0.0446`
    within ~600 minutes -- `EGP_SUPPRESSION_IC50` was hardcoded to `80.0`
    with no relation to `EGP_BASAL_MM_MIN`/`EGP_MAX_MM_MIN`. Fixed by
    treating `EGP_BASAL_MM_MIN` and `EGP_MAX_MM_MIN` as the trustworthy
    literature anchors (measured fasting EGP vs. documented fasted/
    stressed maximum) and deriving `EGP_SUPPRESSION_IC50` analytically
    from them via `_solve_egp_suppression_ic50()` in `hepatic.py`:
    `hill_inhibition(x, ic50, n) = f  =>  ic50 = x * (f/(1-f))**(1/n)`
    where `f = egp_basal / egp_max` and `x` = the reference basal insulin
    (`EGP_REFERENCE_INSULIN_PM = 66.0`, matching `PathwayParameters.Ib`).
    Computed value: `ic50 ≈ 47.08` (down from the hardcoded `80.0`),
    which is independently physiologically plausible -- hepatic insulin
    sensitivity for EGP suppression is well documented to be *more*
    sensitive than peripheral glucose uptake (whose IC50 the old `80.0`
    resembled). Scope note (RESOLVED -- see #14 and the
    `for_metformin()` closing note right after it; both were open
    questions only at the time this paragraph was originally written,
    not anymore): this fix targets only the **default** `EGPParameters()`
    construction. `for_type2_diabetes()`'s `ic50_pM = EGP_SUPPRESSION_IC50
    * 2.5` and `for_metformin()`'s `metformin_scale` were deliberately
    left untouched here -- their own fixed-point exactness was not yet
    verified at this point in the session and might have the same drift
    bug independently (the T2D preset's higher IC50 represents a real,
    intentional hepatic-insulin-resistance mechanism, so re-deriving it
    purely to satisfy the fixed-point equation would silently overwrite
    that mechanism -- needed its own dedicated investigation, not a
    drive-by fix). **Both were in fact investigated later this same
    session**: T2D was fixed with a real citation (item #14 below), and
    `for_metformin()` was confirmed intentionally non-fixed-point (correct
    drug-onset behaviour, not a bug -- see the closing note directly
    after item #14). Verified with `validate_y0(tolerance=1e-8)` plus a
    600-minute standalone integration
    (`test_hepatic.py::test_egp_stable_over_long_trajectory_at_basal_insulin`).

12. **`NEFAPathway.NEFA_BASAL_UM` (350) was not the fixed point of its own
    ODE at basal insulin -- and unlike the hepatic case above, this was a
    structural bug, not just a wrong constant.** The un-normalized
    `nefa_target = nefa_max - (nefa_max - nefa_basal) * antilipolysis` is
    algebraically a convex combination `A*nefa_basal + (1-A)*nefa_max`
    (`A = hill_activation(insulin, ic50, n) ∈ [0,1)`), which can equal
    `nefa_basal` only if `nefa_max == nefa_basal` (no dynamic range left)
    or in the unreachable limit `A -> 1` (insulin -> infinity) -- **no
    finite `insulin_ic50` could ever make `nefa_basal` an exact fixed
    point**, so this could not be fixed by re-deriving a constant the way
    hepatic's `ic50_pM` was. Fixed by normalizing `antilipolysis` against
    its own value at the reference basal insulin
    (`NEFA_REFERENCE_INSULIN_PM = 66.0`) before applying it:
    `suppression_ratio = antilipolysis(insulin) / antilipolysis(66.0)`,
    then `nefa_target = max(0, nefa_max - (nefa_max - nefa_basal) *
    suppression_ratio)`. This forces `nefa_target(66.0) == nefa_basal`
    exactly *by construction*, for any `insulin_ic50`/`hill_n`/`nefa_max`
    -- which also means it automatically fixes every preset
    simultaneously (default, `for_obesity()`, `for_exercise()`), not just
    the default. `output_signals()`'s `NEFA_IR_REFERENCE`-based
    `insulin_resistance_modifier` calculation was untouched (already
    correct, uses a fixed module-level reference regardless of preset).
    Verified with `validate_y0(tolerance=1e-8)` on all three presets plus
    a 600-minute standalone integration for each
    (`test_pathway_extensions.py::test_nefa_stable_over_long_trajectory_at_basal_insulin`).

**Lesson reinforced**: before "fixing" a fixed-point bug by re-deriving a
constant, check whether the formula's *algebraic structure* even permits
an exact fixed point at all for finite parameter values (NEFA's convex-
combination form did not) -- if it doesn't, the fix is a normalization/
restructuring, not a constant swap, and the search for which parameter is
"the anchor" (as done for cortisol and hepatic) doesn't apply.

Test count: 1101 passing (was 1097 -- +4 new regression tests, 2 pathways
× 2 tests each: `validate_y0` fixed-point check + long-trajectory
integration check).

14. **`EGPParameters.for_type2_diabetes()` was over-determined: three
    independent "impairment" multipliers stacked on top of each other
    (`egp_basal*1.30`, `ic50_pM*2.5`, `t2d_egp_scale*1.40`), making the
    preset's own `y0` NOT the fixed point of its own ODE (flagged as a
    "distinct, not-yet-investigated question" in item #11 above) --
    and this was structural over-determination, not just a wrong
    constant: with three independently-chosen "worse" multipliers, no
    single one of them could be re-derived to satisfy the fixed-point
    equation without contradicting the direction the other two were
    deliberately set to represent.** Resolved with real literature,
    not algebra alone: **Beck-Nielsen H, Hother-Nielsen O, Staehr P.
    "Is hepatic glucose production increased in type 2 diabetes
    mellitus?" Curr Diab Rep. 2002. PMID:12643178** (verified live via
    `PubMedFetcher`) reports fasting HGP "may be increased by a mean of
    12%" (not 30%) and, critically, "suppression of HGP by insulin shows
    a rightward shift of the dose response curve (reduced insulin
    sensitivity) but **normal maximal suppression (no maximum velocity
    defect)**." That last clause directly falsifies `t2d_egp_scale`
    as an independent mechanism -- there is no real "maximum velocity
    defect" to represent, so it should stay at its default `1.0`, not
    `1.40`. Fixed: `egp_basal = EGP_BASAL_MM_MIN * 1.12` (anchored to the
    measured 12% figure) and `ic50_pM` now **derived** via
    `_solve_egp_suppression_ic50()` (same technique as item #11) from
    that anchored `egp_basal`, `egp_max` (unchanged -- "no maximum
    velocity defect"), and `hill_n` -- `t2d_egp_scale` left at its
    default `1.0`. This makes the T2D preset's `y0` an exact fixed point
    too, resolving item #11's open question with a real citation instead
    of guesswork. **One test needed correcting, not just re-passing**:
    `test_t2d_hepatic_coupling_impairs_postmeal_suppression` asserted
    `auc_t2d > auc_healthy` (an assumption baked in from the old,
    literature-contradicted 3-multiplier version) -- but PMID:12643178
    also states "suppression of HGP during a meal is close to normal" in
    T2D, so a big postprandial AUC gap via *this specific EGP-coupling
    mechanism* was never actually the correct expectation. Renamed to
    `test_t2d_hepatic_coupling_postmeal_suppression_close_to_normal` and
    changed to `auc_t2d == pytest.approx(auc_healthy, rel=0.01)` -- T2D's
    genuinely elevated fasting/postprandial glucose comes from the
    static `Gb`/disease-state modifiers in `physiology/modifiers.py`
    (tested separately), not from this coupling's own kinetics, which the
    literature says stays close to normal. +4 tests (`t2d_no_maximum_
    velocity_defect`, `t2d_basal_matches_literature_12_percent_elevation`,
    `t2d_y0_is_genuine_fixed_point`, plus the corrected AUC test), 1122 ->
    1125.

    **`for_metformin()`'s own fixed-point exactness (the other half of
    this item's original scope) was also checked, same session.** It is
    NOT a fixed point (`validate_y0()` returns a violation) -- but
    confirmed this is correct, intentional behaviour, not a third
    instance of this bug class: `for_metformin()` keeps `y0` at the
    healthy pre-treatment `egp_basal` (0.032) while `metformin_scale<1.0`

    `test_metformin_hepatic_coupling_lowers_glucose_peak` exists to
    demonstrate. Documented with a permanent regression test
    (`test_metformin_y0_intentionally_not_a_fixed_point`, asserts drift
